articleTitle: Transformer based Radio Map Prediction Model for Dense Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Radio map prediction (RMP) is one of the key technologies to improve spectrum efficiency. In this paper, a novel deep learning model termed as RadioTrans is proposed for RMP task. Specifically, Transformer modules are used to capture the long-range spatial relationship in radio wave propagation. Furthermore, a Grid Anchor technique is proposed to better represent the relative position of the radiation source, destination and environment. The effectiveness of proposed method is verified on an urban radio wave propagation dataset. Compared with state-of-the-art deep learning RMP model, RadioTrans improve the prediction accuracy by 27.3%. Compared with the well-known ray-tracing based method, the prediction speed is increased by 4 orders of magnitude. Code is released at git@github.com:OXSLAB/RadioTrans_Official.git.

articleTitle: Research Progress in Millimeter Wave Radar-Based non-contact Sleep Monitoring - A Review
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Compared with traditional contact medical devices, non-contact sleep monitoring based on millimeter wave radar has the advantages of non-contact, simple operation, and long-term monitoring of human respiration rate (RR) and heart rate (HR), which has broad research value and market prospects. In this paper, we review the recent developments, current challenges and future directions in the field of non-contact sleep monitoring based on millimeter wave radar. We first summarize some representative research works published in recent years to discuss vital sign monitoring, sleep posture estimation, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) detection. It is illustrated that vital signs such as RR and HR can be used as indicators for diagnosing many diseases, helping to diagnose sleep disorders and providing information on the classification of different sleep stages. Sleep posture estimation can be used as a diagnostic indicator for many chronic diseases and may help in pharmacological treatment. OSA monitoring is one of the most valuable research and application prospects in sleep monitoring. Finally, the challenges now facing measurement accuracy and stability, multi-user monitoring, and processing device computational performance are discussed, and future research directions in the field of sleep monitoring are proposed.

articleTitle: In-cabin Monitoring Based on Millimeter Wave FMCW radar
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Accidents caused by people left inside vehicles are drawing attention year by year, so the detection of people inside vehicles is particularly important. Millimeter wave FMCW radar has more advantages than other non-contact devices as well as more adaptability to the working environment while being inexpensive. In this paper, a 60 GHz millimeter wave radar system is built and utilized for in-cabin target detection. An improved Euclidean clustering as well as a state machine approach is used for adaptive monitoring of the different presence of targets, and the effectiveness of the approach is confirmed experimentally.

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement for Vivaldi Antennas with Metasurface Wall
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work a metasurface wall constructed of square split ring (SSR) unit cells is proposed, to reduce the coupling between two Vivaldi antennas at X band. Effective medium theory is utilized to demonstrate the negative permittivity or permeability of the proposed metasurface, which can exhibit the stop band performance. Compared with the initial reference antennas, with a linear distance of 30mm, the isolation value between two antennas with metasurface wall can be improved more than 16 dB at 10 GHz. In addition, simulated results have also demonstrated that the radiation patterns, the peak gains and total efficiencies of decoupled antennas are enhanced by loading the proposed metasurface structure.

articleTitle: Automatic Classification and Recognition Method based on Partially-Connected Differentiable Architecture Search for ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Automatic classification and recognition (ACR) is considered one of promising techniques in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Existing ACR method uses Wigner-Ville Distribution (WVD) time frequency analysis (TFA) of modulation signal to obtain its WVD images which can be recognized by convolution neural network (CNN). In this paper, we proposed an improved ACR method using partially-connected differentiable architecture search (PC-DARTS). The search space is relaxed to a continuous space, and then the performance of the validation set of the architecture is optimized by gradient descent, so as to find the optimal CNN structure for signal classification and recognition. Experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve better performance with lower complexity than the other deep learning-based methods.

articleTitle: Channel Prediction for Millimeter-Wave V2V Communication Using Autoregressive Models
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communications using millimeter-wave (mmWave) technologies can offer gigabit-per-second date rates, thus attracting large research interest. One of the challenges, however, is the potentially severe channel aging effect due to high mobility of both the transmitter (TX) and the receiver (RX). This effect may lead to an unaffordable channel estimation overhead and a degradation of system performance. In order to combat channel aging, we propose channel prediction, i.e., future channel state is predicted based on the estimated but outdated channel state information (CSI). In the paper, classical and low-complexity autoregressive (AR) models are used to predict CSI. We evaluate the prediction scheme based on measured mmWave V2V channels at 41 GHz, where TX-RX relative velocities were as high as 120–180 km/h. Simulation results show that the predicted CSI is much more accurate than the aged one, with normalized prediction errors around -13 to -30 dB. Specifically, channel components or delay taps with strong energy are relatively easy to predict, while for weak components caused by e.g., scattering or diffused reflection, it is very difficult to obtain a low prediction error. The research indicates that channel prediction using AR models can effectively overcome the channel aging problem in mmWave V2V communications. Hence, the proposed scheme has a potential of being used in practical systems to ensure high-mobility system performance.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning in FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach based on deep learning (DL) is proposed to predict electromagnetic transmission problem in two-dimensional free space. The Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method is employed to establish training data sets for the proposed model based on U-net. We demonstrate the performance of the proposed approach using experimental tests. It is found that the newly proposed approach could predict the electromagnetic field with satisfactory accuracy.

articleTitle: The Progress Review and Future Preview of Typical Ionospheric Models
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Focusing on the typical ionospheric model, we overview the recent advance's development history and provide a preview of the future. Specifically, we first present a historical review to show the technological evolution of IRI, ITU-R reference ionosphere model, simplified ionospheric regional model, Asia-Oceania method, Asia Regional model, and other models. And then, we highlight the three features of the future ionospheric modeling: (1) more intelligence, (2) high accuracy on regional methods, and (3) a combination of long-term prediction and short-term forecast methods. We hope that this paper will stimulate more interest in ionospheric modeling and related application.

articleTitle: A 4-Element MIMO Antenna with Grounded Neutralization Line for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A four-element multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna with grounded neutralization line for 5G smartphone application is proposed. The MIMO antenna is composed of two pairs of L-shaped monopoles, each pair of which is mirror-symmetrical about the ground for miniaturization. Meanwhile, the size of two L-shaped monopoles is only 10.5×7 mm (0.119 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>× 0.082 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at 3.5 GHz). Good isolation is achieved by loading the grounded neutralization line between two L-shaped monopoles. Compared with the MIMO antenna without neutralization line, the isolation of the proposed MIMO antenna is improved by 10.5 dB (from 8 to 18.5 dB) at 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of dual band millimeter wave beam shaped array antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the requirement of dual-channel dual-band millimeter wave for high-frequency radio fuze determination, a miniaturized dual-band microstrip beam-shaped array antenna which consists of six patch radiation units and microstrip feed network is designed. Independent adjustment of the two working frequency bands can be achieved by adjusting the size of the patch and the length of the slot.

articleTitle: Characteristics Analysis on NB-IoT Channels in Rural Scenario for Smart Grid Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Future smart meter reading system will consider the combination of wire and wireless transmissions. The Narrowband Internet of Things (NB-IoT), as a promising low power wide area network (LPWAN) wireless transmission technology, has attracted more attentions in smart grid field. In this paper, the channel characteristics of NB-IoT in typical rural scenario are investigated. By reconstructing the rural scenario using the ray tracing method, the multipath signal propagations between the transmitters (Txs) in different positions and receivers (Rxs) can be tracked. Based on ray tracing simulations, the key channel characteristics, such as power delay profile (PDP), channel capacity, root mean-square (RMS), delay spread (DS) and angular spread (AS) are presented and analyzed. The simulation results can provide a significant reference for the future deployments of Tx and Rx, which are crucial for the better application of NB-IoT technology in smart meter reading system.

articleTitle: Pattern Correction of Impaired Antenna Array Based on Mixed Integer Programming
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The impairment of active antenna arrays will lead to the deterioration of their radiation patterns. In this paper, a method based on mixed integer programming (MIP) is proposed to correct patterns of impaired linear antenna arrays. The proposed method uses a fast branch and bound (B&B) process to achieve the low sidelobe pattern correction while the minimization of the number of corrected elements is maintained. Compared with the existing pattern correction techniques, the proposed method exhibits the more superior performance in terms of pattern consistency and number of corrected elements.

articleTitle: A 3-D Printed Ka-Band Waveguide Bandpass Filter With Quasi-Elliptic Response
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A Ka-band quasi-elliptic bandpass filter (BPF) based on stereolithography apparatus (SLA) 3-D printing technique is proposed. The filter consists of four coupled resonators with three direct couplings between adjacent resonators and a cross coupling between the first and fourth resonators. Benefited from this feature, a pair of transmission zeros (TZs) can be produced in the stopband to enhance the passband selectivity significantly. Additionally, two waveguide bends are incorporated with the input and output waveguides to facilitate experimental test. For demonstration, a 3-D printed BPF prototype with center frequency of 30 GHz, bandwidth of 1.4 GHz, and return loss better than 20 dB is implemented and tested. The weight of the filter is 9.8 g only. The measured results demonstrate that the passband return loss is better than 10 dB, and the average in-band insertion loss is less than 2 dB.

articleTitle: Base Station Antenna with Low-Scattering Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A base station antenna with low-scattering dipoles is presented in the paper. The proposed low-band (LB) antenna operates in the band of 1.71-2.11 GHz (VSWR<1.5). By loading window-shaped slots on strip dipoles, it can minimize scattering and work with high-band (HB) antennas operating in the band of 3.3-3.8 GHz. A dual-band array has been designed to validate the performance of LB antenna. Both simulated and measured results have shown that the LB antenna can preserve radiation patterns of HB elements with short distance to it. Besides, it can achieve stable performance in the dual-band array.

articleTitle: Research on Interference Coupling Mechanism and Test Method of UAV in Complex Electromagnetic Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the development of integrated joint operations technology, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) plays a more and more important role in modern warfare and civil science and technology. Compared with manned aircraft, UAV has many advantages in manufacturing and maintenance costs. However, the command and control of UAV depends entirely on the remote operation of ground control station, and its dependence on electromagnetic signals makes UAV more susceptible to interference and threat from complex external electromagnetic environment, and the consequences caused by interference are more serious, which may lead to control failure and crash. In this paper, the composition and characteristics of the complex electromagnetic environment faced by UAV are combed, and the interference coupling mechanism of UAV to external electromagnetic environment is studied. Furthermore, based on the interference coupling mechanism of complex electromagnetic environment to UAV, the anti-interference test of VUAV in complex electromagnetic environment is studied and carried out, and the anti-interference ability of UAV to signals of different systems is verified.

articleTitle: A Soft Source Implementation Technique on Face-Centered Cubic Grids for FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper studies the setting approach of soft source in the FCC- FDTD method, and the electric dipole source is selected to validate the proposed method. In a FCC grid, the soft source implementation technique and the difference in calculation results caused by different electric field sampling methods will be discussed in detail. The research results can provide the basic tools for the practical application in the FCC- FDTD method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Propagation Characteristics for MIMO Air-to-Air Communications With UAV Jitter
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a three-dimension (3D) geometry-based statistical model (GBSM) is employed for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) air-to-air (A2A) communication channel. Considering the UAV flight change, we model the pitch angle variation due to UAV jitter by a sinusoidal random process. Based on proposed model, we derive the space-time correlation function. Numerical results demonstrate that the amplitude and frequency of the UAV jitter variations have a significant impact on multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel correlation.

articleTitle: Broadband Dual Circularly Polarized Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband dual-circularly polarized dipole antenna with compact size, high isolation and wide axial ratio bandwidth has been proposed. The antenna consists of two intersecting dipoles and a square reflector. The dipoles are simultaneously fed by a feed network composed of a 90° coupler to produce dual circularly polarization. The coupler is vertically integrated between the dipole and the reflector for space saving. The antenna has a wide 3-dB AR bandwidth(ARBW) of 96% (1.5-4.25 GHz) and a wide impedance bandwidth (IBW) of 100% (1.5-4.5 GHz) for return loss better than 16 dB. In addition, the antenna obtains a stable radiation pattern and high gain across the whole operational band.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a Terahertz Silicon-based Corrugated Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Corrugated horn is a kind of waveguide antenna frequently used in radio astronomy and satellite communication as a feed for its excellent performance. Due to the short wavelength, fabrication of a terahertz corrugated horn antenna becomes very difficult, which greatly limits its wide application in this frequency band. In this paper, we introduce the design of a corrugated horn antenna that works at a center frequency of 275 GHz which is fabricated using silicon platelet technology. Simulation results show that the bandwidth with better than -25 dB return loss is about 86 GHz, and the antenna gain is 19.3 dBi and while the cross-polarization level is less than -49 dB. The total weight of the horn, including integrated mounting structures for following performance testing, is only 4.2 grams.

articleTitle: Design of A Compact Planar Eight-way Hybrid Power Divider with Ultra-wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact planar eight-way power divider with ultra-wide bandwidth (UWB) is introduced in this paper. To ensure a relative bandwidth of 100% (6~18 GHz), high power capacitance and small size in horizontal direction, a combination of single-ridged waveguide and microstrip line is adopted. In structure, the proposed eight-way power divider presents a relatively small size which meets the requirement of compact distance between output ports. While in electrical performances, the power divider performs well on VSWR (less than 1.38), phase differences (within ±4 degree) and amplitude differences (less than 0.4 dB). The simulation and measured results are provided for comparison.

articleTitle: Broadband Metal Wall Loaded SIW H-Plane Horn Antenna With Improved FTBR
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) H-plane horn antenna with back-lobe suppression for Ka-band application is proposed in this paper. Based on the traditional H-plane SIW horn antenna, by loading a folded metal wall behind the horn aperture, the backward radiation is suppressed. Moreover, for better impedance matching, the substrates are directly extended and metal lines are loaded on the upper and lower substrates separately. Simulation results show that the designed antenna bandwidth reaches 39.9% (from 25.1 to 37.6 GHz). The simulated result also indicates that the proposed antenna achieves stable radiation patterns with the average gain of 9.9 dBi, as well as back-lobe level of larger than 10 dB. Importantly, the front to back ratio (FTBR) of the antenna is better than 20 dB over the operating band basically.

articleTitle: Beamforming and Power Allocation for Uplink NOMA Transmission in Multibeam Satellite Communications With Rate Splitting
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper investigates uplink non-orthogonal mul-tiple access (NOMA) transmission in multibeam satellite commu-nications with rate splitting, where the satellite simultaneously serves multiple ground clusters through multibeam technology while two heterogeneous users in each cluster are paired to benefit from uplink NOMA with rate splitting. Specifically, we first formulate a constrained optimization problem aiming at minimizing the total power subject to the constraints of individual power budget and quality-of-service requirements of the satellite. Afterwards, we propose a partial zero-forcing beamforming scheme along with the alternating direction method of multipliers with reduced computational burden. Finally, simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed scheme compared with the existing works.

articleTitle: Anti-Reactive-Jamming Wireless System: A Strategy of “Masking”
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wireless anti-reactive-jamming system is presented, which involves a legal transceiver pair, a high-power decoy signal transmitter, and a reactive jammer. A “masking” strategy, that is, “do one thing under the cover of another” is utilized to protect the transceiver pair from being jammed. Specifically, a decoy signal is utilized to attract jamming attack(s) and ensure the security of the desired signal. The strategy is demonstrated on a software-defined radio platform - universal software radio peripheral (USRP). The research results show that the proposed method can successfully attract the reactive jammer and protect the desired signal from jamming in practice.

articleTitle: A Dual-polarization Common-aperture Antenna Array for 2G/3G/4G/5G Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-polarization common-aperture base station antenna array covering 2G/3G/4G/5G frequency bands is proposed in this paper. The antenna array includes four dipole antennas working in the 2G/3G/4G frequency band and seven microstrip slot-coupled antennas working in the 5G frequency band. The lower frequency antenna is a dipole antenna based on the principle of sharing a symmetrical array arm, and the working band is 1.7-2.7GHz. In addition, according to the technical application characteristics of the fifth-generation mobile communication system, a microstrip slot-coupled antenna that works in the 3.4-3.6GHz and 4.8-5GHz is designed. It is a new type of base station antenna designed for the working characteristics of different mobile communication frequency bands.

articleTitle: A 125 GHz AMC-Grounded Microstrip Line on Benzocyclobutene Substrate
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An AMC-grounded microstrip line is proposed which shows good transmission performance at lower frequencies. There is a stop band from 60 GHz to 75 GHz, and the insertion loss is large at frequencies higher than 75 GHz. To compose feedlines for AMC-grounded antennas that work at around 125 GHz, a narrow metal strip is inserted in the AMC layer underneath the microstrip. With this modification, the transmission performance around 125 GHz is improved significantly.

articleTitle: A Tunable Nolen Matrix Based on Reconfigurable Phase Shifters
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a new continuous tunable multiple beamforming network composed of a 3 x 3 Nolen matrix and two reconfigurable phase shifters. Two phase shifters with 90° continuous tuning range are cascaded to the outputs of a standard 3 x 3 Nolen matrix in order to realize flexible tuning of the beamforming network, and a total 270° range of phase difference coverage is achieved by tuning these two phase shifters towards different direction. The design method contributes to realize a tapered amplitude distribution, which could help reduce the sidelobe level significantly without additional power dividers or attenuators when an antenna array is connected. The tunable Nolen matrix feeding network designed in this paper operates at 2.45 GHz and has a fractional bandwidth of 3.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, with phase mismatch less than ±10°.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Dual-Band Elliptical Patch Antenna Suitable For WIFI With Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a low profile broadband truncated Elliptic patch microstrip antenna (EPMA) is proposed with dual polarization and dual frequency band based on odd-mode eTM11 and even-mode oTM21. The working principle of the elliptic patch antenna working in eTM11 mode and oTM21 mode is introduced, and by truncating the patch antenna, the oTM21 mode of radiation is transformed from two ends to the broadside. Coupling the stub and slot radiator on the ground plane improved the defect of insufficient impedance bandwidth of the patch antenna. The measured results show that the fabricated antennas obtained the bandwidth of low frequency 2.38GHz-2.7GHz (fractional bandwidth 12.6%) and high frequency 5.1Ghz-5.56ghz (fractional bandwidth 8.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) respectively, the presented antenna is a good candidate for IEEE802.11n (2.4GHZ - 2.48GHz and 5.15GHz - 5.35GHz). In low frequency band, radiation pattern is wide beam, which is suitable for WIFI communication with wide coverage indoor. In high frequency band, the proposed antenna has high gain, which is suitable for WIFI in narrow and long rooms.

articleTitle: Broadband SIW cavity-backed antenna with Orthog-onal T-shaped slot and I-shaped slot
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband planar substrate integrated wave-guide cavity-backed slot antenna working at Ku band is demon-strated in this article. An I-shaped slot, a T-shaped slot and two symmetrical L-shaped slots are designed to expand bandwidth. The antenna can operate at 12.78GHz-16.82GHz with the fractional bandwidth of 27%, while it keeps a stable radiation charac-teristics. The peak gain of the antenna is 6.26dB. These excellent performances make the proposed antenna suitable for the broad-band application of Ku band.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Wideband Bandpass SIW Filters for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Two wideband bandpass filters for the two 5G millimeter-wave bands of 24.75-27.5 GHz and 37-42.5 GHz are presented. The filter is based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and the parallel inductance is realized by metal through-hole. Because of the theoretical size of first hole is too small, a bias distance of the hole is given to make the diameter meet the criterion. Then, machine learning-assisted optimization (MLAO) is used to optimize the two filter models. Finally, simulation results show that the optimized filters can meet the requirements of 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications.

articleTitle: Codebook-based Beam Tracking for RIS Assisted Mobile MmWave Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The emerging reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) technique can effectively compensate the propagation loss in millimeter wave communications. Considering the mobility of users in realistic environment, it is urgent to design efficient beam tracking algorithms for RIS to fast align the target users. In this work, we propose a practical codebook-based RIS passive configuration based on the updating channel parameters, i.e., angle-of-departures (AoDs) of RIS-users links, to avoid complex channel estimation procedure. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has high tracking accuracy, and yields better sum rate performance compared with the conventional channel estimation method.

articleTitle: FMCW-Radar-Based Vital-Sign Monitoring of Pet
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the increasing number of pets worldwide, the health of pets has become a focus of attention in recent years. At the same time, researchers are interested in detecting vital signs of pet, because the vital signs are the important indicators for the diagnosis and treatment of pet diseases. Among vital signs, respiration and heartbeat are the most frequently used. In this paper, based on FMCW radar, different algorithms are utilized to extract the respiration and heartbeat of pet from the radar signal. The respiration rate and heart rate obtained by wearable device are used as reference values to evaluate the accuracy of different algorithms. The experimental results demonstrate that FMCW radar can effectively and accurately monitor the respiration and heartbeat of pet.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Ultra-Wideband Ranging Through Non-Homogeneous Walls
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of inhomogeneous wall obstruction on the ultra-wideband (UWB) ranging error is investigated by experiments. The UWB ranging errors are measured through concrete, brick, gypsum, and wood walls at 10 different positions on each wall. The results demonstrate that for the same wall, the non-homogeneous characteristics of a wall cause fluctuations in the wall's thickness and relative permittivity. The maximum standard deviations of the thickness and relative permittivity are 2 mm and 1.8, respectively. In addition, an efficient UWB through-wall ranging error simulation method is proposed based on the results. The simulated errors are similar to the experimental data. The proposed simulation method is expected to provide an experimental basis for UWB through-wall localization simulations.

articleTitle: An optimization method of scintillation S4c calculation based on genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ionospheric scintillation, reflected in the navigation signals, is defined as the rapid and random fluctuations in the amplitude and phase of GNSS signal. Scintillation indexes S4 and σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">φ</inf> are considered to reflect the fluctuation which are always output by receivers with a sampling rate of at least 50Hz. In this paper, we extend Luo's method [6] of calculating S4c with 1Hz carrier-to-noise density ratio (CNR) by adding the parameter λ. Based on this, we utilize genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize λ to obtain higher accuracy S4c (GA-S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4c</inf>). Compared to the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(50Hz) received by Septentrio PolaRx5S receiver, the root mean square error of GA- S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4c</inf> is 41.38% lower than that of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4c</inf> with original parameter, while the error is larger than that of the least square fitting method. The result demonstrates the feasibility of the optimized λ based on GA to calculate S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4c</inf>.

articleTitle: Ultra Wideband Channel Measurement and Analysis for Low Altitude UAV Air-to-Ground Scenario
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Evaluating and accurately modeling unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) channel model have a significant impact on the design of UAV wireless communication networks. In this pa-per we present an ultra wideband (UWB) channel measurement campaign for low altitude UAV air-to-ground (A2G) scenario. Both line-of-sight (LOS) and non line-of-sight (NLOS) scenarios are considered where the UAV locates at positions with different vertical heights and horizontal places. Based on the channel measurement data, we compare four path loss models to analyze the large scale fading characteristics: the free-space path loss (FSPL) model, the log-distance path loss model (PLM), the 3GPP model and the alpha-beta-gamma (ABG) model. Further, the shadowing fading (SF) is also studied in order to evaluate the impact of blockage by human body on channel characteristics. The result shows that the ABG model has a higher fitting degree, and the maximum shadow fading in the NLOS scenario is twice as much as in the LOS scenario. The conclusion of the paper can be applied in the design and evaluation of UAV communications.

articleTitle: A 32–40 GHz Low-Noise Amplifier for Ka-band Phased Array Radar System in 65-nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A broadband two-stage differential low noise amplifier(LNA) for Ka-band phased array radar system is proposed in this paper. The presented LNA consists of differential cascode structure with inductive source-degeneration and neutralization capacitance technology, which is fabricated in 65-nm CMOS process. A transformer-based broadband matching network is used in input terminal to realize the measured S11 < - 13 dB at 32–40 GHz. The measured maximum gain achieves 12.25 dB at 36 GHz with a 3-dB bandwidth from 32-40GHz. The minimum noise factor is 6.06 dB at 35.5 GHz. It draws 20mA from a 1V supply. The size of LNA core area is only 520µm x 385µm.

articleTitle: Dual function flexible coplanar waveguide for feeding antenna of balanced structure
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A flexible coplanar waveguide (CPW) design is presented suitable for feeding planar antenna with a balanced structure. Two features are provided by the flexible design, transition from balance on the antenna side to unbalance on the receiver side; transformation of characteristic input impedance of the antenna to the value of a standard load. It is essential for the CPW to be bended to fit the purposes hence the effect of bending of CPW on the transmission performance and method to feed planar antenna are investigated. The common mode propagation due to the inserted feedline is observed and the solution to eliminate the auxiliary common-mode effect in the structure is also discussed.

articleTitle: Wideband metasurface electromagnetic energy harvester with polarization insensitivity
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Wideband metasurface electromagnetic energy har-vester is proposed with polarization insensitivity. A metasurface unit cell is composed of four rectangular blocks and an inscribed ring. The load is connected to the metal floor through 4 through holes. Electromagnetic energy is captured and consumed in the load. Experimental simulation results show that in the 5.1GHz-6.2GHz frequency band, the working efficiency of the metasurface unit exceeds 90%, and the relative wideband is 18.97%. The working wideband with a working efficiency of more than 50% is 76.55%. The electromagnetic energy harvester also has polarization insensitive characteristics.

articleTitle: A Conformal Broadband Monopole Antenna for VHF/UHF Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a conformal broadband monopole antenna working at very high frequency (VHF) band and ultra-high frequency (UHF) band. The proposed antenna is composed of an open ring ground and a circular monopole patch, which is fed by modified coplanar waveguide (CPW). Base on analysis of the effect of open ring ground, a broadband CPW-fed antenna is designed. Simulated results show that, with the electrical dimension of 0.25λ × 0.25λ at the minimum operation frequency, the voltage standing wave ration (VSWR) of the antenna is less than 2 from 98MHz to 622MHz (145%).

articleTitle: Multipath Component Clustering Based on Improved Self-organizing Feature Map for 5G Millimeter Wave Radio Channels
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Recently, clustering algorithm has become an important research hotspot, as cluster based wireless channel modeling can reduce the complexity of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) channel models. In this work, a clustering algorithm based on maximum-minimum distance algorithm (MMD) assisted Self-organizing Feature Map (SOM) is proposed, namely, MMD-SOM. Specifically, MMD algorithm is used to initialize the weight of the network, which solves the problem of inadequate network training in traditional SOM caused by randomly setting the initial weights. Furthermore, an output layer is added to the network, which gets over that SOM is easy to be over-trained in the unsupervised situation. The performance of the improved algorithm is evaluated based on the measured and simulated channel data, both numerical simulations and experimental clustering results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Coupling Reduction in Closed Coupled Dual-Band Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper,a closely coupled dual-band microstrip patch antennas that resonates at 3.6 and 4 GHz is presented. The isolation between array elements can be enhanced synchronously at both frequencies by etching a slot- shaped defected ground structure (DGS) and vertically placing a dielectric wall with microstrips on both sides. The slot-shaped DGS can reduce the antenna mutual coupling at 3.6 GHz due to its stop-band characteristics, while the pair of microstrips printed on the dielectric wall acting as a half-wavelength resonator is used to achieve decoupling at 4 GHz. Simulation results show that the isolation between array antennas decreased from -8 dB to -26.1 dB at 3.6 GHz and from -9 dB to -30.2 dB at 4 GHz. The measured results indicate that the isolation has a noticeable increase of about 19.9 dB and 23.1 dB at two operating frequencies.

articleTitle: Satellite Navigation Multipath Channel Sparse Reconstruction Scheme Applied in Performance Evaluation of Constellation Channel Emulation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we study how to decrease the computational complexity of constellation channel emulation and keep the identical results, when employing a channel model in the evaluation of satellite navigation receivers for zero on site testing. We propose a sparse reconstruction scheme for the satellite navigation channel model. In this scheme, we explore how to create a channel impulse response subset via K-medoids technique, which can retain the multipath-error effect of the original channel. The obtained sparse channel can be used for realistic emulation on the satellite navigation channel model without huge hardware resources. This allows a fast and cost-efficient implementable emulation system. The evaluation results indicate that the proposed scheme and approach provides good result under the preservation of the auto-correlation function criterion.

articleTitle: Study on the Composite EM Scattering from Sea Surface with a Ship Target based on Scale Model
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The main purpose of this work is to use the scale model to study the composite scattering from sea surface and ship target based on the refined facet scattering field model (RFSFM) together with the geometrical optics and physical optics (GO-PO) method. The feasibility and error of freshwater used in the scale model are analyzed by the comparisons of Fresnel reflection coefficient between the freshwater and seawater, as well as the radar cross section (RCS) of sea surface and coupling field, between the prototype composite scene and scale model. The numerical results show that the freshwater used in the scale model to investigate the composite scattering from a ship target on sea surface is feasible when the frequency is larger than 10GHz, which could provide the theoretical basis for the scale model measurement.

articleTitle: A Compact Magnetoelectric Dipole Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Antenna-in-Package Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact magnetoelectric (ME) dipole antenna is presented in this paper. By etching four parallel transverse slits in the surface of the antenna, the current path flowing along the patch could be lengthened, and therefore the antenna size can be reduced. To verify the design idea, a prototype was designed at 60 GHz. The antenna size was optimized to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.67 \times 1.57\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, namely 0.33 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}\times 0.31\lambda_{0}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the wavelength in the free space at 60 GHz. A simulated 18.6% 10-dB impedance bandwidth can be obtained, from 54.7 to 65.9 GHz. The simulated peak gain is 7.4 dBi at 60 GHz. This proposed compact antenna can be a good candidate for millimeter-wave (mmW) Antenna-in-Package (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> iP) designs with High-density interconnect (HDI) technology.

articleTitle: Investigation on Simulation of Sea Surface SAR Image
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the real SAR imaging process, a simulation method of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image for time-varying sea surface is proposed. Time-varying sea surface scene and electromagnetic scattering model are built to obtain the profile and complex reflectivity of sea surface for the SAR echo signal simulation. The radial velocity due to the orbit velocity of the large-scale waves would cause additional Doppler shift and Velocity Bunching (VB) effect. In this paper, the VB effect in SAR image is simulated via changing phase of echo signal and producing an additional Doppler shift. The simulated results show the VB effect of SAR. This work is helpful for better understanding SAR images of ocean waves.

articleTitle: Decoupling of a MIMO Antenna Pair by Common and Differential Modes Cancellation For 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposed a new multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna structure with a shared radiator, which is proposed for the fifth generation (5G) terminal phone. Theoretically, it is proved that if the common mode (CM) impedances are same as differential mode (DM) impedances, the mutual coupling effect between two separate antennas can be completely eliminated. In particular, analyzing the resistance and reactance relationship of the two modes and the self-impedance by impedance-compensation to realize decoupling. The results of simulated and measured show that the two-antenna MIMO system can all achieve good isolation larger than 13dB from 4.4 to 5 GHz, only with lumped element capacitance compensation structure.

articleTitle: Design and Implement of Beam Steering Based on Phased Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Phased array radar has a significant role in military and civilian use. The development trend of the phased array radar front system is a large number of phase shifter units, a small space, and a complex structure. These characteristics correspondingly require the beam steering system to have the characteristics of fast calculation speed, small structure, accurate data compensation, and many additional control functions. This article first introduces the basic principles, composition and functions of the beam steering system, and then introduces the hardware and software schemes of it based on the actual needs of the project. On this basis, the terminal software is further designed to realize the self-detection of the beam steering board. The modularization and intelligence of the entire beam control system has certain adaptability and promotion value.

articleTitle: Study on Analytical Model of Discrete Raindrop Size Distribution
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Rain drop size distribution (rain drop spectrum) is the key element to the theoretical prediction of specific attenuation by rain, and a large number of models for this have appeared in the literature. The measures rain drop spectrum is generally discrete, and analytical formulas need to be established to facilitate application. In this paper, a new analytical expression of Laws-Parsons distribution has been proposed, which have better accuracy than Ulbrich's expression and de Wolf's expression for the calculation of rain specific attenuation. Moreover, by analyzing the average raindrop spectra of Qingdao, Guangzhou and Xinxiang, it is found that the Marshall-Palmer distribution is in the best match, especially in the millimeter wave frequency band.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study on Bistatic RCS of Measured Targets for Automatic Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As a basic attribute of target, radar cross section (RCS) is an important recognition source in the field of automatic target recognition (ATR) in the low-resolution radars. The correct understanding of target characteristics is the basis of target recognition. In this paper, the RCS characteristics of general aviation aircraft and civil aviation aircraft are statistically analyzed by using the measured data collected by a multistatic passive radar. The analysis results show that aircrafts with different sizes and shapes have obvious differences in RCS characteristics, indicating that their statistical characteristics can be used for ATR. Results obtained in this paper can provide beneficial guidance for the study of target recognition in passive radars.

articleTitle: Investigation of high power and efficiency microwave power transfer system at 5.8GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A C-band microwave power transfer (MPT) system is designed and investigated in the article. The transmitting microwave power is greater than one kilowatt. The phased arrays are used to transmit large amounts of power to the receiving terminal. The high power feed system between the source and transmitting antenna is a waveguide splitter to reduce loss as much as possible. There are 256 quadrate patches to constitute a sub-array with size of 42 cm. The transmitting arrays are consisted of four sub-arrays and each sub-array is etched on Rogers 4003C substrate with ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>= 3.55 and 32 mil thickness. The transmitting antenna gain is 30.8 dBi and the return loss greater than 10 dB. The rectifying patch antenna consist of a high efficiency receiving antenna and rectifier circuit at 5.8 GHz. The single GaN diode conversion efficiency of radiofrequency to direct current (RF-DC) was tested more than 70% with 33 dBm input power and 430Q-load. In the process of study, the practical transmission power and efficiency are more than 1.5kW and 10%, respectively. The excellent performance of the MPT system indicates that they are suitable for wireless power supply application with ten meters.

articleTitle: Efficient Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering from Targets based on UDS and SVR
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic scattering characteristics of complex targets have always been the research focus in radar recognition. In this paper, we propose an efficient method that combines sampling design with machine learning to predict the radar cross section (RCS) of complex targets. In particular, uniform design sampling (UDS) is adopted to acquire the target's backscattering data of high representativeness, support vector regression (SVR) is trained as an efficient and accurate surrogate model for regression. Afterward, several experiments were carried out based on a SLICY model, and the results fully verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Investigation on SAR Image of Target on Rough Surface
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of target detection and recognition technology, SAR image simulation technology for complex target is of great significance. In this paper, the electromagnetic scattering of complex target on rough surface is studied by SBR method, and the simulation results are compared with FEKO software to verify the effectiveness of the algorithm. Through the electromagnetic scattering model, the SAR echo data of complex target and rough surfaces in broadband are obtained. The polar format algorithm is used to simulate the SAR image of target on the surface.

articleTitle: A Novel Magneto-Electric Dipole for Wideband Application
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel wideband magneto-electric dipole is comprised of a couple of shorted patches with rectangle hole in vertical direction and a planar dipole placed horizontally. A r-shaped feed line with a circular metal sheet is employed to feed the element, whose horizontal part resonance at 1.4GHz. Four short planes connected with ground ensure high gain and less back radiation. There is an impedance bandwidth of 98.8% for VSWR≤2 (1.31 to 3.78 GHz) from the simulation results. This type of antenna has stable gain radiation pattern with low cross polarization and almost similar E- and H-plane radiation pattern. Moreover, a maximum realized gain of 8.6dBi and an average gain of 8dBi over the operating bandwidth is realized.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler Feature Extraction of Space Object based on Narrowband Radar with Real-Data Result from Incoherent Scatter Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The micro motion of space object can cause sinusoidal modulation in phase of radar echo, referred to as the micro-doppler effect. Here we propose a method to extract the micro-doppler feature of target from its time-frequency distribution. The residual translational motion after match filtering needs compensated at first to keep only the non-stational part of spectrogram in time-frequency analysis, which is prepared for inverse Radon transform (IRT) that can form a 2-D imaging of target in transverse plane composed of scattering centres with diverse radius and initial gesture angle. Both the simulation and real-data analysis show promising results.

articleTitle: An L/S Multi-Band Shared-Aperture Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an L/S multi-band shared-aperture circularly polarized antenna is proposed. Generally, a circularly polarized wave can be implemented by feeding four radiation patches with 90° phase difference in turn. For each frequency band (B1 and B3) in the L-band, four patches are fed by probes connected to their feeding network respectively, which is composed mainly of three Wilkinson power dividers. In S-band, four patches are also fed by probes connected to a feeding network, but, the feeding network is composed of two directional couplers and two Wilkinson power dividers to realize dual-frequency dual-circularly-polarization. The centrosymmetric structure keeps the antenna having a good axial ratio. The simulation results show that the gain of the L/S-band antenna at frequency band of B3 (1.266~1.34 GHz), B1 (1.556~1.566 GHz), Sd (2.05~2.15 GHz) and Su (2.2~2.35 GHz) is more than 3dBi. The impedance bandwidth (VSWR<2) in B3 / B1 / Sd / Su band is about 19.5% / 47.0% 128.8% / 17.8%, respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Various Shield Grounding Modes on CM Crosstalk between Shielded Cables
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, simulation models were built to analyze effect of the number and position of grounding points on common-mode crosstalk between shielded cables. Effects of various grounding modes were compared deeply. The simulation results were finally verified by experimentation.

articleTitle: Composite Scattering from Dielectric Rough Surface with Target based on Hybrid MoM-PO Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the hybrid MoM-PO is proposed to simulate the composite scattering from a target located above or below a dielectric rough surface. In this approach, the traditional method of moments (MoM) is firstly used to calculate the induced current of the rough surface or the target alone. Then the process of the multiple iteration physical optics method (PO-PO) is applied to deal with the mutual coupling of the rough surface and the target. The accuracy and efficiency of the hybrid MoM-PO method are assessed by comparing the numerical results of the hybrid MoM-PO with the PO-PO and the traditional MoM. Comparing with the PO-PO, the accuracy of the hybrid MoM-PO is improved. And the hybrid MoM-PO costs less time than the traditional MoM.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Layer Element for Wideband and Highly Efficient Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel dual-layer highly efficient and wideband transmitarray antenna (TA) is proposed. First, a novel wideband TA unit cell with simple structure is presented. The simulated results of element show an adequate phase variation range over 360°. Then, a 15x15-element TA is designed and simulated by ANYSY HFSS. The final simulated results show that the presented antenna can obtain 11.8% 1 dB gain bandwidth (20.7- 23.3 GHz) and 50.5% aperture efficiency. Its peak gain is 26.9 dBi at 22 GHz.

articleTitle: A Frequency Reconfigurable Band-pass Filter Based on Microstrip Open-Loop Hole Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Design of a microstrip bandpass filter (BPF) with frequency reconfigurability is presented in this paper. The designed filter is constructed by using dual-mode open-loop hole resonator (DOHR). Varactor diodes are used as tuning elements in order to adjust center frequency. The achieved results indicate a center frequency tuning range of 2.04~2.5GHz, which can be used for LTE, CDMA, WLAN, etc.

articleTitle: 3D Metal Printed UHF-Band Feed for Satellite Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As a potential processing method for satellite applications, several additive manufacturing techniques have been applied to build some spaceborne feed horns and microwave components from C- to V-band. However, these techniques cannot be effectively applied to process low-band products with large size, such as UHF band antenna feed. This paper presents a hybrid process for the large size product, which combines Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing and milling. An UHF-band antenna feed is manufactured through this hybrid process. Compared with traditional subtractive processes, the material used by this hybrid process is only 1/6, and the processing cycle is shortened from two months to 25 days.

articleTitle: A Method for Inversion of Electrical Parameters of Materials Based on Ray Tracing Algorithm and Stochastic Gradient Descent Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In wireless channel deterministic models, it is important part for the setting of environmental electrical parameters. Traditional calculation methods such as genetic algorithm and the ant colony algorithm are inefficient. This paper studies the stochastic gradient descent(SGD) algorithm to solve the electrical parameters. The simulation results show that the method based on ray tracing algorithm and SGD algorithm to solve the electrical parameters of materials is feasible and efficient.

articleTitle: Antenna Design of Millimeter Wave Radar for Smart Toilet
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Presence detection, seating detection, and water level detection in smart toilets have received widespread attentions. This paper uses a low-cost, simple structured 24G millimeter-wave radar with one transmitter and two receivers to achieve these functions. Presence detection and seating detection require the antenna to radiate signals forward, while water level detection requires the antenna to radiate signals vertically down to the water surface. This paper proposes a new bidirectional radiating antenna of millimeter-wave radar. The transmitting antenna is a hybrid end-fire and broadside radiating antenna, composed of the Vivaldi antenna and the wideband high efficiency electromagnetic structure (WHEMS) antenna. The hybrid end-fire radiating antenna is used for presence detection and seating detection, and broadside radiating antenna is used for water level detection. With advantages of the antenna, we have achieved accurate tracking of toilet users, and the water level measurement accuracy can reach ±2 mm.

articleTitle: Wireless Channel Characterization for the High-Speed Flying Trains in Vacuum Tube Scenario Based on Propagation Graph Modeling Theory
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the development of conventional wheel high speed railway, the Vacuum Tube High-speed Flying Train (high-speed flying train) has gradually entered people's vision. In order to analysis and evaluate the wireless channel characterization for the in vacuum tube scenarios. A modeling way based on propagation graph modeling theory and Lambertian scattering pattern is adopted. By using this way, the virtual channel impulse response (CIR) considering the line-of-sight (LoS) and single-bounced components is obtained. Then the wireless channel characterizations including the Doppler power spectrum and the K factor are analyzed and evaluated. And the results of train and no train in the tube are compared. The obtained results will provide reference for the future communication system design in the vacuum tube scenarios.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Interference Effect of Speech Communication System
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With the ubiquitous wireless network access, the limited frequency band resources and the rapid increase of equipment make the interference frequency higher and higher. Whether in military or civil fields, speech signal is one of the main signals transmitted by modern communication system. The speech quality output by communication system is the key factor to evaluate the overall performance. Evaluating the performance of those systems is of great importance to promote the quality of speech communication. In this paper, the deep convolution neural network is used to evaluate the quality of speech communication. Compared with the traditional machine learning evaluation method, the non-reference evaluation model is realized, and the evaluation accuracy has been improved by 8%.

articleTitle: 2.4GHz Bluetooth Frequency Band Performance of Folded WHEMS Antenna in TPMS
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the tire pressure monitor system (TPMS), the low gain and low radiation efficiency of the electrically small antenna lead to the low efficiency of the wireless transmission of the system. In this paper, we propose a new type of antenna called folded WHEMS to improve the wireless transmission efficiency, while using 2.4GHz Bluetooth frequency band to reduce its battery power consumption and prolong the usage time of the device. And then we will build a model in FEKO to simulate and analyze the antenna performance in TPMS and measure in anechoic chamber. The simulated and measured results show that the folded WHEMS antenna has great performance and can be applied in TPMS.

articleTitle: Optimization of Outdoor Ray-Tracing Algorithm Based on Artificial Fish Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the ray-tracing algorithm is used to perform electromagnetic simulation calculation in outdoor scenes, and is improved the simulation accuracy by using an artificial fish swarm algorithm to optimize the model electromagnetic parameters, that reduce the root mean square error value of the calculated power of ray-tracing algorithm and the measured power data for the problem of inaccurate modeling of simulation model electrical parameters. Firstly, the measured data are selectively acquired in the outdoor environment, and secondly, the artificial fish swarm algorithm is used to optimize the range of electrical parameters of the ray-tracing algorithm to improve the electromagnetic calculation accuracy of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Probing Cosmic Dawn in a Global Spectrum Detection System
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dedicated detection system has been proposed in this paper for probing Cosmic Dawn through measuring the 21cm global spectrum. A wide-band antenna with low beam chromaticity has been developed for the detection system, real-time calibration with a set of calibration suits enable solution of system parameters and understanding the system performance. Preliminary results have been obtained through a series testing and observation in radio quiet zone-Hongliuxia Station in Xinjian province.

articleTitle: Compact Planar Antenna Array for X-Band Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact planar microstrip antenna array with low side-lobe and low profile is presented in this paper. The array unit is composed of two dielectric substrates layers, which enhance the peak gain in the main direction. The double-layer microstrip antenna unit achieves a gain of 8.7 dBi. While the whole antenna array is combined of 24 units, which feeding network is integrated on the same layer with the driven patches. The 24-elements planar array has achieved side lobe levels (SLLs) lower than 20.6 dB for both the phi=0 deg and phi=90 deg planes. The simulated results also reveal that the proposed antenna array achieves good impedance matching (VSWR ≤ 1.3) and gain performance (peak gain 21.5 dBi) from 9.3 to 9.9 GHz. Overall dimension of the proposed microstrip planar antenna array is 3.55λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×5.12λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.30λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at 9.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Cross band and Wide Bandwidth Dynamic Channel Simulator
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The wireless channel simulator can perform half-physical simulations of channel characteristics such as path loss, multipath fading, and frequency shift as a measuring instrument for wireless communication system testing and performance evaluation. To support the technical requirements of wireless channel simulation, we constructed a cross band and wide bandwidth dynamic channel simulator based on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). The actual test results show that the multipath fading distribution results of the channel simulator are consistent with the theory. Thus, it can provide a test method for the whole life cycle of the wireless communication system.

articleTitle: A Circular Polarization Cassegrain Reflectarray Antenna for Beamscanning Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a cassegrain reflectarray antenna is proposed for beamscanning applications. The proposed antenna consists of a main reflectarray, a sub reflector and a circular polarization horn as the feed source. The main reflectarray uses spitted-ring elements with different rotating angles to achieve the desirable phase shifting of the reflectarray. The sub-reflector is designed as a hyperboloidal surface to obtain good radiation performance. In order to obtain the beamscanning performance, the phase shifting on the main reflectarray is calculated and the simulation results are analyzed. A prototype of the proposed antenna is simulated at Ka band. Simulation results exhibit a maximum gain of 24.9dBi in the boresight direction, and the scanning gain of 23.6dBi, 23.2dBi, 21.37dBi, 20dBi at the pointing angles of 15°, 30°, 45°, 60° respectively.

articleTitle: Generation of OAM vortex electromagnetic wave by using microstrip antenna array
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The OAM vortex electromagnetic wave are generated by using the particular circular phased microstrip antenna array, which can provide more efficient and reliable transmission of information. Based on the theoretical analysis of OAM, the proposed phased microstrip antenna array can generate vortex electromagnetic waves carrying OAM at a center frequency of 6 GHz. The excitation is carried out by using the phase difference between adjacent antenna elements as a constant value, and a circular antenna array with a double-layer circular microstrip antenna as the antenna element is designed. By controlling the phase difference between the antenna elements, the orbital angular momentum with OAM mode numbers of 0, 1, 2, 3 are obtained. It is known from the results that by designing antenna array with different structures and changing the phase difference between the antenna elements, vortex electromagnetic waves carrying good orbital angular momentum can be obtained.

articleTitle: Surface Wave Conversion for Enhanced, Robust and Wide-Angle Absorption
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The EM metasurface absorber has essential applications in radiation prevention, energy collection and stealth technology. In this paper, we propose a simpler design method for perfect metasurface absorber by combing the surface wave conversion supercell (SWCS) and resonance supercell (RS). We take the first order Mie resonance of SrTiO3 dielectric cylinder at 8 GHz for illustration. The RS reduces the scatterings of surface wave in inter-SWCSs, enhancing the absorption and reaching perfect absorption. Due to the surface wave conversion effect, the composited absorption supercell (CAS) is more robust than uniform single absorption structure. The dispersion relation shows that the surface wave cannot propagate in RS, solving the problem of impedance mismatch in the inter-SWCSs. Moreover, we propose the two-dimensional designed CAS for polarization-insensitive and wide-angle absorption. Our work provides a new prospect for surface wave conversion effect in EM absorption domain.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a short linear antenna with a cylindrical plasma reflector
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The radiation and receiving pattern of a short linear antenna surrounded by discharge tubes was measured. They were investigated for different numbers of switched-on lamps, as well as different values of the discharge current. Measurements were carried out in the frequency range 0.5 - 1.5 GHz by using a spectrum analyzer with a tracking generator. The parameters of the gas-discharge plasma were estimated. The influence of electron density and frequency on the radiation pattern is determined. An analysis of the measured characteristics by simulation as well as by using simple model of a ring antenna array is represented.

articleTitle: Adversarial Jamming for a More Effective Constellation Attack
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The common jamming mode in wireless commu-nication is band barrage jamming, which is controllable and difficult to resist. Although this method is simple to implement, it is obviously not the best jamming waveform. Therefore, based on the idea of adversarial examples, we propose the adversarial jamming waveform, which can independently optimize and find the best jamming waveform. We attack QAM with adversarial jamming and find that the optimal jamming waveform is equiva-lent to the amplitude and phase between the nearest constellation points. Furthermore, by verifying the jamming performance on a hardware platform, it is shown that our method significantly improves the bit error rate compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Impact of Radio Frequency Interference on GNSS Ionospheric Scintillation Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ionospheric scintillation has seriously adverse impacts on the propagation of GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) signals and can cause signals received by GNSS receiver to fade. Therefore, it is important to study the characteristics of the occurrence and variations of GNSS ionospheric scintillation. In the analysis of single-frequency GNSS ionospheric scintillation data, radio frequency interference may be misjudged as amplitude scintillation because radio frequency interference may cause large values of the amplitude scintillation index S4 for the received GNSS signal. In order to minimize the impact of radio frequency interference on GNSS ionospheric scintillation data analysis, ionospheric scintillation measurements of the raw signal power (or carrier-to-noise density ratio) at multiple GNSS frequencies should be used to study the characteristics of the occurrence and variations of GNSS ionospheric scintillation.

articleTitle: Calibration of Ray Tracing Model Based on Feedback Step Method in Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Ray tracing model as a deterministic model in the prediction of radio waves propagation has the advantages of fast operation and accurate prediction. However, its accuracy depends on the preset electric parameters, especially for complex indoor environment, the relative dielectric constant and conductivity of the wall is particularly important to the model. Therefore, an electric parameter optimum algorithm is needed to use for model calibration. In this paper, an indoor scene of an apartment is taken as an example. Based on the measured power value, a feedback step search method is used to correct the electrical parameters of wall material, so that the corrected model can predict the power of this particular scene more accurately.

articleTitle: Time Domain Analysis on the Common-mode EMI of a Twelve-phase Generator Rectifier System
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A common-mode EMI model based on ideal voltage source equivalence is proposed and analyzed for a twelve-phase generator rectifier system. A voltage state model of common-mode of the generator rectifier system is proposed according to the time-domain analysis of the equivalent circuit in the conducting and commutating process of the twelve-phase rectifier system. The characteristic of the common-mode EMI is obtained and analyzed in this paper.

articleTitle: A Compact and Planar Monopole Antenna with Discrete Slow-Wave Structures
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A microstrip monopole patch antenna with discrete slow-wave structure is proposed in this paper. Aiming to realize the antenna with a very compact size, the proposed antenna is designed to include a slotted circular patch, discrete slow-wave structures, and a set of shorting vias. The well-matched results of simulation and measurement show that, the proposed antenna has a maximum gain of 4.54 dBi and a low profile of 0.02 wavelength. More importantly, compared with that of the referenced circular patch-ring antenna, the electric size of the proposed antenna is significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Properties of a Layered Isotropic Chiral Slab Using the Propagation Matrix Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic characteristics of homogeneous and inhomogeneous slabs containing the active isotropic chiral medium are investigated using the propagation matrix method. The effects of the gain-loss, thickness, chirality parameter, angle, and polarization states of incident plane waves on co- and cross-polarized reflection and transmission coefficients for a single layer or layered active chiral slab are discussed.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Assisted Wireless Communication: Path loss Modeling with Multipath Fading
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is a key enabling technology for 6G. The free-space path loss model of RIS has been proposed in existing research, but the influence of multipath is not taken into account. In this paper, by establishing a RIS-assisted wireless communication model that considers multipath factors, the path loss of the RIS-assisted SISO system affected by multipath fading is modeled and the path loss simulation results are fitted with the CI model. This work adds the impact of multipath on RIS path loss model for the first time and lays the foundation for the practical application of RIS.

articleTitle: A Perspective on Pet Emotion Monitoring Using Millimeter Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Understanding a pet's emotions is the key to improving pet welfare. Previous studies have demonstrated that pet emotions can be interpreted by using pet vital signs, and the most effective way to monitor and identify vital signs is millimeter wave radar, but few studies have applied millimeter wave radar to pet emotion monitoring. In this paper, we summarize the changes of vital signs of pets under different emotions through literature combing. The relevant studies on vital sign radar are also analyzed and compared, and the technical features and challenges of millimeter wave radar are summarized. Finally, an innovative research direction of applying millimeter-wave radar to pet emotion monitoring is proposed.

articleTitle: A Slot Metasurface for the MIMO Antenna Isolation Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this study, a slot metasurface is proposed to suppress the mutual coupling of the MIMO antenna. The designed metasurface is composed of many periodic slots and is placed directly above the MIMO antenna. The coupling of the MIMO antenna is reduced by suppressing the TM wave propagation between antenna arrays. The simulation results show that when the distance between the antenna elements is 0.023λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>is the wavelength at 3.5 GHz), in the working frequency band, the mutual coupling between the antenna elements is suppressed by more than 27 dB, which is improved by about 20 dB.

articleTitle: A High-Isolation Dual-Polarized Microstrip Patch Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized 4×4 array with high ports isolation and low cross-polarization. Based on multi-layer microstrip patch structure, the two polarization modes are excited by “cross” shaped aperture which is coupled by two special feeding lines, respectively. To obtain low cross-polarization, the aperture is placed in the center of the ground plane to improve the symmetry of radiation pattern. The bandwidth is increased by adding parasitic patch and hollowing its substrate. Metal via holes were designed around the patches to suppress the surface waves propagation to improve the scanning performance. The simulated results show that, the impedance bandwidth with VSWR < 2 reaches 30%, isolation is more than 55dB, cross-polarization levels are below -57dB with scanning range reaching to 50° in the E-plane and 40° in the H-plane.
