articleTitle: Time-Domain Near-Field Scattering from Composite Target-Ocean Scene Illuminated by Far-Field Antenna Sources
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A near-field time-domain shooting and bouncing rays (TDSBR) method is proposed to analyze the transient scattered near-fields from a composite target-ocean scene illuminated by far-field antenna sources. The time-domain far-field incident sources can be obtained by a convolution of pulsed excitation with the inverse Fourier transform (IFT) of antenna radiation far-fields. The TDPO near-field integral expressions for dielectric surface are reduced to closed-form expressions by applying locally expanded phase approximations and surface partitioning. The forward and backward tracing technique and the equivalent mirror antenna method are used to obtain the ray bouncing path in the composite scene under antenna radiation. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Leaky Wave Antenna Based on Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line with Spatial Harmonic Suppression
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the leaky wave antenna (LWA) based on the substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) structure can suppress high-order spatial harmonics by adding slots with different periods on its conductor surface. Through the spatial harmonic suppression theory, the leaky wave antenna can realize the beam scanning from backward to forward with a single radiated harmonic, and the working frequency band of a single spatial harmonic can be expanded. The design antenna of -lst-order-spatia harmonic can cover the beam scanning range from - 68°to 78°throughout a frequency band from 13 to 40 GHz, and this developed design is desirable for the wireless communication, beam scanning radar and other applications.

articleTitle: Research on Composite Electromagnetic Scattering Based on MOM-PO Hybrid Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The electromagnetic scattering properties of three-dimensional objects are computationally analyzed by the method of moments-physical optics (MOM-PO). The hybrid method considers the mutual influence between the numerical method region and the high-frequency approximation region to calculate the electromagnetic scattering of the composite target. This method greatly improves the calculation speed while ensuring a certain accuracy, and makes the calculation of large targets possible.

articleTitle: An Application of Double-sided Parallel Strip Line Resonator in Dielectric High Frequency Test
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel double-sided parallel-strip line (DSPSL) resonator is proposed. A new technique using the double-sided parallel-strip line resonator is presented for the measurement of complex permittivity of microwave dielectric substrate. The physical model of the test is established by transmission line theory, and the complex permittivity of the sample to be tested is calculated by resonator theory and angle-preserving transformation. Experiments are carried out on several typical samples to validate the feasibility of our improved technique. The test frequencies range from 65 to 110 GHz. The method has the advantages of simple test fixture, high test accuracy, wide frequency range and fast test speed.

articleTitle: Investigation of Transmission Phase of SSPP Lines with Linear Tapered Transitions
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The transmission phase of spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) transmission lines with linear tapered transitions is investigated in this paper. Based on the theory of microwave network, the scatter parameters of the whole structure are calculated, which agree well with the simulated results of commercial solver. Moreover, by using the dispersion equation of SSPP unit cell, the transmission phase of the transition part can be obtained from the SSPP transmission line with equivalent height. Good agreement is achieved between the calculation and simulation, proving the validity of the proposed method in this paper.

articleTitle: A GPU Acceleration Algorithm for Urban Electromagnetic Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The development of wireless communication technology relies on the accuracy of propagation modeling simulation. In this paper, we propose a real-time electromagnetic propagation modeling method for complex urban environments, combined with a high-precision 3D physical model of the city, to achieve accurate prediction of electromagnetic (EM) wave coverage. This method takes full advantage of GPU multi-threading and implements shooting and bouncing rays based EM wave ray tracing based on NVIDIA Optix pipeline, and then realizes the attenuation calculation of EM field intensity using geometric optics and uniform theory of diffraction. We first perform 3D reconstruction and surface reconstruction in the actual scene to obtain an accurate 3D physical model, then use the Optix interface to implement forward ray tracing, calculate the field strength of each ray when it reaches the receiving antenna, and performs vector superposition to obtain the total field strength at the receiving antenna. The experimental results show that the accuracy and efficiency of the process have achieved satisfactory results.

articleTitle: A Source Reconstruction Method for Near-Field Data Inversion
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces an electromagnetic inverse source technique used for near-field(NF) antenna measurement-the source reconstruction method (SRM). We have established a NF-NF equivalent model to realize the reconstruction of the electromagnetic current on the reconstructed surface. Since this method has no strict requirements on the source, it can be used for antenna or scatterer diagnosis. Examples show that this method can accurately fit the NF characteristics of the source.

articleTitle: A Compact and High Gain SIW H-Plane Horn Antenna With Stepped Hard Boundary Condition
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact and high gain substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) H-plane horn antenna loading stepped hard boundary condition is proposed in this paper, which is applied for the Ka-band. The proposed antenna is based on the traditional H-plane horn antenna, and by loading stepped hard boundary condition, the aperture efficiency and gain of the proposed antenna also can be improved. The stepped hard boundary condition is achieved by excavating the internal dielectric of the tapered horn. Three layers of the dielectrics are added in advance of the aperture to achieve better the impedance matching. The simulated result indicates that the proposed antenna has a wide bandwidth of 14.6% (from 31.1 to 36 GHz) and an average gain of 9.38dBi. Importantly, compared with the original antenna, the proposed antenna achieves an average gain improvement of 0.6 dBi from 31 to 34 GHz and 2 dBi from 34–36 GHz. Moreover, Under the same aperture conditions, the longitudinal length is shorter by 21.3% than the original antenna.

articleTitle: An Inversion Method for Cross Well Electromagnetic Imaging through Casing
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Cross well electromagnetic imaging technology breaks through the limit of logging distance of single well, achieves the accurate description of remaining oil distribution between two wells, reduces the blindness of infill drilling in the later stage of production well, saves the cost and improves the recovery rate. In this paper, a new method is proposed to remove the casing effect, the theoretical formula of through casing inversion imaging method is derived, which not only speeds up the convergence of inversion results, but also improves the accuracy of inversion results. This method not only removes the casing effect, but also removes the influence of the instrument, so that the cross well electromagnetic is free from calibration before logging. It can also be used for cross well electromagnetic inversion in non-casing wells. The numerical simulation results verify the correctness of the method. Finally, the inversion results are consistent compared to the original measured data without calibration coefficients of the previous instrument. This method solves the problem of inversion of cross well electromagnetic imaging data through casing.

articleTitle: An Embedded Printed Log-periodic Dipole Array Antenna for UAV Swarm Cooperative Positioning
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a printed log-periodic dipole array (LPDA) antenna embedded in the wing structure for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is presented. Simulation results show that the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) is less than 2.5 over the entire operating bandwidth (0.38 GHz - 1.3 GHz) of the LPDA. Directional radiation and stable radiation pattern have also been validated over the whole frequency range. These advantages indicate that the proposed antenna design is applicable to UAV swarm cooperative positioning system.

articleTitle: Ray-Tracing-Based Indoor Channel Prediction Using Point Cloud Geometrical Modeling
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An accurate method of modeling indoor environment for ray tracing algorithm is presented in this paper. The ray tracing model has been commonly used in modeling indoor channel these years. In order to provide accurate environment information for ray tracing, we use the laser scanner to obtain the point cloud data of indoor environment, and process the point cloud according to the characteristics of the model required by ray tracing method. We use this method of modeling indoor environment to simulate the indoor environment of 1–5 GHz and compare with the measurement results. The results are relatively consistent.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Low-Profile Planar Wideband Antenna Array for Smart Skin
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile broadband array antenna that can be applied to smart skin. The antenna element is composed of two dipoles printed on same layer with unbalance feed structure. In order to suppress the occurrence of harmful resonances, a grounded plate capacitor structure is constructed between the radiating arms of adjacent antenna units. The profile of the antenna is less than 7mm, and the element spacing is half-wavelength of the highest frequency. The infinite array simulation results show the antenna achieves a bandwidth of 8–18 GHz for scanning up to 50° both in the E- and H-planes. Simulation predictions are validated with measured results for embedded element performances.

articleTitle: Human Posture Recognition Based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Sensor-based human posture recognition is an important research direction in the field of pattern recognition and plays an important role in many fields. The extracted features will directly affect the accuracy of pattern recognition. In this paper, the posture recognition method based on a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory neural network (Bi-LSTM) is designed and validated, the neural network is adopted in this algorithm for extracting features instead of manual extraction. Finally, the accuracy of the algorithm is verified by experimental data. The results show that the posture recognition algorithm constructed by the Bi-LSTM has a high recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: A 3.3-3.7 GHz Broadband Doherty Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a broadband Doherty power amplifier (DPA) based on GaN transistor for 5G communication. Double-points matching method and post-matching technology are used to design output matching network of main power amplifier and power combine network to overcome the narrow characteristic of conventional DPA with two quarter wavelength microstrip lines as impedance inverters. In the frequency band of 3.3-3.7 GHz, the simulation results show the saturation drain efficiency of 59-66% and the efficiency of 47– 51% at 6-dB output back-off power level. The saturation output power of the DPA is 43.9-44.6 dBm with the power gain of 10.8- 11.4 dB.

articleTitle: Branch-shaped Flexible Antenna Integrated with AMC Structure for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact dual-band antenna system with artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) reflector and operating in ISM band is proposed. The monopole antenna fed by coplanar waveguide is used as the main radiator. The circular AMC array below the antenna can greatly improve the performance of the antenna and enhance the isolation between the antenna and the human body. At 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz, the antenna gains are 3.35dBi and 7.03dBi, respectively. In addition, it can work normally in the corresponding frequency band on human tissue and when bent to a certain extent. Therefore, the antenna can be a promising candidate antenna for wireless body area network (WBAN) applications.

articleTitle: Experimental Results of Passive Radar on Moving Platform for Drone Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Passive radar on moving platform has great potential application prospect for its significant advantages. This paper describes the first drone detection experimental campaign of passive radar on moving platform based on DTMB signal. In the target detection application, the echoes of slow-moving targets will be overlapped by clutter returns which are spread in Doppler due to the receiver's movement. A signal processing scheme which contains generalized subband cancellation (GSC) algorithm and reduced-dimension space-time adaptive processing (STAP) is proposed in this paper. It can offer direct signal cancellation and space-time clutter rejection capability. The results demonstrate that the proposed signal processing scheme is an effective solution for target detection.

articleTitle: A LTCC Antenna Array in Ka- Band for Beam Scanning Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an antenna array for phased array antenna operating in Ka-band (32 - 38GHz) is presented. The proposed antenna is dipole, and the dielectric layer we used is low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC). The active VSWRs of E-plane, D-plane and H-plane are less than 2.25, 2.75 and 2.57 while scanning to 30°, without oversampling the aperture. An antenna array with 64 elements is simulated, and the simulation results show that the proposed antenna array has a scanning angle from -30° to +30° with low gain decrease and good active VSWR. The simulated maximum gain of the antenna array is about 24.6dBi at 35GHz. The proposed phased array antenna has a good application prospect in radar systems.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Duct 3D Propagation Model of Electromagnetic Wave Based on Ray Tracing Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper propose a 3D wave propagation model in the atmospheric duct with ray-tracing method. First, Taylor's second-order approximation is applied to derive the ray-tracing algorithm. The algorithm has no limitations imposed on the atmospheric environment. Second, the pathloss of each ray was calculated based on 3D ray tracing method and the pathloss formula. Finally, the results from the application of the ray-tracing model to atmospheric ducts are presented. These results will also be compared with the software Advanced Refractive Effects Prediction System 3.6, based on the numerical solution of a parabolic equation.

articleTitle: Prediction of Electromagnetic Wave Propagation Loss in Evaporation Duct Based on 3D Vector Parabolic Equation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Established the evaporation duct model by using the NPS model based on the WRF mesoscale atmospheric numerical model in the paper; Meanwhile, applied the three dimensional vector parabolic equation(3D-VPE) to predict the evaporation duct propagation loss of the maritime tans-horizon propagation experiment link, and verified with the experiment results.

articleTitle: A Design of Planar Omnidirectional Ultra-WideBand Monopole Antenna for X Band
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a kind of broadband omnidirectional mono-pole antenna based on the gradual radiation structure. The proposed antenna covers the whole X band from 8 to 12 GHz. The design and test results of the antenna are presented and discussed in this paper. In order to confirm the results, the antenna is simulated and tested. The simulated results are in good agreement with the test results. The results show that |S11| of the antenna is below -10 dB in the X band, and its gain is higher than 0 dBi in most directions.

articleTitle: Design Lumped Elements by NUSC-ADI-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the non-uniform system-combined (NUSC-) alternative-direction-implicit (ADI-) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is adopted to design the lumped elements. As the obvious advantages in non-uniform technique, the high accuracy can be achieved to solve the general FDTD method. On other hand, the lumped elements play an important role about electromagnetic fields. Hence, those methods can be combined with each other and the lumped circuits have been successfully validated by the NUSC-ADI-FDTD method.

articleTitle: Super-Wide Band and Frequency-Independent Antenna for 21cm detection in Lunar-Orbit Satellite Array
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Detection of the redshifted 21cm signal is a key to unlock the mystery of early cosmic evolution. The global 21cm signal from the cosmic dawn era can be measured with a single antenna. This can be achieved with a satellite on the lunar orbit, where the absence of ionosphere and radio frequency interference (RFI) enables high precision measurement. We describe here the design of a wide-band, frequency-independent disk-cone antenna for such a satellite, which is to be part of the lunar orbit array Hongmeng project. In this paper we will focus on science requirement, the design and fabricating method, simulation and measurement results of the disk-cone antenna. Maximum direction of the disk-cone antenna placed on the ground is between 60°-70° at 50 to 120MHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of the based-on graphene PIT metamaterials with THz wave
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a plasma-induced transparency (PIT) metamaterial based on graphene disc and parallel graphene strips, which can achieve two different modes of PIT effect under the x and y electric field polarization modes. Through theoretical analysis, it is found that when the electric field is extended by x polarization, the PIT effect of bright-dark mode coupling can be realized, which is also the main discussion direction for this paper.

articleTitle: Study on the Scattering Coefficients of the Cement Surface at 28GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The scattering properties of the cement surface play an important role in determining time and angle dispersion of the fifth-generation (5G) mobile communication in urban environment. The 28 GHz scattering distribution of the rough cement wall surface (RCWS) were acquired by the outdoor environment experiment at different incidence angles in this paper. The measurements reveal that the dlstributions of the scattering signals don't conform to the Lambert distribution used in the conventional ray tracing. The scattering coefficient reaches up to the maximum near the specular direction compared with the Lambert distribution, Moreover the other direction is less than the specular one. The scattering coefficients can be applied to simulate the signal propagation in urban environments to improve the reliability of the system.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Dual-Polarized Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An ultra-wideband dual-polarized dipole antenna with jarless radiation pattern is proposed for 2G/3G/4G/5G base stations. The antenna consists of two crossed dipoles, two sets of parasitic patches, four metal baffles, and a metal reflector. To fulfill broadband performance, clover-shaped dipoles are used and excited by parallel double transmission lines. For sake of improving the matching, two sets of directors are used and placed above the dipoles. The radiation pattern is stabilized by four metal baffles attached to the reflector. The proposed antenna implements a wide bandwidth of 98.5% (1.7-5 GHz) for return loss more than 12 dB and the isolation is greater than 20 dB. In addition, this design achieves jarless 3-dB beamwidth (HPBW) of 66 ± 7° during the operating band.

articleTitle: Transfer Matrix Method Study on Interaction of Electromagnetic Waves with Stratified Biaxial Bianisotropic Chiral Media
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The transfer matrix method is applied to analyze the interaction of electromagnetic waves with stratified biaxial bianisotropic chiral media for the s and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> linearly, as well as left-and right-handed circularly polarized incident waves. The reciprocity and differential reflectances for stratified chiral slabs are illustrated. The work in this paper may provide guidelines for formulating and solving electromagnetic propagation and scattering problems for planar structures containing biaxial bianisotropic chiral media.

articleTitle: Wide-band DOA Method with Sparse Array for Interference Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The wide-band direction of arrival (DOA) method is proposed for interference cancellation when the frequency of communication is wide, which not only inherits high-precision advantage of multiple signal classification (MUSIC), but also introduces minimum redundancy array (MRA) for avoiding DOA ambiguity. Besides, calibration of channel and Jacobi mod-el with CORDIC rotation ensure accuracy of DOA in hardware. Hence, there will be a remarkable improvement of DOA accura-cy with wide-band working frequency. Implementation in hard-ware and numerical experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance of proposed method. It is ideal for DOA estimation in anti-interference of communication.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband 1bit reconfigurable reflectarray based on tight coupling method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The paper utilizes the tightly coupled antenna design method to introduce the tightly coupled form into the design of the reconfigurable reflectarray element, and realizes an ultra-wideband 1bit reconfigurable reflectarray element. The method of the tightly coupled antenna is to connect adjacent elements together. And the adjacent reflectarray elements are connected together, which can expand the bandwidth. The form of tight coupled is achieved by the comb-strip which is used to connect the adjacent reflectarray elements. The tightly coupled reconfigurable reflectarray element is composed of two rectangular patches and two comb-shaped strips. One of the rectangular patches is divided into two patches by the groove, and a PIN diode is loaded on the groove. The opened and closed of the PIN diode can achieve two states with a phase difference of 180°. In addition, the period of the reconfigurable reflectarray element in the polarization direction is one-third of the wavelength, which is also the reason for increasing the bandwidth. The simulation results show that the bandwidth of the 1bit reconfigurable reflectarray element with a difference of 180°±20° between the two-phase states is 8GHz-12.5GHz, and the relative bandwidth is 43%. An 1bit reconfigurable reflectarray is designed with 18×12 elements, and the bandwidth of the array is 40%.

articleTitle: An Improved Empirical Conversion Function between the Peak-to-peak Fluctuation and the S4 Index
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ionospheric scintillation fading must be taken in account in the attenuation margin design of the VHF/UHF satellite systems. Most of the studies on the scintillation observations are based on the S4 indices. Therefore, a conversion function from the S4 index to the peak-to-peak fluctuation is needed for the analysis of the scintillation fading in the VHF/UHF signals to be transimitted to/from the satetillite. Based on the relationship analysis of the peak-to-peak fluctuations of UHF/L-band signals and the corresponding S4 indices observed at three low-latitude stations in China, an improved empirical conversion function from the S4 index to the peak-to-peak fluctuation is put forward. The improved conversion function has a saturation trend in the strong scintillation regime, when the S4 indices are greater than 1.0, which may be helpful for the analysis of the scintillation fading in the VHF/UHF signals.

articleTitle: The Influence of Cables in The Interference Suppression Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to study the changes of field-line coupling attenuation, in the laboratory environment, the transmission mode of the cable, the location of the cable grounding point, the grounding method and the high-frequency capacitor absorption loop at the connection end of the cable and the equipment and the different combinations of these measures The comparison of the following test results determines the method to effectively suppress the field-line coupling, quantifies the anti-interference ability, provides effective and easy anti-interference measures for engineering applications, and can provide help for the electromagnetic compatibility design of the system.

articleTitle: Research of Near-Field Electromagnetic Scattering of Rough Surface Illuminated by Electric Dipole Sources
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: When the distance between incident wave and rough surface does not meet far-field approximation condition, it is necessary to study the characteristics of electromagnetic (EM) scattering in near-field. In this paper, a one-dimensional random rough surface is generated based on the Monte Carlo method and the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is used to calculate the scattering field strength. When an electric dipole source is selected as incident wave, the simulation results of the near-field EM scattering of the one-dimensional rough surface indicate that the incident angle and the correlation length affect the horizontal characteristics of the scattered-field strength of the rough surface in near field and the root mean square (RMS) height affects the vertical characteristics, which has certain help for the study of EM scattering echo of rough surface in near field.

articleTitle: An X-band Dual-polarized Microstrip Phased Array Antenna with Wide-angle Scanning
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A design of dual-polarized phased array antenna based of microstrip patch antenna at X-band is presented in this paper, which can realize beam scanning between ±45° in both directions of vertical and horizontal polarization. The element antenna adopts two rectangular patches arranged in different layers to broaden the bandwidth, and radiates linearly dual-polarization by two different methods of feeding. According to the requirement of wide-angle scanning, the element spacing is small which results in a strong coupling among element antennas and loss in radiant efficiency. For majorization, electric walls and a 180° phase shift are introduced to the array design.

articleTitle: Broadband Measurement of Dielectric Properties for Microwave Materials
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the principle of single-frequency measurement by the resonance method, this paper proposes to achieve a broadband measurement of 0.7-10 GHz through a cavity multi-mode method. The three modes of TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</inf>, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">030</inf>and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">090</inf> are selected to measure the permittivity and loss tangent of the planar media sample located in the center of the cylindrical cavity. According to simulation calculation, the proposed work can realize that the maximum relative error of permittivity does not exceed 1.7%.

articleTitle: Influence of the Inhomogeneous Ionosphere on the Radio Wave Propagation Path
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To analyze the effect of an ionospheric model with a horizontal gradient on the propagation path of radio waves, on the basis of ignoring the influence of the geomagnetic field and collision, this paper selects the international reference ionosphere as the background ionospheric model, uses the Runge-Kutta method to solve the Haselgrove equations, and finally obtains a three-dimensional ray-tracing model of shortwave propagation in the ionosphere. The propagation trajectories of radio waves through the homogeneous and inhomogeneous ionosphere based on different emission elevation angles, radio wave frequencies, and geographic latitudes are simulated and analyzed. According to the results, the existence of the horizontal gradient will cause the radio wave propagation trajectory to deviate.

articleTitle: A Non-diffraction Microstrip Antenna Array for Wireless Power Transfer Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband microstrip antenna array generating the non-diffraction beam is proposed. The whole design is based on the classical transmission line theory and the increasingly popular non-diffractive theory. The overall method is to design the patch array and the feed network with superior performances separately, and then combine them to obtain the final ideal properties. Simulation and measurement results show that the finally obtained microstrip antenna array integrates the great performances of the patch array and the feed network, which not only successfully realizes the non-diffractive focusing beam with a focusing distance of about 1.18m, but also gets a great gain of 17.02dB and a bandwidth of 13.91% (5.54-6.34GHz) with a return loss of -17.01dB at 5.8GHz. This design is different from the common non-diffractive metasurface, and it provides a more practical scheme for the application of non-diffractive theory from the practical point of view.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual Circularly-Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband dual circularly-polarized antenna is present by employing a directional printed cross dipole to realize broadband. A dual-ring 3dB hybrid is connected to the feed points on dipole by using two coaxial cables. The 3dB hybrid produces -90° or +90° phase difference between the X-polarized dipole and Y -polarized dipole, then the left circular polarization and the right circular polarization are achieved in the bandwidth of 50%. The proposed antenna is fabricated, the test results match well with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Measurement-Based Doppler Analysis in Viaduct Scenarios for Railway
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The channels of railway communication system are mostly characterized by nonstationary time-selective fading process caused by its high mobility. In this paper, the Doppler statistics of wireless channels, which shows the time-selective fading effect in railway viaduct scenarios, are characterized based on measurements conducted along the passenger dedicated line. Multi-tone channel sounding signal with the bandwidth of 20 MHz is employed as the excitation signal that is transmitted from the base station along the railway track. Furthermore, based on the field measured data, time-varying power delay profile and Doppler power spectral density (PSD) are estimated by the impulse responses from the measured channel. Time-varying Doppler shift and Doppler PSD are analyzed. Finally, the observed propagation mechanisms of the different regions of Doppler PSD are explained.

articleTitle: Design of an Optically Transparent Ultra-wideband Electromagnetic Absorber
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an ultra-wideband optically transparent electromagnetic absorber (EMA) with a fractional bandwidth of 113.09%. The absorber consists of a multi-layered transparent structure with a periodic indium-tin-oxide (ITO) patch array attached to a polyethylene terephthalate (PET) film layer. The absorber can reach -10dB attenuation rate in the range of 8.8-31.7 GHz for vertical incident electromagnetic waves under transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarization,

articleTitle: A Planar Circular Polarization Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array Based on Nonuniform Layout and Element Random Rotation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a Planar wide-angle scanning array is designed with low sidelobe level (SLL) by the nonuniform layout and the random rotation of elements. Initially, a microstrip-monopole antenna unit is designed and the wide beam and circular polarization are obtained. Besides that, the positions and rotation angle of array element are optimized to realize low SLL and improve the axis ratio (AR) performance. The array is fabricated and measured. The experimental results indicate that the designed phased array support a scan up to ±56° in both orthogonal planes with the gain fluctuation of 4.3 dB, which are identical to the simulation results.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Study on the Carrier Frequency Offset Measurement in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation method are widely used, carrier frequency offset (CFO) estimation has become one of the most important issues in wireless communication systems. To find out the factors on this figure of merit, we performed some measurements in different testing scenarios, including over-the-air (OTA) testing performed in reverberation chamber (RC) and shielding chamber (SC) and conduction measurement. It is interesting to find that power attenuation and multipath fading have no influence on CFO and the value of CFO depends on the temperature of device.

articleTitle: Design of a Beam Steering Microwave Lens Based on Transformation Optics
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As a commonly used receiving antenna, waveguide has the main disadvantages of small receiving area and low energy convergence. In this paper, a novel microwave lens based on the concept of transformation for beam steering is studied. Equipped with such a lens, the waveguide can have a larger receiving area and better energy convergence. The electric-field distributions of the microwave lens are simulated by three-dimensional simulation software HFSS. The simulations of incident waves at different angles further proves the convergence performance of the lens. The implementation of the lens illustrate the practicality of transformation optics to achieve a new class of microwave devices and it possesses potential applications in reception systems.

articleTitle: Wide-band Circularly Polarized Antenna Array for OAM Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new cross symmetrical dipole was designed and applied in a 2*2 array to generate the required vortex electromagnetic wave within the operating frequency. The cross symmetrical dipole is composed of crossed dipoles and a resonant ring with cutting corners and opening. Details of design, simulated results of this new cross symmetrical dipole and the 2*2 array are presented and discussed. The simulation results show that both the unit and the array have confirmed the validity of the design.

articleTitle: Research on Similarity Evaluation Method of Complex Electromagnetic Environment Based on Similarity Theory
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The assessment of the similarity of radar complex electromagnetic environment currently has more qualitative assessment and the assessment index is difficult to quantify, etc. To address these problems, an assessment method based on the similarity principle is proposed in this paper. The radar complex electromagnetic environment is analyzed in the time domain, frequency domain, modulation domain, power domain, and polarization domain to derive similarity characteristic parameters, innovate the assessment index, and improve the calculation method of similarity factor.

articleTitle: Simulation and application of electromagnetic wave propagation logging tool in microwave band based on CST
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: There is significant difference between the dielectric parameter of formation water and hydrocarbon. By measuring the dielectric constants of rocks and fluids with the electromagnetic wave propagation logging technology in the microwave band, the oil and water layers can be effectively distinguished; Based on the three-dimensional electromagnetic field simulation software (CST), this paper establishes the simulation model of microwave electromagnetic wave propagation logging tool probe, simulates and calculates the horizontal and vertical formation's conversion chart of microwave electromagnetic wave propagation logging tool, and develops the application of microwave electromagnetic wave propagation logging tool in many oil fields.

articleTitle: A New Metal Crossed Dipole Antenna for the EISCAT_3D Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The EISCAT _3D radar is the next generation incoherent scatter radar system which will provide 3D monitoring of the atmosphere and ionosphere. This paper focuses on the design and test results of the antenna element for the EISCAT _3D system. The antenna element adopts a metal cross-shape antenna element with four knife-shaped array arms to reduce snowfall accumulation. A cross-shape parasitic sheet is add to the top of the element to decrease the active reflection loss of the antenna in the array. The simulated results showed that the active reflection loss for all scan angles in the transmitting band is <-12.1dB, and the passive return loss a single antenna are better than -17.5 dB in whole 218-248MHz.

articleTitle: Magnetic shock wave excited by dissymmetric dipole of pulse current excitation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new conception “magnetic shock wave” has been cited in this paper. Physical model of the theory calculation has been established based on the experiment equipment. The conception and production mechanism of the magnetic shock wave has been studied. The propagation characteristic, velocity and attenuation ratio of the magnetic shock wave has been analyzed and calculated. The calculation results show that the magnetic shock wave is a kind of “near filed” excited around of excitation equipment. It should still satisfy the Maxwell equation, and it can still be explained and understood using the classical macroscopic electrodynamics theory. The field is also a kind of broad band instantaneous pulse because the excitation current is a kind of instantaneous pulse. It has very significant dispersion and distortion. The observation result of the different receiving sensor is different in the different distance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Shielding Effectiveness of Multi-layer Steel Cages under High-Altitude Nuclear Explosion
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In view of the strong electromagnetic pulse environment of high-altitude nuclear explosions, the shielding effective-ness of different structural steel cage in protection engineering is studied, which provides an effective reference for the normal operation of electronic equipment. The MoM method is used to perform coupling calculations on eight different structures of steel cages. The influence of two parameters that the number of layers and the size of the square holes on the shielding effectiveness is analyzed. And a preliminary assessment was conducted from the amount of steel bars about the two factors. The results show that increasing the number of layers of the steel cage can more effectively prevent the coupling of high-altitude nuclear explosive electromagnetic pulses into the steel cage than reducing the size of the metal mesh, but it led to more steel consumption.

articleTitle: Clutter Simulation of Dynamic Sea Surface under Two Motion Modes of Radar Seeker
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the traditional EM scattering model of the sea surface, sea clutter with different parameters are usually calculated under the static condition of the radar platform. However, most radars move in different motion states, e.g., radar seeker is equipmented in a moving missile-borne platform. This paper introduces in detail the model and process of the integration of moving radar seeker and sea surface under the side-looking radar and forward-looking radar seeker. The vector superposition of the results of the physical optics method (PO) on facets is used to calculate the EM scattering under the condition of seeker beam irradiation. Sea clutter under different marine conditions and radar platform parameters are simulated and analyzed. It is pointed out that the amplitude of the side-looking motion radar platform increases significantly when the wind speed increases. When the platform velocity increases, it has little effect on sea clutter time series. For the forward-looking motion radar platform, the frequency increases significantly with the increase of wind speed or the increase of platform velocity.

articleTitle: Group-Based Antenna Selection for Massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In massive MIMO antenna systems, system complexity and hardware cost can be reduced by applying appropriate antenna selection techniques. However, the strong correlations between large-scale antenna elements will affect the performance of antenna selection. In this paper, a group-based antenna selection algorithm is proposed. First, all the antennas are dividing into different groups, the antennas within the group have strong correlation. Second, the antennas that contribute the most to the channel capacity are selected from each group as the final selection results. The simulation results show that the channel capacity of applying the proposed algorithm is very close to that of applying the optimal antenna selection algorithm, and the performance is better than the algorithms in other references. Besides, the complexity of the proposed algorithm is much lower than that of the algorithms in other references.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Assisted Surrogate Model for Refractivity Structure Constant against Altitude
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An accurate surrogate model for the refractivity structure constant against altitude is presented. The surrogate model is based on Gaussian process regression (GPR) and makes it possible to accurately predict the values of refractivity structure constant at different altitudes even when the measurement data is scarce. A measurement dataset containing 46 measurement data is divided into a training dataset and a test dataset with different proportions to verify the performance of the proposed method. Results show that when the ratio of training data to test data is 1:1, the predictive root mean squared error (RMSE) of GPR is 0.055. In the worst case, i.e., the ratio of training data to test data is 1:5, the predictive RMSE is 0.233. These fully verify the practicability of our proposed method.

articleTitle: 3D-GSPR: An Effective Algorithm for 3D Phase Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Recently, phase retrieval has received much attention in optical imaging. In this paper, we propose an effective algorithm called the 3-dimensional (3D) greedy sparse phase retrieval (3D-GSPR) for solving the 3D phase retrieval problem. Our algorithm extends the conventional GESPAR algorithm by using techniques like 3D discrete Fourier transform over ten-sors. Numerical experiments show that the proposed algorithm is effective for 3D phase retrieval.

articleTitle: 3-D Printed Circularly Polarized Antenna Array With Stepped Parallel Groove Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a 3-D printed circularly polarized (CP) antenna array is proposed. It is with a 1 ×4 configuration and consists of four identical open-ended waveguide elements and a two-stage four-way power divider. In order to realize CP radiation, a novel stepped parallel groove structure is designed for each array element. It is placed inside the waveguide and operates as a linear to circular polarizer. Through our study, it is found that the proposed antenna array can achieve a wide impedance bandwidth of 19% (9.1-11 GHz), a wide 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth(ARBW) of 14% (9.1-10.6 GHz) and a peak gain of 10.2 dBic. The proposed antenna array has advantages of simple structure, light weight and easy fabrication. It is a promising candidate for various CP array applications.

articleTitle: A wideband miniaturized dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A wideband miniaturized directional dipole antenna is proposed in this paper. A U-shaped back cavity is utilized to realize lower resonant frequency without increasing the length of the antenna. In addition, a parasitical element is adoped above the dipole arms, the bandwidth of the antenna is enhanced. The design exhibits a physical size of 260mm×198mm×187mm, equivalent to a compact electrical size of 0.2A×0.152A.×0.143A. at 0.23GHz. Simulation results indicates that the VSWR is lower than 2.0 in the frequency range of 0.23GHz~0.97GHz, the impedance bandwidth reaches 123%.

articleTitle: Auto-Encoder Based Inversion for Inhomogeneous Evaporation Ducts from Sea Clutter
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Inverting the modified refractivity profile of the evaporation duct from radar sea clutter has prominently pragmatic utility and widespread industry prospects. Notwithstanding, the modified refractive index (M) profile structure of the evaporation duct will exhibit the inhomogeneous characteristics in the range direction as the multifarious meteorological conditions over the sea, which will seriously affect the tangible detection performance of radar. Numerous attempts have been made to ameliorate the accuracy of the inverted parameters of evaporation duct profiles by utilizing various intelligent models. Nevertheless, modeling of the range direction inhomogeneous evaporation duct, conventional modeling approach of extracting the dimensional features of the high dimension M profile is not befitting the feature extraction where the range direction is persisting nonlinear relation. To tackle this issue, we propose a novel model, namely one-dimension residual convolutional autoencoder, to extract features from inhomogeneous evaporation ducts and to overcome the dimension issue inherent in modeling the range direction parameters of evaporation duct profiles. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed approach is more befitting and efficacious for evaluating the range direction dependent inhomogeneous evaporation duct M profile.

articleTitle: LC-based Terahertz Reconfigurable Reflectarray with Offset Feed
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a 30×30 off-fed LC-based terahertz reconfigurable reflectarray at 0.35 THz is presented. A double dipole LC phase shifter with phase shift of greater than 355° in the range of 346.525-352.475GHz is used as the unit cell of the reflectarray. The 2-bit LC-based reflectarray is simulated. The reflectarray realizes wide beam scanning over 5-110° and remains good radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Two-Port Antenna Pair Decoupling by Modal Control for 5G Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband two-port antenna pair is designed for the fifth generation (5G) application. The -6 dB impedance matching bandwidth of the antenna pair can cover 3.1-5.28 GHz and the isolation is better than 10 dB. Compared to the traditional decoupling method of characteristic mode, we excite a pair of decoupling modes at each port simultaneously. An eight-element multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna composed of four two-port antenna pairs is simulated, fabricated, and measured. The proposed antenna pair is a good candidate for the 5G Application.

articleTitle: A Tri-band Microstrip Antenna with Triple Polarization Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A low-profile tri-band stacked patch antenna with omni-directional liner polarization (LP) and directional circular polarization (CP) characteristics is proposed in this paper. Two layers of patches are used to generate triple resonances. The top patch is fed by a single coaxial probe and the bottom patch is excited through electromagnetic coupling. Symmetrical corner truncations are used to achieve CP. Conductive vias are employed to realize omni-directional LP at the desirable operating band. A prototype antenna is designed and fabricated, which operates at the frequency bands centered at 1.615 and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> GHz, respectively, for supporting two satellite communication services at one time and providing dual-band CP characteristics. Furthermore, omni-directional vertical LP characteristic in S-band is also realized for data link between unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The occupied volume of the proposed antenna is 70mm×70mm× 5.4mm. When working at the CP modes, its VSWR is less than 2 and the axial ratio (AR) is less than 3 dB. While operating at the LP mode, its VSWR is less than 2.5 and the variation for omni-directional radiation pattern in the horizontal plane is less than 2 dB. The proposed antenna is useful in highly integrated airborne platforms.

articleTitle: A Lower Atmospheric Duct Comprehensive Index and AIS Signal Propagation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The lower atmospheric duct is an important propagation environment for the over-the-horizon propagation of radio waves. Quantifying the spatial distribution and strength of the lower atmospheric duct is helpful to fully understand its propagation characteristics and improve the efficiency of signal propagation evaluation in a duct environment. Based on the predicted data of regional atmospheric duct, a new method for intuitive and efficient environmental assessment of the atmospheric duct is proposed in this paper. A duct comprehensive index is used to quantify the lower atmospheric duct conditions, and compared with the AIS (Automatic identification system) signal received on shore to verify the effectiveness of the method. The results show that the duct comprehensive index has good consistency with the maximum receiving distance of AIS signals. The environmental assessment method of the lower atmospheric duct is feasible.

articleTitle: Application of Ulaby Model in Simulation of Altimeter Fuze
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the application mechanism of scattering information of background of surface features in the design process of altimeter fuze is not clear, a simulation method of altimeter fuze based on Ulaby model is proposed. This method is based on the Ulaby model to model the target characteristics of background of surface features. The target characteristics information is used as the input information of fuze detection in the missile target encounter process, adopting the digital signal processing method. The response characteristic model of fuze target detection is established, and the response simulation of fuze detection to the time-varying scattering characteristics of background of surface features in the process of missile target encounter is carried out, and the response characteristics of echo and IF signal processing are clearly reproduced. The experimental results show that Ulaby model can be used to distinguish different background of surface features types. The target type information is added as another dimensional fuze detection information, and the detection accuracy is further improved by combining the height information.

articleTitle: A New Formula for Computing Minimum Trapped Frequency of Evaporation Duct
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the past, the minimum trapped frequency formula of evaporation duct is obtained under the assumption of linear attenuation, while the profile of actual evaporation duct is linear-logarithmic, which leads to the calculation error of the formula. Based on the integral minimum trapped frequency formula, the calculation results under different stability conditions considering the logarithmic evaporation duct profile are simulated and analyzed. And the minimum trapped frequencies of different evaporation duct heights under neutral conditions are obtained. Then, a new formula for computing minimum trapped frequency of evaporation duct is obtained by using the least square method. Considering the logarithmic modified refractive index profile, the new formula significantly reduces the prediction error of minimum trapped frequency compared with the integral calculation res ult.

articleTitle: Correction of Time Domain Measurement Error of Reflection Coefficient of Dielectric Plate
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the free space time domain measurement of die-lectric plate material reflection coefficient, a 16-element error model is introduced to correct the diffraction and scattering prob-lems caused by the finite size of dielectric plate. Firstly, the testing principle of time domain reflection measurement system is intro-duced, and the edge effect error caused by the limited size of die-lectric plate is analyzed. Then the calculation formula and correction principle of the 16-element error control model are given, and the measurement amplitude of the reflection coefficient of the single-layer dielectric plate is corrected, and the analytical solution is compared, and the error is less than 5%. The results show that the 16-element error model can effectively control the exper-imental errors in free space time domain measurement.

articleTitle: The role of charged dust particles on conductivity in polar mesosphere summer echoes regions
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The effects of electron bite-outs caused by charged dust particles on the effective collision frequencies, Parallel, and Pederson conductivities are studied by introducing the collision frequency of electrons and charged dust particles. It is found that considering the collision frequency of electrons and charged dust particles alters the conductivity, particularly in the electron bite- out regions.

articleTitle: Multiband metamaterial absorber based on fractal nesting and Jerusalem cross square ring combination
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Two novel multiband metamaterial absorbers are proposed in this paper. The unit cell of the absorber consists of a metal patch with nested or combined patterns on the upper and lower layers and a metal backplane. Each layer is separated by a medium. The main absorption peaks of the fractal nested structure are at 18.91 GHz, 20.06 GHz, 26.57 GHz and 30.10 GHz. The main absorption peaks of the Jerusalem cross and square ring combination structure are at 11.50 GHz, 14.12 GHz, 18.56 GHz, 29.50 GHz and 31.60 GHz. It is found that the design of nesting and combining metal pattern is beneficial to realize multiband absorbing.

articleTitle: Focusing effect of inhomogeneous plasma on electromagnetic wave
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the propagation process of electromagnetic wave in plasma with low internal density and high outer layer density is simulated by CST software. The energy distribution of electromagnetic wave is measured by field monitor and it is found that the distribution of plasma can focus electromagnetic wave. With the help of Drude model, this phenomenon is explained. By changing different parameters such as microwave frequency and the form of incident electromagnetic wave (plane wave and wave guide), the properties of focusing effect are investigated. The research of this thesis has reference value for the applications of plasma and electromagnetic wave interaction.

articleTitle: A Link Delay Monitoring System for VLBI
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper designs a monitoring system for measuring absolute link delay of antennas in real time by comb spectrum generator and optical devices. It eliminates the difficulty of existing methods that all devices of the whole link should be removed from antennas and be measured in sections. The system meets the needs of delay sensitive applications e.g. very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), pulsar timing, UT1 measurement, etc. Through testing, the measurement accuracy of this system is 40ps level at 10s integration.

articleTitle: A Relay TT&C Link for Re-entry Spacecraft in Black-out Zone Based on Large LEO Constellation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The interrupt in tracking telemetry & command (TT&C) is very dangerous for re-entry spacecraft, especially manned spacecraft in black-out zone. A relay TT&C link based on TT&C system on large LEO (Low Earth Orbit) constellation is proposed in this paper to resolve the problem. The Unified (carrier system) S band (USB) is widely used in spacecraft engineering applications. Therefore, the TT&C payloads on LEO satellites can serve as relay stations to provide TT&C links between spacecraft and ground stations. Compared with the GEO (Geostationary orbit) satellite and orbit cabin relay link, the proposed link has a small time delay, more target choice and better link budget. Meanwhile, it will be a smaller cost solution for the lots of existing manned spacecraft based on the Soon-To-be-Built large LEO constellation.

articleTitle: Calibration Method and System of Isotropic Electric-field Probe
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A calibration method and system of isotropic electric field (E-field) probe is presented in this paper. The proposed calibration method is substitution method, using a transfer standard for E-field probe calibration. The calibration system is composed of GTEM cell or microwave chamber, decided by the calibration frequency. The uncertainties of calibration are determined by all the accuracy of the calibration devices. The calibration method and system is applied to the calibration of 100 kHz~60GHz E-field probe.

articleTitle: Radio Wave Propagation Prediction in Urban Based on Parabolic Equation Methods
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper predicts the characteristics of radio wave propagation in urban environment by four types of parabolic equation (PE) methods, including 1-way/2-way two-dimensional PE(1W-2DPE/2W-2DPE) and 1-way/2-way three-dimensional PE(1W-3DPE/2W-3DPE). An open street scenario was modeled and simulated. The calculation values of path loss in line of sight (LOS) link generally align with the measured value, which shows the methods are feasible. As to the results of simulation, compared and discussed the advantages and disadvantages of the four models, and proposed the guidance for the application scenario of the four PE methods.

articleTitle: Ocean Wave Inversion from Airborne SAR Data by Doppler Information
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Due to the limitation of spatial resolution, spaceborne SAR data, which is usually used for surface current inversion, is difficult to observe ocean waves by the Doppler information. In February 2021, three L-band airborne SAR experiments were carried out in the South China Sea. The high-resolution SAR data obtained from the experiment provides a valuable opportunity for ocean wave inversion using the Doppler information and has been successfully retrieved. The comparison between retrieved sea waves and the buoy measurements shows that the two results are in agreement with each other.

articleTitle: Designing and Testing of Energy Selective Surface Based on PIN Diode
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an energy selective surface (ESS) based on PIN diode is designed and manufactured, and performed irradiation tests under the environment of ultra-wideband electromagnetic pulse (UWB-EMP). The test results show that the ESS designed in this paper has good protective effect against UWB-EMP. When the space field is 2100 V/m, the shielding efficiency can reach 15 dB. Meanwhile it is concluded that the response time of PIN diode affects the shielding efficiency. The amount of variation in shielding efficiency is determined by the diodes array. The results provide reference for the application of ESS in electromagnetic protection.

articleTitle: A Simplified Method for Ablative Plasma Effect on Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The method of reducing ablative plasma to dusty plasma is detailed. The results are shown in the form of antenna patterns, which show that increase in radius and density and decrease in charging frequency would intensify the attenuation of electromagnetic field. The electric field intensity was obtained through ray-tracing method with ray-based coordinate system to simplify the calculation, which is carried out under different radius, densities and charging frequencies of dust grains. The above parameters are used to acquire attenuation coefficient for further counting of electromagnetic field intensity propagating through dusty plasma. To investigate the effect of different input frequency, X-band and C-band are tested under conditions of RAM C-II and RAM C-III.

articleTitle: A Wideband ±45° Dual-polarized Crisscross-Shaped Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A Wideband ±45° Dual-polarized Crisscross-Shaped antenna is proposed for 690–960 MHz base station applications. A J-shaped parasitic branch and a rectangle parasitic branch connect to the radiator, so the bandwidth of the antenna is improved. The simulated and measured results show the proposed antenna exhibits a bandwidth covering the entire LTE700/GSM850/GSM900 band (690–960 MHz), high isolation, and stable patterns.

articleTitle: Vivaldi Antenna with Improved Double-Slot for Enhancing Low-Frequency Performance
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband Vivaldi antenna based on aT-junction feeding and improved double-slot is proposed. The top and bottom layers of the antenna are connected by a phase inverter to reduce cross-polarization. Besides, the method of loading rectangular linear gradient slots can optimize the impedance characteristics, improve the distribution of surface current, and extend the low-end frequency limitation from 2 to 0.7 GHz. The simulated results of the modified Vivaldi antenna exhibits a gain of 7.11-12.21 dBi over the frequency band of 0.8-6 GHz, particularly the gain is greater than 10 dBi in the 1.7-6 GHz band.

articleTitle: Study on Roll-Off Characteristics at Upper Cutoff Frequency of SSPP Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the roll-off characteristic at the upper cutoff frequency of spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) transmission lines with linear tapered transitions is studied. The SSPP structure with different number of units are investigated using a cascaded equivalent circuit model. It is found that the roll-off rate reaches its maximum value at a specified number of units. The variation of the roll-off rate with different geometric parameters is also discussed.

articleTitle: Study on 340 GHz Wave Scintillation Characteristics Based on Experimental Data
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: the near ground scintillation characteristic at the frequency of 340 GHz is analyzed based on the experimental data. The experiment is carried in the outdoor instead of the lab to study the real atmospheric influence on the propagation of 340 GHz wave. Results show The near ground scintillation is relatively weak in this frequency. And the probability density function of the scintillation amplitude conforms to Gaussian distribution. The correlation between meteorological parameters and scintillation index S4 in June is studied. It is concluded that water vapour density is the main factor that affect the scintillation at 340 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a compact microstrip Filter-Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact microstrip filter-antenna with a center frequency of 5.0GHz and impedance bandwidth of 260MHz is designed. It consists of four cross-coupled half-wave open-loop resonators, a segment of coupled-line and a T-shaped microstrip antenna. T-shaped antenna acts as both radiator and last resonator of the filter. The maximum gain of the filter-antenna is 1.48dB. The design structure is simple and the overall size of the integrated design of the filter and antenna is effectively reduced. Moreover, the filter antenna has good out-of-band suppression and radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: Tianlai Interferometer Array for Dark Energy Radio Detecting and Transient Objects Survey
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Tianlai project is a dedicated experiment to test key techniques for 21 cm Intensity Mapping of dark energy radio detection over the redshift range z<3. It is comprised of two pathfinder arrays: the cylinder array with three 15m-wide cylindrical antennas oriented in the north-south direction, and the dish array with 16 dishes of 6m aperture. These arrays observe large area of sky by drift scan. Recently fast radio burst (FRB) backends with digital beam forming capability are installed, which could form 16 beams for the dish array and 96 beams for the cylinder array with the time resolution better than 0.2 millisecond. The original correlation backend and the FRB backend will work simultaneously, so that the intensity mapping experiment could be conducted along with FRB search at the same time.

articleTitle: In-House Made Inverted Microstrip Line Phase Shifter Based on Nematic Liquid Crystal
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Nematic liquid crystals are anisotropic dielectrics whose properties could be controlled by surface anchoring, exter-nal electric or magnetic fields. A typical design method of tunable inverted microstrip line phase shifter based on liquid crystal for microwave application is investigated. Two phase shifter designs based on the proposed method were introduced with the center operation frequency of 10 GHz and 20 GHz respectively. The prototype design operating at 20GHz is manufactured. The dielectric anisotropy of the liquid crystal used for the prototype is 0.45. A differential phase shift of 27.2° was achieved at 20 GHz with the physical length of 20 mm, connected to two coplanar waveguide ports of 50 ohms through vias, and under an external bias of 7 V.

articleTitle: Study on the Transmission and Scattering Characteristics of Blue-green Lasers Through the Atmosphere-ocean Interface
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Sea surface sometimes become dynamic, non-uniform, anisotropic and random. In this paper, a dynamic sea surface is established based on the Monte Carlo method and with the help of JNOSWAP sea spectrum simulation, and the influence of the wind speed and wind zone of the blue-green laser passing the sea surface on the backscattering coefficient and transmission coefficient is discussed. The results show that the backscattering coefficient of the sea surface at a large incident angle is greater than that of a small incident angle. This is due to the occlusion effect of the sea surface; When the blue-green laser passes through the sea, the maximum transmission coefficient appears at the position of the refraction angle. As the wind speed and wind area increase, the transmission coefficient decreases. This work provides support for the research on key technologies and basic theories of cross-medium target laser detection by gas-sea blue-green lasers and wireless optical communication.

articleTitle: Microwave cavity resonance spectrum used for plasma diagnostics in AC glow discharge plasma
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, microwave diagnostic was applied to AC glow discharge plasma. The electron density and the collision frequency changing with the input power in the fluorescent lamp have been measured by microwave cavity resonance spectrum (MCRS) which is proven to be useful for low density plasma diagnostic. By using the global model, electron density and collision frequency can be calculated by the variation of spectrum map. The resonant mode is altered by changing the position of the microwave antenna. The spectrum is measured by spectrum analyzer (DSA-815), and the frequency ranges from 9 kHz to 1.5 GHz. Finally, the experimental results are compared with the theoretical results.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Dual-circularly Polarized GPS Antenna with Excellent Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a compact dual-band dual-circularly Global Positioning System (GPS) antenna consisting of multilayer microstrip patches with 4 arms and 4 feeding probes is presented. In order to simultaneously generate LHCP and RHCP, two input ports with a phase shift of 90° are employed for the feeding probes. Optimized by using a specially designed feeding cable, the radiation pattern shows that the proposed antenna possesses an excellent quality circularly polarized (CP) radiation pattern covering 1510–1580 MHz and 1660–1680 MHz bands with an axial ratio less than 8 dB. The proposed antenna has a wide angle CP radiation of 120° with low profile and a miniaturized structure of 0.194λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ×0.194λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ×0.130λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>at 1.575 GHz, which makes it be of excellent practicability for GPS applications.

articleTitle: Design of the Broadband low-scattering metasurface based on pixelation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The method of pixelizing and arranging pixels on metasurface unit are proposed to optimize the design of broadband low-scattering metasurface. The random code is read into Matlab first. Then the corresponding metasurface structure is modelled and simulated to obtain the reflection phase of each metasurface through the API between Matlab and HFSS. Finally, all phases are subtracted in pairs to obtain the phase-difference of any two units. If two units have phase difference range of (180° ± 37°) at the widest continuous frequency band, the two metasurfaces composed of the two units will have the wider 10dB reduction bandwidth than any other simulated unit. The method in this paper can be applied to study of unit patterns that are difficult to express mathematically, and also can be used in creating the data-set for deep-learning.

articleTitle: SAR Moving Target Detection with Low Range Sampling Based on Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Under the traditional Nyquist sampling theorem, high-resolution large-scene synthetic aperture radar imaging brings a heavy burden to A/D conversion and data storage and transmission systems. Compressed sensing radar is a new technique which combines with the traditional radar via compressed sensing; its mission is target detection and imaging which over lap with the traditional radar system. In compressed sensing, a low-dimensional, non-adaptive, linear projection is used to acquire an efficient representation of a compressible signal directly using just a few measurements, so that it can reduce the requirements of hardware. This paper introduces the basic theory of synthetic aperture radar moving target detection, analyzes the moving target detection method based on compressed sensing, and makes simulation verification.

articleTitle: A pattem-reconfigurable FP antenna using PIN diodes
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: By loading a reconfigurable partially reflective surface (PRS), switching radiation pattern is achieved for an Fabry-Perot antenna consists of a patch antenna. The PRS is formed by a curved metal structure element on a dielectric substrate and controllable PIN diodes are carefully designed to make the transmission phase reconfigurable. Through the design several states with different beam width among 20.6° to 111.5° are realized while the high gain property of FP antenna is guaranteed. Compared with the original patch antenna, a minimum 10.85dBi gain increase is obtained.

articleTitle: Coseimic Ionospheric Disturbance Stastic Analysis of 2015 Nepal Earthquake
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Nepal M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>7.8 earthquake occurred on April 25, 2015. The epicenter was located at 28.1 ° N, 84.7 ° E and focal depth is fifteen kilometers. The secondary pressure wave generated by earthquake will be coupled with the atmosphere, which will affect the plasma in the ionosphere and change the electron concentration of the total electron content (TEC). Surface acoustic wave, Rayleigh wave surface and gravity wave excited by vertical coseismic crustal movement in large earthquakes will produce coseismic ionospheric disturbance (CID).

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband CPW-to-Stripline Transition Based on a Multilayered PCB Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
