abstract: An ultra-wideband CPW-to-stripline transition is proposed in this paper. The entire transition structure is based on a multilayered PCB structure using thin dielectric substrates. The electromagnetic coupling and matching designed between CPW and stripline is completed by resin plating on multilayer dielectric plate. At the same time, a back-to-back structure of the CPW-to-strip line transition is simulated and optimized in the full-wave commercial electromagnetic simulation software. A prototype of the back-to-back transition structure was fabricated and measured, and the experimental results indicate that the VSWR is less than 1.25, the insertion loss is less than -0.3 dB in the entire frequency band within 2-18GHz. Its good performance together with simple structure and usage of thin dielectric substrates making it a good candidate in feeding the vivaldi antenna.

articleTitle: A Waveguide-fed One-dimensional Bulleye Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a waveguide-fed one-dimensional bull-eye antenna, which innovatively combines a waveguide slot array antenna with a bull-eye antenna. The antenna array uses a simple bulleye structure and the feeding uses the waveguide slot antenna with a large power capacity. The simulation results show that the antenna has a high gain of 23dBi and a power capacity of 9MW at 1.9GHz. The antenna gain increases with the increase of the number of grooves of the bulleye antenna or the number of slots in the waveguide. The antenna has the features of high gain, low loss, high power capacity, low cost and easy conformation.

articleTitle: Design and Preliminary Test results of a L-band Phased Array Feed for QTT
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Phased array feeds (P AFs), which placed near the focus of a reflector, provide continuous multiple beams with good performance. Relative to traditional horn feeds, P AFs for radio telescopes have a larger and denser field of view and a higher sky survey speed. This paper presents the composition and preliminary test results of a P AF system for QTT (Qi Tai Telescope), which will be next world-class fully steerable radio telescope.

articleTitle: Design of Balun Structure for Calibration Loop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As a key component of a calibration system, the performances of a calibration loop antenna determines the accuracy of the measurement system. If the degree of imbalance is introduced between an antenna and a feeding cable, some current will flow on the outer surface of the feeding cable, which is called common mode current. The common mode current will change the radiation performance of the calibration loop antenna, resulting in uncertain errors in the calibration of the system gain and efficiency. To solve this problem, the design of three different types of balun structures for calibration loop antennas were analyzed in this paper. Finally, the measured results show that the balun structures have effectively suppressed the common mode current on the calibration loop antenna.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of Spitze angle at Qingdao
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the process of using O-mode of high-power radio transmitter to heat the ionosphere, the heating effect strongly depends on the incident angle of the pump wave. The incident wave with different inclination angles will lead to different variations of ionosphere. In this study, the O-mode heating with different inclination angles in Qingdao were simulated using two-dimensional (2-D) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) based on the magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) theory. Qingdao is located in typical mid-latitude regions. The simulation was used to investigate the efficiency of the O-mode to Z-mode conversion in the ionosphere. The results presented the Spitze angle of Qingdao is 27°, which is consistent with the theoretical calculation. This work will provide a reference for ionospheric heating by oblique incidence in the middle and low latitude regions.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Polarization Reconfigurable Slot Antenna Based on Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An ultra-wideband polarization reconfigurable slot antenna based on liquid metal (LM) is proposed. The Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) structure with microchannels are loaded on the upper and lower sides of the Rogers5880, to provide conditions for polarization reconfiguration. The left-hand circular polarization (LHCP), right-hand circular polarization (RHCP), and linear polarization (LP) are achieved by injecting LM into microchannels in different directions. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna achieves - 10dB impedance bandwidth of 81.5% (2.29-5.44GHz) in LP state, -10dB impedance bandwidth of 48.3% (2.78-4.55GHz) and 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 51.1% (2.61-4.40GHz) in CP state.

articleTitle: Recognition of digital phase modulation signal in wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Digital modulation signal is an important field of wireless communication. With the continuous development of wireless communication technology, the recognition technology of digital signal is also advancing. In this paper, the recognition technology of digital phase-modulation signal is studied, and the received MPSK signal is converted into an isopotential horoscope through data processing. Based on deep learning theory, three deep learning models such as ResNet, VGG16 and Mobilenet are selected to carry out feature extraction and recognition of the isopotential constellation of MPSK signal, and the accuracy of recognition is compared.

articleTitle: A Low-RCS Fabry-Perot Resonant Cavity Antenna with Reduced Profile
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A low-profile Fabry-Perot (F-P) resonant cavity antenna with an enhanced gain and a reduced radar cross section (RCS) is presented. The antenna is composed of an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC)-partially reflective surface (PRS) superstrate, an AMC ground and a radiation patch. The PRS and AMC ground form a F-P cavity. Due to the zero-phase reflection of the AMC ground, the thickness of the cavity is reduced into quarter wavelength. In addition, such a thickness results in a phase difference of 180° between reflections of the PRS-backed AMC superstrate and the AMC ground, which makes the backward RCS of the antenna is reduced. Simulated results demonstrate the designed F-P antenna realize 4.6 dB gain promotion at 10 GHz and Radar Cross Section reduction cover 8 to 20 GHz in contrast to the primary patch antenna.

articleTitle: A microwave diffraction focusing method for oblique incidence
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Microwave will have oblique incident diffraction effect in some specific scenes, which will cause the main maximum field intensity deviation and the signal reception will be poor. In order to solve the problem of main maximum field intensity migration, a method based on the Fresnel diffraction and the superposition of even or odd half wavelengths in the diffraction region is proposed, and the simulation is carried out with MATLAB. The simulation results show that this method can refocus the oblique incidence microwave diffraction to the center region.

articleTitle: Effect of noise on restoring ultra wide spectrum pulse waveform by V-shaped symmetrical antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: V-shaped symmetrical antennas are often used to restore UWB pulse signals. Firstly, two reflection mechanisms of V-shaped symmetrical antenna receiving free space plane wave are analyzed in this paper. The first reflection occurs in the whole process of plane wave coupling with V-shaped symmetrical antenna. The second reflection occurs at the connection between the V-shaped symmetrical antenna and its feeder. When the duration of the received pulse is greater than the round-trip time of the wave in the antenna, the waveform will be distorted by using the transfer function obtained by truncating the time-domain pulse. Therefore, this paper restores the waveform through the real transfer function of the antenna. Through a specific engineering example, the influence of oscilloscope noise on restored waveform is further analyzed.

articleTitle: Discussion on the Phase-Correction Mirror in the Quasi-Optical Mode Converter
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This work report investigations on the phase-correction mirror design for the Quasi-Optical mode converter. Specifically, the last mirror in a three-mirror converter system is generated by phase-correction, and its performance of pure Gaussian beam shaping is analyzed via different incident beam conditions. Based on numerical analysis, it can be concluded, the key for a good Gaussian conversion is that the magnitude pattern of the incident beam should be close to round Gaussian before the phase correction. That can be considered as the principle of beam shaping in the Quasi-Optical mode converters.

articleTitle: A novel broadband dual polarization cavity-backed microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a dual polarization cavity-backed microstrip antenna based on printed board technology is proposed. The impedance bandwidth of the antenna exceeds 65%. The isolation of two ports is less than -20dB in the range of 5.91GHz to 11. 48GHz, and in the range of 8.41GHz to 10.62GHz, the ports' isolation is less than - 30dB, with the bandwidth about 64% and 32% respectively. In addition, a 10×10 array are simulated, in the band, the cross polarization in the end firing direction is lower than -30dB. And the radiation patterns of 7GHz, 9.6GHz and 12GHz show that the cross polarization level of the antenna in all direction is lower than -30dB. In a word, the antenna achieves large bandwidth and ensures good isolation between ports and low cross polarization level. Moreover, it's performance changes little after forming array, so it has certain practical value.

articleTitle: A Design Method of Circular Symmetrical Focusing Reflectarray Supporting Multi-channel Wireless Transmission
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a circular symmetrical focusing reflectarray design method that supports multi-channel wireless transmission. When the wireless nodes are distributed symmetrically from the reflectarray, the reflector array provides electromagnetic wave focusing ability for its diagonal node communication. By constructing an equivalent environment, converting the multi-channel electromagnetic wave focusing problem into a vertical focusing problem, and adjusting the parameters in the equivalent environment based on the actual environment. Realize the design that supports multi-channel circular symmetrical reflectarray.

articleTitle: Analysis of TEC Time-Frequency Characteristics of Anomalous Star Links Across the Equator
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the simulation TEC data of the small satellite-GNSS satellite star link, this paper has carried out the time-frequency characteristics analysis of the equatorial anomaly, which is a typical ionospheric disturbance. Based on the first-order time difference method, the second-order time difference method and discrete cosine transform method, the time-frequency variation characteristics of the typical small satellite-GNSS satellite link TEC caused by the equatorial anomaly are obtained. Such as reversal structure of first-order time gradient, multi-wave packet structure of second-order time gradient and discrete pulse structure in frequency domain with first-order and second-order time gradient. These phenomena can be used as characteristic parameters to characterize equatorial anomalous events. It is of great significance for the development of autonomous identification method of ionospheric anomalous events based on small satellite networks.

articleTitle: Quad MIMO millimeter wave antenna for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to effectively alleviate the current situation of spectrum congestion in the low frequency band, this paper proposes a millimeter wave rectangular microstrip antenna for 5G communication, based on the dipole broadband millimeter wave unit antenna, a quad MIMO antenna is designed, the antenna size is 10.1mmx12mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>0.508mm, the operating frequency of the antenna is 28GHz, the operating bandwidth is 23~73.5GHz. It completely covers the 5G millimeter wave spectrum range of 24.25~27.5GHz and 37~42.5GHz specified by China, and the isolation degree between each unit antenna is lower than -15dB, which can ensure the normal operation of the antenna.

articleTitle: A New Method to Enhance the Radiation Characteristic of a Low Profile Horizontal Dipole with a Modified Ground
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A new method to enhance the radiation of a low profile horizontal dipole is proposed in this paper. By modifying the ground with two simple meanderline-shaped slots, the radiation of the horizontal dipole is enhanced with very low profile. The mismatch loss caused by the diminution of the height between the ground and dipole can be improved through the coupling and phase compensation from the modified ground. Simulation results show that the proposed dipole design can obtain an overall profile of 0.03 λ 0, a |S11| <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leqslant$</tex> -10 dB bandwidth of 11.3% and a boresight gain of 7.8 dBi at 2.1GHz. The good agreements between the simulation and measured results validate the proposed design.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Filtering Dipole Antenna with Integrated Differential Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article proposes one way for designing a dual-polarized printed dipole with integrated differential feeding structure. Firstly, a new filtering dipole is proposed and analyzed, which consists of three microstrip resonators. The dipole consists of a partial structure of two resonators and another resonator is used to realize the function of differential feeding. The proposed filtering dipole achieves a second-order Chebyshev response. A dual-polarized dipole is designed and fabricated based on this dipole. The simulated and measured results of the fabricated dual-polarized print dipole antenna are present. The measured S11 and S22 of the fabricated antenna are less than -10 dB in the passband (1.17 to 1.255 GHz) and the isolation (S21) is bigger than 28 dB. The measured gain is bigger than 7.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Frequency-Dependent Atmospheric Radio Refractivity Models for THz band
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Atmospheric radio refractivity has an obviously impact on the signal transmission path and communication group delay effect. In this paper, we first analysis existing radio refractivity models and establish the reference refractivity based on molecular response theory (MRT) and empirical results. Then, two frequency-dependent atmospheric radio refractivity models are proposed respectively for sub-500 band and THz band, which can avoid complex calculations in MRT. Taking the established reference refractivity as the benchmark, the numerical results show that the mean absolute errors of the two proposed models are almost less than 0.3 and 0.4 in sub-500 GHz and THz bands, respectively. This work will contribute to the research of THz communication and THz weather radar, etc.

articleTitle: Application of Electromagnetic Wave Propagation Theory to the Earth Exploration: Take the Simulation of the Magnetotelluric Fields of the Dipping Interface as an Example
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electromagnetic wave propagation theory is often used in the geo-electromagnetics. Due to the different governing equations, its application is often limited to qualitative interpretation. This article tries to learn from the method of electromagnetic wave propagation in metal, and obtains the analytical solution of magnetotelluric field in the dipping interface model is compared and analyzed with the numerical solution of magnetotelluric.

articleTitle: Pixelated Microwave Sensor for Angular Displacement Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A pixelated sensor based on a complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR) is proposed to measure angular displacemen. The variation of the resonance frequency of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> with the rotation angle is defined as the sensitivity of the sensor. The angle sensing area is pixelated first, then the sensitivity of the sensor as the fitness function is optimized with the binary particle swarm algorithm (BPSO), and finally the sensor that is more sensitive to angle changes is proposed. The simulation results show that the pixelated angle sensor has higher sensitivity than the rectangular CSRR sensor and the circular CSRR sensor of the same size. The sensitivity of the pixelated angle sensor is 19MHz/degree, while that of the rectangular CSRR sensor and circular CSRR sensor are 1.3MHz/degree and 1.6MHz/degree respectively.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit of Metamaterial Formed by Array of Conductive Disks
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The use of metamaterials to obtain a wideband wide angle impedance matching (WAIM) for compact phased array of interconnected crossed rings is investigated. The metamaterial layer above the planar array is formed by array of conductive disks in contrast to the conventional multilayer homogeneous dielectric structure. The equivalent circuit of the metamaterial layer to enhance wideband array antenna design is derived based on a hybrid technique. The values of the components in the equivalent circuit to represent metamaterial layer is given. The response from the equivalent circuit is verified by using the full-wave numerical simulations on the metamaterial structure. The results show the effectiveness of the method in analyzing the electromagnetic characteristics of the structure and improving the performance of the whole array system.

articleTitle: Fixed-Frequency Beam-Scanning Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a fixed-frequency beam-scanning leaky-wave antenna (LWA) based on the spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) structure. A coplanar waveguide is adopted as the feed structure of the antenna. A radiating patch array is loaded beside the SSPPs transmission line, and the radiation state of each patch element is controlled by the loaded PIN diode. Beam scanning can be achieved using the period-reconfigurable method. Finally, a beam scanning range of 56° is realized at 13.5 GHz, with a peak gain of 9 dBi.

articleTitle: Wideband Back-to-Back Folded Dipole Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Antenna-in-Package Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A back-to-back folded dipole antenna is presented in this paper. Comprised of a pair of two symmetric folded microstrip lines, this presented antenna is fed by parallel vias coupled from an open-ended grounded co-planar waveguide (GCPW), which is used to obtain desired differential current. To have a more symmetric radiation pattern, a back-to-back structure is employed. The idea was verified with a prototype designed for 60-GHz millimeter-wave applications. After optimization using ANSYS HFSS, the size of the antenna can be obtained as 1.0 x 1.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, namely 0.20 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>x 0.22 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ0 is the wavelength in the free space at 60 GHz. A wide 10-dB impedance wideband of 32.2% (52.9-73.3 GHz) can be obtained. Having the advantages of wide bandwidth and small size, this antenna is thus suitable for millimeter-wave antenna-in-package designs.

articleTitle: An Improved Finite Difference Time Domain Method: Convolutional Perfectly Matched Layer in Alternating Direction Implicit Formulae
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The convolutional perfectly matched layer with alternating direction implicit scheme is improved to decrease the reflection error level with bigger Courant number (CFLN). We demonstrate the advancement in detail by dispersing finite difference time domain equations. Although the method needs a bit more computational memory, results show that the reflections with different CFLNs are perfectly limited in a similar range in the modified the scheme.

articleTitle: A Method for Accurately Measuring the Thickness of Plane Medium
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A segmented method for measuring the thickness of plane dielectric film in the inner wall of rectangular cavity sensor is put forward based on the principle of dielectric perturbation method and transverse resonance method. The microwave rectangular resonator is applied as the sensor, and it works in TE101 mode in the proposed method. The relationship between the thickness of the resonator film and the resonant frequency is deduced theoretically, and the feasibility of TE101 mode to accurately measure dielectric film is analyzed by simulation. Simulation results show that the proposed method has the advantage of high measuring accuracy. The method can accurately measure the thickness of dielectric films.

articleTitle: Near-field Echo Signal Model of Ground Background Based on Scattering Distribution Function
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional millimeter wave proximity detector model using backscattering coefficients has a large height setting error when the background echo signal quality is poor and the signal-noise ratio is insufficient, a near-field millimeter wave echo signal model based on scattering distribution function for complex feature background is proposed. The model is optimized as an upper half-space scattering distribution function based on the characteristics of feature types to study the near-field scattering functions of soil, vegetation and other backgrounds, and the scattering signals of each microscattering unit in the irradiated area of the detector beam at different moments are calculated in real time by combining with the missile target encounter model, and the echoes received at the detector are obtained in real time after integration. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional method, the model can meet the requirements of detection simulation with higher accuracy of background echo calculation under the condition of lower signal-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Heating rate of thermal electrons by the fast part of EDF in the ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We propose to use the bi-Maxwellian electron distribution function (EDF) to describe the characteristics of the electron gas in the ionosphere. Such EDF allows one to simulate almost all EDFs found in practice by changing the ratio between the temperatures and densities of two groups of electrons. As a result, this made it possible to obtain simple analytical formulas for calculating the heating of Maxwellian thermal electrons by fast ones. It is shown that the linearized representation of the interelectron collision integral obtained for a one-temperature EDF is not suitable for calculating the heating of electrons in a two-temperature EDF.

articleTitle: Reaction of PMSE and PMWE to HF heating: comparison during a heater cycling
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Using the EISCAT VHF radar observations, the comparison of reaction of polar mesosphere summer and winter echoes (PMSE and PMWE) to HF heating is presented. The response of PMSE and PMWE to HF heating shows a similar pattern however, it is found that HF heating effects on PMSE is 0.92 times greater than its effect on PMWE. In addition, after the heater switched-off, the overshoot produced in PMSE is 1.7 times greater than it produced in PMWE. Furthermore, due to HF heating, in PMSE the greater enhancement produced in electron temperature produces PMSE modulation 1.2 times greater than PMWE modulation. For greater statistical significance to the present conclusions further investigations with larger dataset are required.

articleTitle: On Hybrid AOA/RT Non-cooperative Target Localization in NLOS Outdoor Scenario
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, the non-cooperative target localization problem in the outdoor environment is addressed, which suits the non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenario. Localization accuracy is highly affected by non-cooperative source and multipath phenomena, making the problem harder to handle. A non-cooperative target situation cannot obtain the time of arrival (TOA). Therefore, traditional precise positioning methods fail in this scenario. Thence, to handle the localization problem at adverse conditions, this paper takes the angle of arrival (AOA) into account. Considering the channel reciprocity between transceivers, a novel localization method is proposed by combining AOA and ray-tracing (RT). Besides, a density-based clustering algorithm is used to enhance localization accuracy. Our simulation validates the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed approach, outperforming the fingerprint (FP) localization method and showing the hybrid algorithm's benefit.

articleTitle: Analysis of Tuning Range and Quality Factor Characteristics and Its Application to Tunable Bandstop Filter
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the tuning range and quality of four types of varactor-loaded resonators, varactor-loaded λ/2 resonator, varactor-loaded λ/4 resonator, varacor-loaded open-loop resonator, and dual-varactor-loaded resonator, are analyzed. To verify the varactor-loaded λ/4 resonator has largest tuning range and the varactor-loaded λ/2 resonator has largest quality, a dual-band banstop filter based dual-mode resonator is proposed. The dual-mode resonator can be represented by varactor-loaded λ/2 resonator circuit and varactor-loaded λ/4 resonator circuit. The simulated results are presented to verify the theoretical predications.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-Polarized Crossed Dipole
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-polarized crossed dipole with broad impedance bandwidth and high port-isolation is introduced in this paper. The crossed dipole antenna consists of four radiation arms, a metallic reflector and a balun. The radiation pattern can be widened with radiation arms tipped down at a 7 percent tilt. To achieve the unidirectional radiation, a metallic reflector (80mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>80mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup>3mm) is mounted at the back of the antenna. The balun used in this paper is different from the balun mentioned in other literature, it can convert the coaxial feed structure to the differential feed structure., thus improving the performance of the dual polarization configurations. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has stable symmetric unidirectional radiation patterns in the operating frequency band from 2.25 to 3.12 GHz with the port-to-port isolation better than 35dB. By setting the phase difference between the two ports to 90°, circularly polarized pattern polarization pattern can be obtained.

articleTitle: Adaptive SVM Assisted Density-based Clustering Algorithm for mmWave Radio Channels
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Channel clustering is a significant implement in channel modeling and simulations. In this work, we propose an automatic clustering algorithm, namely adaptive support vector machine (SVM) assisted density-based algorithm (ASD). Firstly, adaptive-K is used to calculate the key multipath components (MPCs), which is vital to train the SVM. Secondly, the SVM is applied in clustering by the full partition of MPCs feature space, where the SVM is insensitive to the distribution variation of intra-cluster. Then, validation index silhouette coefficient S is used to select the optimum number of MPCs in one class, which are used to train the SVM classify model. Finally, the performance of the proposed ASD algorithm is evaluated based on measured data in mmWave band. Experimental clustering results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The proposed algorithms can be applied in multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) channels without knowing the number and initial locations of cluster in advance.

articleTitle: Ocean Wave Inversion Using TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X Images
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Most real interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) systems are a combination of along and cross track configurations. For the hybrid interferometry, the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images of TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X are successfully used to retrieve the sea surface elevation (SSE) and the wavelength of dominant waves in this work. The significant wave height (SWH) of the retrieved ocean wave is 0.62m and the wavelength of dominant waves is 305m. The difference between the retrieved SWH and the SWH provided by European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) is -0.09m, which is acceptable in the ocean wave inversion. Since the ECMWF does not directly provide the wavelength of the ocean waves, there is no available reference wavelength to compare with the wavelength of ocean waves retrieved in this paper.

articleTitle: On the Performance Computational Model of the Radar in the Complicated Electromagnetic Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Base on the radar signal detection process, the performance computational model of the radar in the complicated electromagnetic environment is constructed. The interferences models are constructed as well. According to the computational models the radar performances are computed and the computational results agree with the theory analyses. The computational model adapt to arbitrary interference.

articleTitle: Deployment of Multiple Interfering Unmanned Aerial Vehicles for Maximal Transmission Rate
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV) communication are considered to be the key technology in 5G to address coverage and emergency communication in remote areas. In order to achieve full coverage for all users, we consider using multiple UAVs to jointly provide coverage for the target area. And there is interference between multiple UAVs, which will reduce the received signal-to-noise ratio of users, thus affecting the communication quality. In order to reduce the interference in the communication of multiple UAVs, an optimization problem model is established to maximize the minimum transmission rate of users. The proposed multi-population genetic algorithm is used to solve the problem and the locations of all UAVs that maximize the minimum transmission rate of users are obtained.

articleTitle: Research on Target Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics Based on Improved Parabolic Equation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The standard parabolic equation(PE) method is an effective way to solve the target scattering problem, but the error of calculation is large in the case of high elevation angles. In order to improve the limitations of the standard parabolic equation algorithm, this paper introduces the Padé-(1,1) polynomial into the parabolic equation algorithm, combining the absorption conditions of the perfectly matched layer (PML) to solve the scattering field distribution of electrically large targets. It is shown that the introduction of Padé-(1,1) polynomial into the standard parabolic equation can more accurately calculate the scattering field distribution of the target. It can solve the problem of electromagnetic scattering within 40 degrees in the axial direction, effectively. At the same time, it also overcomes the shortcomings of the long-time calculation of target electromagnetic scattering by the full-wave method and the high requirements of computer hardware. This improving parabolic equation provides a new idea for the calculation of the scattering field of wide-elevation targets.

articleTitle: A Low-Angle Tracking Error Analysis Method in Maritime Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a low-angle tracking error analysis model based on the two-way parabolic equation (2WPE) method in maritime environment. The estimation of elevation error is carried out based on the improved fractal sea surface model with different wind speeds. Furthermore, the presence of noise in the receiving channel is also considered. The simulation results show that the presented model well represents the effect of the rough sea surface on the low-angle tracking application.

articleTitle: Strong Electromagnetic Protection Circuit for RF Front End of Autodyne Radio Fuze
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the RF front end of autodyne radio fuze is weak in resisting high-power and energy-based jamming, a design method of electromagnetic protection circuit for RF front end is proposed. The method is to add an electromagnetic protection circuit composed of microwave limiter, RF band-pass filter, and single pole double throw switch, which between RF front-end circuit and transceiver antenna of the autodyne radio fuze. The electromagnetic protection of RF front-end core high-frequency devices is carried out by means of excess energy attenuation, selection of passing frequency, and transmission channel locking. Experimental verification shows that the electromagnetic protection circuit can protect the RF front end of the Autodyne radio fuze in both the frequency domain and the time domain, and improve the survivability of the fuze in the high EM environment.

articleTitle: Theoretical simulation of ELF excitation in modulated heating F layers in low and middle latitudes
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to study the characteristics of extremely low frequency (ELF) radiation source modulated by ionospheric modulation heating F in low and middle latitudes, based on the theory of ionospheric driving current, a numerical model of ELF excited by amplitude modulation heating F layer was established. According to the analysis of this model, under the action of amplitude modulation heating wave, it will cause the electronic pressure gradient to oscillate according to the modulation frequency to form an oscillating diamagnetic ring current, which in turn excites the ELF radiation source. The minimum value and the distribution of double-peak morphology, the dipole moment intensity of the radiation source decreases rapidly with the increase of the modulation frequency.

articleTitle: A Compact Low-pass Filter Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Using Novel Butterfly Unit-Cell Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a compact low-pass filter with a novel butterfly unit-cell structure based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) is presented. The filter mainly consists of the novel butterfly unit-cells structure, and transition structures. The novel butterfly unit-cell structure is composed of an elliptical patch rotated 30° to the left and right directions, which can significantly reduce the size and insertion loss after hollowing out. Compared with the traditional rectangular and elliptical structure, the novel butterfly unit-structure has better dispersion characteristics, which can greatly improve the filter's in-band flatness and out-of-band rejection capability. Owing to the advantages of the dispersion characteristics of the novel butterfly unit-cell structure, the size of the proposed filter is smaller than other filters. The length is reduced by about 20%. The simulation results show that the insertion loss of the proposed low-pass filter is very low, and the maximum value is only 0.9 dB. The simulation results show that this novel butterfly unit-cell structure has a good application prospect in the design of SSPPs microwave devices.

articleTitle: The composite scattering of a missile above the sea surface
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The research of composite scattering between target and background has always been a hotspot in the RCS computation, target identification and stealthy. In this paper, the sea surface modeling by Weierstrass fractal function, the composite scattering of sea surface and missile based on physical optics method (PO) and shooting and bouncing rays (SBR) method are investigated. The results of the electromagnetic scattering software ESEE, by using OpenGL graphic programming technology and C++ multithreading processing technology, are presented. The results are validated by comparison with commercial software. The composite scattering of different sea states, different heights and different attitudes are investigated.

articleTitle: GMR 2D Magnetic Probe for Measuring Lightning Surface Current Distribution on Metal Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Utilizing giant magneto resistive (GMR) sensors, a two-dimension (2D) measurement system is developed. Based on the high sensitivity, wide bandwidth and small size of GMR sensor, a 2D detection probe is designed for this system, and its basic structure and operating principle are described in detail in this paper. In order to test the performances of this developed system, an experimental scheme of calibration and frequency response is presented. To further validate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed 2D measurement system, an experiment measuring lightning surface current density on an aluminum cylinder is conducted. Comparisons of experimental and simulation results are given. Results show the 2D measurement system is capable of detecting the distribution tendency of current density on cylindrical surface. The developed system provides a practical tool to detect lightning surface current distribution on the curved surface.

articleTitle: A High Fidelity Time-domain Disk-cone Antenna for Electromagnetic Pulse Measuring
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A high fidelity time-domain disk-cone antenna is proposed in this letter for electromagnetic pulse measuring. The proposed antenna is formed by a disk, a lower cone, an upper cone and a coaxial cable feed. Different from the traditional disk-cone antenna, a small upper cone is added between the disk and lower cone in order to improve the antenna's capacitance distribution and realize impedance matching. With further optimization, the proposed antenna has good broadband characterristics and high pulse fidelity, which makes itself a good candidate for electromagnetic pulse measuring.

articleTitle: Research on a fuze anti-jamming strategy under the background of complex ground objects
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of the reduced reliability of the radio proximity fuze under the jamming of complex ground objects,a method of fixed height for laser and radio combined detection is proposed. Using the method of dual-beam separate airspace detection and information fusion,a mathematical model of the fuze's fixed height initiation is established. Through the analysis of the dynamic ground detection model and the ground objects jamming detection model, this design idea and mathematical model against the ground objects jamming effectiveness are confirmed.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement for the Central Element in a 7-element GNSS Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The effect of mutual coupling (MC) between arrays changes the input impedance of each element, resulting in impedance mismatch and gain loss. In this letter, MC for a global navigation satellite system (GNSS) antenna consists of 7 elements is discussed. We find that the active and passive antenna array have different mutual coupling conditions, and the measured active central element has a significant gain loss in the zenith direction using the embedded element pattern method. We use the Ansoft HFSS simulator for secondary simulation to improve the antenna array. The antenna is adj usted by changing the impedance value of each port to simulate the state of the active antenna, and finally, a more suitable array structure is obtained to enhance the gain of the central element. Compared with the gain of the original measured central element, the gain of the adj usted central element is improved by about 8 dB, and the gain patterns of the outer elements are not affected too much.

articleTitle: Newton-ADE-FDTD Method for Oblique Incident Unmagnetized Time-varying Plasma
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article combines the fundamental Newton's equation of motion with the auxiliary differential equation (ADE) method, the Newton-ADE-FDTD iterative formula of isotropic time-varying plasma with oblique incidence of electromagnetic wave is derived. The biggest difference between this method and the common ADE-FDTD method is that the derivative of the logarithm of the electron density of the time-varying plasma is added to the updated equation of the current density. This method is used to calculate the reflection coefficient of electromagnetic wave entering the unmagnetized time-varying plasma slab at different incident angles, and compared with the analytical solution and the ADE-FDTD method, the results show that the Newton-ADE-FDTD method is correct and effective.

articleTitle: An Improved Ultra-Wideband Circularly Polarized Cross-Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband Circularly Polarized (CP) cross-dipole antenna is proposed. And it can be divided three layers. The top layer is composed of a pair of crossed-dipoles and four parasitic rectangular patches. The middle layer consists of metal walls, and the bottom layer is a metal ground. The purpose of adding four parasitic patches, four metal walls and rings of phase delay for the dipole arm is to expand the impedance bandwidth (IBW) and axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW). In addition, by improving the feed structure at the dipole arm, the ARBW can be further widened. The overall design size of the final antenna is 0.8λ0*0.8λ0*0.29λ0 (λ0 is the wavelength at 3.7 GHz). The simulation results depict that the IBW of is 99.3% (1.83 GHz~5.44 GHz) and 3dB ARBW of is 91.4% (2.02 GHz~5.42 GHz). The gain range of the proposed antenna is 3.3dBic to 6dBic in the CP working frequency band.

articleTitle: BER of FRFT-based SCIFDM System for Ionospheric Scatter Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Large transmission loss and time-frequency dual selective fading characteristics make ionospheric scatter communication a challenge. In order to improve the performance of ionospheric scatter communication, the fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) module which can process nonstationary signals is used to replace the traditional fast Fourier transform (FFT) block. The simulation results show that the modulation method based on FRFT can effectively improve the bit error rate (BER) performance of single carrier interleaved frequency division multiplexing (SCIFDM) system. In addition, for different fading channels, the best performance can be obtained by adjusting the order of FRFT.

articleTitle: Design of E-band Co-aperture Dual-polarized terminal antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents two types of E-band co-aperture dual-polarized antennas for mobile terminal devices, including broadside and end-fire, and explains its implementation mechanism and design methods. The broadside antenna uses L-shaped probe differential feed to realize dual polarization and widen the bandwidth. It has wide beam in the polarization direction, and the central frequency 3dB beamwidth are 137° for H-pol and 139° for V-pol in E plane. The end-fire antenna combines an open waveguide antenna with a planar dipole antenna to achieve end-fire co-aperture dual polarization. In order to improve matching performance and increase antenna gain, introduce parasitic patch and metal grid wall as director and reflector respectively. Antenna structure parameters are optimized by ANSYS HFSS, and the performances such as realized gain, cross polarization and port isolation of both elements meet the design requirements. The 1×4 linear arrays are proposed according to the designed elements, which can realize one-dimensional beam scanning in a certain scanning range.

articleTitle: Defend Against Jamming Attacks Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Cognitive radio network has the learning ability to adjust transmission behavior to adapt to dynamic electromagnetic environment, and it has become a research hotspot in the field of the new generation of intelligent wireless communication systems. However, recent research results show that cognitive radio networks are vulnerable to interference attacks, resulting in a serious decline in spectrum utilization. In this paper, an intelligent anti-jamming scheme based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, and the anti-jamming decision of the communication party is modeled as a Markov decision chain. This method can help the communication transmitter to learn a combination of communication parameters that can maximize the probability of communication success. In the specific implementation, we use Double DQN as the communication decision-making brain, and specially designed a convolutional neural network suitable for the communication spectrum as input to accurately estimate the action value function. The simulation results show that our method has better performance than the traditional anti-jamming method based on reinforcement learning.

articleTitle: Analysis of 3D Magnetic Plasma Electromagnetic Scattering Based on Precise-Integration Time-Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A technique ground on precise-integration in time-domain (PITD) is applied to resolve the problem of electromagnetic scattering characteristics of magnetized plasma. The method combines the main equations of current density vector and electric field intensity vector with the principal equation of electric flux density D through the calculation method of auxiliary differential equations, and the equations are rewritten as linear ordinary differential equations for solving, and the coefficient matrix and integral terms in the equations are processed by the exact integration (PI) analysis and Gaussian integration methods, respectively, to obtain the component iterative equations for the solution of the ordinary differential equations. The technique is further implemented to analyze the galvanomagnetic scattering characteristics of a homogeneous time-varying magnetized plasma sphere through the simulation verification of a three-dimensional non-magnetized plasma sphere.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Dual-Band ±45° Dual-Polarized Antenna Array for Millimeter-Wave Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A millimeter-wave compact dual-band ±45° dual-polarized antenna element is presented firstly. It consists of dual-ring patches in different sizes, four parasitic strips and two L-probes for ±45° dual-polarized feeding. The antenna element is operating from 24.22 to 30.5 GHz and from 36.82 to 45 GHz, which are completely covering n257~n261 frequency bands of 5G communication. Then a 1 × 4 antenna array has been investigated for beam scanning, working from 24.5 to 29.3 GHz and from 37.5 to 45 GHz. The simulated realized gain in broadside direction is 10 and 11.1 dBi at 27 and 39 GHz respectively. The main beam direction can achieve ±58° scanning at 27 GHz, while achieve ±32° scanning at 39 GHz.

articleTitle: Research on impedance matching of monocone feed based on inductive capacitive compensation technology
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Starting from the geometric structure of the connection between the monocone and its feeder, and based on the inductive and capacitive analysis technology, this paper qualitatively analyzes that when the virtual feed point of the monocone is located in the plane of the mirror, the feed point is inductive relative to the coaxial line. By loading a ring at the inner core of the feed point, the reflection at the feed point structure is significantly improved after capacitive compensation. By analyzing the polarity of the feed point reflection signal, a more refined compensation scheme is proposed. The simulation results show that this compensation scheme can reduce the feed point reflection by one order of magnitude.

articleTitle: A Reflect-Transmit Array with Full-Space Independent Beamforming Capability
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel reflect-transmit array (RTA) is presented that can enable independent beam steering in full space. The proposed unit cell consists of a metallic Jerusalem cross resonator, which locates between a pair of orthogonally oriented subwavelength metal gratings. By adjusting the length of the metal resonator, 2-bit codes (including '1-bit reflection and transmission phases) are generated. Next, the entire 25x25-element array fed by a pyramidal horn antenna, which is subjected to the quick response (QR) code, is divided into transmission and reflection distribution. The entire structure of the array is arranged in accordance with the transmission beam toward θ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>= 0° and the reflection beam toward θ0 = 160°. The simulated results demonstrate the full-space independent beamforming capability.

articleTitle: A Novel Polarization Rotating Unit Cell for Folded Reflectarray with 2-bit Reconfigurable resolution
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel two-layer reconfigurable reflectarray unit cell with polarization rotating ability by utilizing the feature of linear-to-circular conversion is developed in this paper. A mixed method combining alterable polarization and tunable resonator is innovatively employed in the unit cell design to provide 2-bit phase reconfiguration. The unit cell is designed, fabricated and measured. Experimental results using the waveguide simulator method demonstrate the good magnitude and phase performance within the frequency band from 28 to 32GHz. Therefore, the presented unit cell is an attractive candidate for a wide bandwidth folded reflectarray antenna (FRA).

articleTitle: An improved method for solving plane thin dielectric problems based on simplified prism vector basis functions
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new method to solve the scattering problems of thin dielectric structures. In this method, simplified prism vector (SPV) basis functions are used, which greatly reduces the number of unknowns, and the multilevel fast multipole algorithm is used to accelerate the calculation of far groups (SPV-MLFMA). Further, for the near groups with large number of unknowns, we introduce H-matrix theory and adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm to further accelerate the filling of nearby groups. The SPV-MLFMA+ACA method effectively reduces the calculation time and memory consumption compared with SPV-MLFMA. Numerical results verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Sea Surface Scattering Characteristics Based on Slope Statistics of Sliding Window
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In view of the insufficient applicability of the current engineer laser short-range sea surface scattering echo related calculation model, it is impossible to effectively evaluate the performance of the system under different conditions, the simulated wave pool environment is used to obtain the detection system at a fixed height and attitude. Data has limitations such as limited sample points and high funding. This paper proposes a sea surface scattering echo model based on three-point sliding window function statistics. By discretizing the sampling of the wave cross section and obtaining the slope statistics under different intersection conditions, the ray tracing method and the slope value are used to determine the effective surface element. The statistical value of the detection probability and the value of the SNR interval under different sea conditions and attitude angles are obtained by simulation, this provides adaptability assessment and related technical index reference for laser short-range sea surface detection.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Time-varying Multimode Propagation on Receiving Performance of Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the receiving performance of shortwave array antenna changes with communication time, transmission distance and other factors, based on the ionosphere reflection propagation model and the shortwave channel model, this paper analyzes the influence of different states of ionosphere on the incoming signal, and gives the expression of the received signal of each element under the time-varying multimode propagation state. On this basis, the receiving performance curve of the array antenna is drawn, which provides a basis for the design of the communication system.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation Research on SHS of Ti-B System Used in Space Experiment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The electron density in the ionosphere space can be significantly enhanced by releasing easily ionizable metal into the ionosphere. The reflection and scattering of radio waves can be established or enhanced, thereby affecting the propagation of electromagnetic waves in the information system. The lanthanide metal as diluent, which is mixed in the titanium-boron system, is heated to a gaseous state by using titanium-boron self-propagating combustion synthesis reaction. The gaseous state lanthanide metal is released into ionosphere, which can fully interact with the oxygen atom to generate a high-density plasma cloud. In this paper, a one-dimensional Fourier combustion model of the self-propagating combustion synthesis reaction of titanium-boron is established according to the conservation of energy and mass. The SHS process of the Ti-B system is numerically simulated by using the finite difference method and the Gauss-Seidel iterative algorithm. The influence of green compact porosity on combustion temperature and combustion synthesis spread rate is studied. At the same time, the effects of uneven porosity and convection heat dissipation are considered. The calculation results show that the porosity has a certain influence on the combustion characteristics of the reaction system. The combustion temperature of the combustion wave with different porosities basically remains unchanged. The combustion temperature varies between 2170K ~ 2200K. The porosity has a great influence on the propagation rate (combustion speed) of the combustion wave. When the porosity is about 30%, the combustion speed is about 4.5mm/s. However, as the porosity increases, the combustion speed continues to decrease. When it is greater than 80%, the combustion speed is reduced to zero, and the combustion will be quenched. The simulation calculation results can be used for the future system design of space experiment.

articleTitle: Rayleigh lidar observations of temperature variations in the middle atmopshere over Qujing
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A Rayleigh lidar has been operated in Qujing for observing the middle atmospheric temperature in altitude from 30 to 70 km. Good agreement is found between lidar and satellite, and between lidar and model. Based on the data set consisting of 10 nights of measurements, the nocturnal temperature evolution in the height range of 30 - 60 km is studied. The results clearly show a trend of high temperature before and low temperature after midnight in the upper stratosphere and lower mesosphere, in particular a structure of tidal associated temperature disturbances with downward phase propagation between 35 and 45 km. The amplitude of temperature oscillation is approximately 3 K. These results are consistent with other lidar measurements made at similar latitudes.

articleTitle: Behavior from Phase Factor Approximate Upon the Beam Propagation in Bessel Beam Angular Spectrum Expansion
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this study, the effect of approximate order numbers of phase factor on beam propagation in Bessel beam angular spectrum characterization is studied. Based on angular spectrum expansion, the analytical expression for beam propagation are presented under the zero, first, and second-order approximation of the phase factor. The corresponding analysis and discussion for the results are conducted.

articleTitle: Research on a New Flat Plate Lightning Three-dimensional Electric Field Sensor
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we develop a new flat plate lightning three-dimensional (3D) electric field sensor which takes the printed circuit board (PCB) as the shell. The measurement antenna of sensor is integrated with the shell, making its layout more reasonable, structure more stable, light weight and easy to carry. Meanwhile, the sensor is equipped with corresponding waterproof cover and support device to make it suitable for lightning electromagnetic pulse (LEMP) 3D electric field open-air test. The calibration test shows that the sensor has good linearity and small inter pole coupling coefficient.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Bandwidth of Microstrip Antenna by Introducing Parasitic Feed Line
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper present a new method to enhance the bandwidth of microstrip antenna. Based on this method, a new broadband microstrip antenna is designed. This paper innovatively adopts a parasitic feed line and places it under the radiation patch to excite the vertical polarization wave, which can greatly broaden the bandwidth. By improving the feed structure and optimizing the parameters, the VSWR of designed antenna is lower than 2 ranging from 1.42 GHz to 1.8 GHz, and the relative bandwidth reaches 23.6%. In addition, the antenna unit has a small size, which can realize large angle scanning in a wide frequency band. In this paper, a 4 X 4 array is simulated and verified the wideband large angle scanning performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced microwave absorption property of rare earth Sm-La co-doped barium ferrite ceramics
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Doping of rare earth elements to modulate the microwave absorption properties of materials remains a challenge, especially using the strategy of two-element substitution. In this paper, the rare earth elements of Sm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+-La<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>+ co-doped barium ferrite Ba(SmLa)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12-2x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</inf>(x = 0, 0.5, 1, denoted as BFSLO-x) ceramics were the compounds which were planed to use sol-gel method. The synthesized BFSLO-x materials were of typical single hexagonal phase and sheet nanostructure with the tolerably particle sizes based on the XRD and SEM measurement. With the increase of x, the values of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> and M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> decrease, while the values of He elevate. The use of rare earth elements causes the arisen of super-exchange, which was the reason for the weakening of saturation magnetization and the decrease of remnant magnetization. Electromagnetic parameters of the sample could be well adjusted by rare earth element doping, and the performance of microwave absorption could also be enhanced. The maximum reflection loss of BFSLO-1.0 sample could reach -21.6 dB at 14.90 GHz with an effective absorption bandwidth of 2.48 GHz. The results provide a viable option for the study of high-performance microwave absorbing materials through rare earth doping strategies.

articleTitle: Physical mechanism analysis of complex target scattering center based on ISAR image
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The physical mechanism of complex target scattering center formation is analyzed by inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image in this paper. Firstly, the scattering electric field of the target is calculated by shooting and bouncing rays and the physical theory of diffraction (SBR-PTD) method, and the scattering electric field is used for the ISAR imaging of complex targets. Then the scattering field intensity distribution figure of the target at the center frequency and center azimuth angle of the ISAR image is figured. Finally, the scattering center distribution of the target is analyzed. ISAR image and scattering field distribution intensity figure reflect the scattering center of the target.

articleTitle: Research of Vortex Electromagnetic Beam Generation and Scattering Characteristics Based on FEKO
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to investigate the generation and scattering characteristics of vortex electromagnetic (EM) beam, a uniform circular array (UCA) is used to generate the vortex EM beam. The scattering field, total field and radar cross section of vortex EM beam illuminating a sphere are calculated, respectively. Results indicate that phase difference of each dipole in UCA has exceedingly significant effect on the incident field, furthermore, it affects the scattering characteristics and the modal spectrum of the scattering field. It reveals that the scattering field and total field illuminated by vortex EM beam are also vortex fields, in addition, topological charges of scattering field and total field have high consistencies with incident field, these can provide a theoretical basis for the research of vortex EM beam radar detection.

articleTitle: Improvement on the Polarization Ratio Model of the L-band Echo from Sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The L-band polarization ratio (PR) is analyzed on the basis of the SAR data acquired by the airborne radar UAVSAR. And two new empirical PR models are proposed based on 60 quad-polarization images. One of the new empirical PR models is a function of incidence angle only, while the other has additional dependence on scatter coefficient. Unlike the forms of some PR models which are functions of wind speed, the new PR models for L-band data do not depend on wind speed, which makes the models more convenient for application. Finally, another 60 quad-polarization UAVSAR images are used to validate the performance of the new PR models. Meanwhile, the behavior of an empirical PR model proposed by other scholars is also presented for comparisons. From the results we can conclude that the PR predicted by the new model which includes scatter coefficient is more consistent with the measurements.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Thinned Array Antenna with Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a thinned array synthesis method based on convolutional neural network is proposed. Different from the full array, thinned arrays cannot be synthesized by conventional methods. If the full-wave simulation method is adopted, the cost of the array synthesis will increase. The method proposed in this paper only needs to use a small amount of simulation data to obtain the relationship between the feed phase and the beam direction. The training set used is the feed phase and the corresponding pattern at 30° intervals. A 16 × 16 full array and three different thinned arrays are used to test. The results show that the convolutional neural network can keep good accuracy under these conditions.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Polarized Filtering Antenna for 5G Sub-6 GHz Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a filter antenna applied to 5G base stations. The design uses the antenna's own resonance characteristics to expand the antenna bandwidth and achieves the antenna filter performance without adding a filter circuit. The antenna simulation design size is 0.34λ×0.34λ0.27λ, and the working frequency band is 3.25-4.23 GHz (∣S11∣< -15 dB), covering 3.3-3.8GHZ required by 5G base stations, realizing the antenna miniaturization and broadbandization. The realized gain of the antenna in the frequency band is 8.3±0.5dBi, and the in-band radiation is stable.

articleTitle: Study on Zonal Drifts of Low-Latitude F Region Irregularities over Southern China Using $C/N_{0}$ Measurements from BDS GEO Satellite
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper we estimated the zonal drift velocity of low-latitude <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{F}$</tex> region irregularities over Southern China by using the 1-Hz carrier-to-noise density ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(C/N_{0})$</tex> observations of the geostationary earth orbit (GEO) satellite C03 of BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS). The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C/N_{0}$</tex> data analyzed were collected between April 2014 and April 2015 by two very close stations, i.e., HKCL (22.296°N, 113.908°E) and HKQT (22.291°N, 114.213°E). The two stations are located approximately along the east-west direction with a separation of about 31.38 km. The statistical results indicated that low-latitude F region irregularities over Southern China drifted eastwardly with the drift velocity ranging from 30 to 200 m/s. In most cases (with the occurrence rate of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 72 %) the eastward drift velocity of these F region irregularities varied between 70 and 130 m/s. These statistical results were consistent with those of previous studies. This study also verified the feasibility of the method, which estimates the zonal drift velocity of low-latitude F region irregularities by using the 1- Hz <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C/N_{0}$</tex> measurements of BDS GEO satellite's B1I signal collected by two very close stations.

articleTitle: HF Propagation Effects Caused by Artificial Plasma Cloud in the Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Releasing easily ionized metal vapor, such as barium, strontium, lithium, cesium, or samarium, can form an enhanced electron density region, which can affect radio wave propagation significantly. The high-frequency (HF) radio wave propagation effects caused by chemical releases in the ionosphere have been investigated. Ray tracing technique have been used to successfully model HF radio wave propagation path. The results show that the new propagation paths of HF radio wave are established by the artificial plasma cloud, and the lower the frequency is, the more complex the propagation path becomes. Up to four new propagation paths are created for 10MHz wave propagating 500km. For 15MHz and 20MHz wave propagating 500km, there is a new propagation path, which is inexistent without artificial plasma cloud, in other words a new radio link is created.

articleTitle: HRRP Analysis of Composite Model from a Target above Rough Ground
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the paper, high resolution range profile (HRRP) of a target above rough ground is analyzed based on the scattered echo data. The electromagnetic scattering of composite model is solved by the hybrid method of physical optics (PO)- shooting and bouncing ray (SBR). And an octree data structure is used to accelerate the ray tracing progress. The bistatic electromagnetic scattering of a reduced-scale vehicle target above rough ground is calculated by our method and compared with the simulation result with MLFMM in FEKO. Then by inverse Fourier transform of backscattering echo data, the range profile of composite model is obtained.

articleTitle: Research on Influence of Charged Sand Atmosphere on the Performance of Ku and Ka Band Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In arid and semi-arid areas, in the atmosphere carrying sand particles, in order to make the radar work all-weather, it is necessary to research the properties of microwave propagation in the sand atmosphere and the impact on the radar performance. The absorption, scattering and backscattering of sand particles carrying different size and different charge are analyzed by Mie theory. At K and Ka band, using the log-normal particle size distribution spectrum in sand atmosphere with different visibility, the specific attenuation and the backscattering per unit volume of charged sand particle are studied. Based on meteorological radar equation, the radar echo power and radar reflectivity are analyzed, and the relations between they with visibility and particle charge are given. The results show that the charged particle in the sand atmosphere increases the microwave attenuation. The attenuation reaches a maximum when the charge-to-mass ratio is about 50uC/kg. When the amount of sand particle charge increases, the backscattering factor increases. The radar echo power of the sand atmosphere increases with the decrease of visibility, but when the distance is greater than a certain distance, due to the increase of attenuation, it decreases with the visibility decrease. The effect of charged particle in sand atmosphere becomes larger with increasing frequency and distance. This study can lay a good foundation for radar detection in sand and dust atmosphere, and inversion of the physical properties of the sand atmosphere.

articleTitle: Design of a Transparent Chessboard Glass for RCS Reduction and Microwave Shielding
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel transparent dielectric metasurface for RCS reduction and microwave shielding. By controlling the permittivity of the metasurface elements, the phase difference of the reflected wave can be close to 180°. In this case, the reflected beam will be strongly scattered. The dielectric metasurface is composed of PMMA and lead glass. A transparent nano silver wire film is used as the metal back. This composite glass has the functions of transmitting visible light, scattering and shielding microwave. The measured dual-band 10 dB RCS reduction bandwidth of this chessboard composite glass is 4.4-4.8 GHz (8.7%) and 5.7-6.4 GHz (11.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). The measurement results are in good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Hydrothermal assembly of NiCoAI/Ti3C2Tx MXene composites for tunable microwave absorption
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Herein, a new type tunable microwave absorber of NiCoAl/Ti3C2T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> MXene was proposed and synthesized via a simple hydrothermal method. The scanning electron microscopy confirmed that the NiCoAl is of high quality with flower-like structure uniformly bonded on the laminar Ti3C2Tx surface. The dielectric properties of the samples in X-band frequency were studied, and their microwave absorption properties and mechanisms were investigated. Benefit from the synergistic effects of improved interfacial polarization, defect dipole polarization and optimized impedance matching, NiCoAl/Ti3C2T x MXene composites display enhanced microwave absorption. Under a matching thickness of only 1.6 mm, the minimum reflection loss of the absorbers reaches -27.4 dB, and the absorption bandwidth achieves 2.5 GHz. Besides, by adjusting the thickness from 1.4 to 1.8 mm, the effective bandwidth can cover the total X-band. These results demonstrate that the NiCoAl/Ti3C2Tx composites have potentials for both tunable dielectric constant and high-performance microwave absorption.

articleTitle: All Metal Focused Transmitarray Antenna for Microwave Measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A focused transmitarray antenna adopting double double scoop-shaped elements is presented. The transmitarray is composed of four square phase shift layers and three metal waveguide layers stacked on each other. Folded interdigital structure, which not only greatly reduces the periodic size of the element, but also improves the oblique incidence stability of the element. It can be seen from the results that the spatial resolution of the proposed antenna at the center frequency is about 1.0 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The antenna has good focused performance and is suitable for various microwave measurement devices.

articleTitle: A Design of Low-profile Miniaturized Dual-polarization Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With rapid development of modern wireless communication systems, there is an urgent need for miniaturization and planarity antenna with lower profile, lighter weight and lower cost. Dual polarization shared dipole (DPSD)antenna can reduce almost half size of tradition dipole by multiplexing two polarized dipole arm structures. In this paper, based on artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) with reflective phase band-gap characteristics in a specific phase, a dual-polarized antenna with low profile, high isolation and high gain is designed. Simulation results show that the profile is down to 23mm, and improves the gain to 9.8 dB.
