articleTitle: Design of an Ultrawideband Dual-polarization Vivaldi Antenna Array in Integrated with Internal Monitoring Network
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an Ultrawideband dual-polarization printed Vivaldi array is investigated. Different from traditional Vivaldi arrays, a coupler with hexagonal coupling structure is designed for the proposed array and integrated with the feed balun of the antenna element. Based on this structure, a internal monitoring network is established in the line array. Simulated results show that the line array obtains a wide impedance matching over f1-f2 GHz (f2/f1 = 3, f1 and f2 is the lowest and the highest frequency respectively). The infinite array exhibits an operational bandwidth over f1-f2 GHz when scanning down to 50° at phi = 0° and at phi = 90° for both polarizations, with active VSWR< 4. Radiation patterns of 9 × 9 finite array are presented and the cross-polarization levels are simulated to be below -20 dB. And the coupling value for the internal monitoring network is in the range of -39 dB to -29 dB over the operating band.

articleTitle: Inversion method of ground dielectric constant in NEMP simulator working area based on unidirectional induction sensor
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the unidirectional induction characteristics of a unidirectional induction sensor, this paper separates the direct wave and reflected wave at a point directly below the working area of NEMP simulator; When the geometry of NEMP simulator is known, the transfer function between the field at the point to be investigated and its mirror point relative to the ground is established by full wave algorithm; Through the relationship between the field at the mirror point without ground and the field of scattered wave with ground, the ground dielectric constant can be solved conveniently.

articleTitle: Integrated Active Phased Array Antenna for Mobile Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An integrated active phased array antenna operating in S band for mobile satellite communication was presented. A low-cost single probe-fed circular-polarized microstrip antenna was proposed to obtain low profile, light weight and good electrical performances, and the radiation unit covered both Rx and Tx frequency bands. An integration technology, which included the antenna units, the RF circuitry, the cooling system, the networks and secondary beam control system, was introduced to maintain the performance of low profile. And the overall height of 19-element phased array antenna was less than 50mm. The experimental results showed that the antenna array could scan electrically ± 60° in the elevation and 0-360° in the azimuth, the G/T value was more than -17dB/K, and the EIRP value was greater than 25dBW.

articleTitle: Research on the Composite Electromagnetic Scattering from Soil Surface and Combinatorial Target Placed on It
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Dobson semi-empirical model and dielectric complex permittivity formula are used to represent the real and imaginary parts of the soil dielectric constant, the soil surface is simulated with the model of exponential distribution and Monte Carlo Method, the composite scattering of soil surface and combinatorial target placed on it is studied by the finite difference time domain method, the angular distribution curve of the composite scattering coefficient is obtained. The results show that the composite scattering coefficient oscillates with the scattering angle, and the scattering enhancement effect occurs in the mirror reflection direction. The influence of the root mean square and the correlation length on the fluctuation of soil surface, the soil moisture content, the scale and dielectric constant of combinatorial target on composite scattering coefficient is complex.

articleTitle: Tunable Second-Order Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface Based on Liquid Crystal
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this article, a design method for tunable LC-based FSS with a large tuning range and second-order band-pass frequency response is proposed. An LC-based bandpass FSS unit cell based on U-shaped strip is designed, which can provide a large tunable capacitance. A double-layer structure is proposed to obtain a second-order frequency response. Numerical simulation results show that the central operating frequency of the double-layer structure is tuned from 12.92 GHz to 11.76 GHz with a tunability of 9.4%. Moreover, the double-layer structure achieves second-order frequency response and angular stability of up to 60° for arbitrary LC states.

articleTitle: A 1x2 SIW Filtering Antenna Array with Tunable Radiation Nulls and High Gain
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A 1x2 substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filtering antenna array with tunable radiation nulls and high gain is proposed in this letter. A coplanar waveguide (CPW) power divider is used to excite the antenna array. The antenna element has two vertically integrated SIW cavities, containing a TE210 mode cavity and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{110}$</tex> mode cavity. Two slots are etched symmetrically on the top to couple to the TE110 mode cavity. A radiating slot is etched on the center of the TE110 mode cavity with a slight offset, which can divide the TE110 mode into two half- TE110 modes. By the integration of the two SIW cavities, two radiation nulls can be introduced at the two edges of the passband and achieve a high selectivity. Two radiation nulls can be adjusted independently. To enhance the realized gain, a grid-slotted patch is introduced above the radiating slot with an air layer. A prototype is fabricated and measured, showing that the antenna array has a bandwidth of 6.7% (from 4.74 GHz to 5.07 GHz) with a peak gain of 10.7 dBi.

articleTitle: Simulation of Spatiotemporal Variation of Evaporation Duct Height based on WRF Model with Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Base on the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model, an attempt to estimate the evaporation duct height was made in this paper. A suite of simulations was conducted along five routes in different regions of the South China Sea at different times. To verify the validation, we compared the simulated results with those measured by sensors on research vessels. The fitness between the simulated and measured values differs from one another due to the potential errors in the numerical and measured experiments. However, the simulated values consist well with the measured values in terms of the variation tendency under most of the cases, thus indicating that the WRF model can be used to estimate the occurrence of the evaporation duct and the simulated results are good references for a more accurate estimate using other methods.

articleTitle: Optimum Array Beamforming for Multiple Desired Signals via the Branch-and-Bound Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Optimum array beamforming for multiple desired signals via the branch-and-bound algorithm is presented in this paper. By maximizing the output signal-to-interference-noise ratio (SINR) and restricting the sidelobe level, adaptive anti-interference and low sidelobe level are realized. Furthermore, auxiliary variables are introduced to optimize the array response phase of the desired signal to reduce the pointing error of multiple desired signals. The overall design is formulated as a quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP) solved by the branch-and-bound algorithm. Simulation results are given to prove the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A method for dangerous liquid detection based on microwave technology
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A method for dangerous liquid detection based on microwave technology is proposed. According to the principle that various mediums have different microwave reflection characteristics, machine learning algorithm is used to classify the reflectivity of dangerous liquid and safe liquid, so as to realize the recognition of two kinds of liquids. In this paper, a pair of broadband microstrip antennas working in 0.5GHz ~ 3.5GHz are designed. Combined with the small scalar network analysis module and embedded system, a portable and miniaturized equipment for dangerous liquid detection has been developed. The experimental data show that this system has good repeatability and accuracy.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Rotation Scheme for Sequentially Rotated Circularly Polarized Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A fast algorithm for evaluating the cross-polarization characteristics of sequentially rotated circular polarization phased array is presented, which can be used to design a specific array rotation scheme and improve the cross-polarization suppression of wide-angle scanning phased array. Based on the parasitic cross-polarization array factor, a novel multilevel hierarchical array elements rotation scheme is designed to further reduce and disperse the cross-polarization peaks.

articleTitle: Evaporation Duct Inversion Using Radar Sea Clutter from Multiple Antenna Heights
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Atmospheric duct is an abnormal atmospheric structure in the marine environment, which has a significant impact on the performance of wireless communication equipment. Accurate monitoring of atmospheric duct height is of great significance for radio information system. The inversion of the atmospheric refractivity can be solved using easily measurable radar sea clutter. In this study, combined with the deep learning model optimized by particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, we propose a method of using radar sea clutter of multiple antenna heights to invert the atmospheric refractivity together. The method is applied to the inversion problem of atmospheric refractivity estimation, which verify the feasibility of using radar sea clutter of multiple antenna heights to invert the atmospheric refractivity together.

articleTitle: Variation of ionospheric slab thickness observations at Beijing
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ionospheric equivalent slab thickness (EST) is defined as the ratio of the total electron content (TEC) to the F2-layer peak electron density (NmF2) and it is a significant parameter representative of the ionosphere. Because it contains TEC information, EST is also a very useful parameter for satellite navigation and positioning. In this paper, a statistical study of EST at Beijing is presented based on GPS-TEC and ionosonde NmF2 data during the year 2010–2017. The results show that:(1) The diurnal variation of EST in different seasons show great differences. The EST during the daytime is greater than that during the night time in summer, while the EST during the nighttime is larger than that during the daytime in winter. The EST variations in equinox are between them, and its value during the daytime is slightly larger than that in the nighttime. (2) The pre-sunrise peak of EST only occurs in winter, and it gradually weakens with the increase of solar activity. (3) The overall variation of EST in high solar activity years and low solar activity years is consistent. With the increase of solar activity, the average slab thickness during the day and night continues to decrease, and the influence of solar activity on the plate thickness at night is more significant. (4) The morphological change of the disturbance index (DI) of EST during magnetic storms is basically the same as its geomagnetic quiet period. The EST changes during the daytime are more stable, and the EST disturbances are more intense during the night time.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a Broadband Absorber Using Resistive Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband absorber with high absorptivity is studied. The proposed structure is constructed from resistive frequency selective surface (FSS), PMI foam substrate and metal plate, such that the absorber exhibits above 90% absorption rate (equals to reflection coefficient lower than - 10dB) from 4.2 GHz to 17.6 GHz (covering C, X, and Ku bands). The novelty of the research lies in dedicating the selection principle of FSS units by calculating its ideal equivalent impedance characteristic according to transmission line theory. The analysis results show that when actual impedance of the loaded FSS conforms to the ideal region calculated by the above method, the absorption rate of the designed absorber can be guaranteed above 90% in corresponding frequency range.

articleTitle: Cascaded Network for Inversion of Electrical Conductivity in High Noise Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a cascade network is proposed to reconstruct the electrical conductivity through the electrical fields, presenting great computing efficiency and high accuracy. Benefit from the unsupervised U-net, the framework is applicable to high noise environment. Compared to traditional algorithms, the proposed physics informed neural networks (PINN) avoids meshing and iterative calculation. Therefore, it can be used to predict the conductivity distribution of objects with complex geometric shapes simultaneously. We believe this work will be benefit to fields related to electrical conductivity inversion problems.

articleTitle: Slot Matching for Substrate Integrated Waveguide Circularly Polarized Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, based on the research of substrate integrated waveguide slot antenna, a new method of terminal matching by short-circuit pin and matching slot is proposed, which changes the original traveling wave array into standing wave array, and realizes a new substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) circularly polarized slot array antenna. The radiation unit of the antenna is composed of two, including an inclined angle of 45, an “octagonal” slot pair structure. The coplanar waveguide is used to feed the antenna, and the dielectric substrate with a dielectric constant of 2.2 is selected. The structure of SIW is changed from traveling wave excitation to standing wave excitation. The simulated results of 8-element line array show that VSWR≤2 and axial ratio 3dB are achieved in the frequency band of 12.32GHz~12.84GHz, and the gain is 14.8dBi at 12.55GHz near the center frequency point.

articleTitle: Scattering of a shaped beam by a PEMC sphere
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The generalized Lorenz-Mie theory (GLMT) for a perfect electromagnetic conductor (PEMC) sphere illuminated by a laser beam of arbitrary shape is developed. After that, by expanding the incident and scattered waves using vector spherical wave functions (VSWFs) and considering the appropriate boundary conditions for the PEMC sphere, the relation between the expanded coefficients of the scattered fields and the beam shape coefficients (BSCs) of the incident beam is derived. The analytical expressions for the extinction, scattering and absorption efficiencies are gotten. According to the scattering characteristics of the PEMC, the scattering efficiency is divided into three parts that are co-polarized, cross-polarized, and interference components. The numerical results and discussions focus on the effects of polarization, size parameter, admittance, and beam parameters of Structural beam to the PEMC sphere. There is a discovery that the intensity and distribution of the total electric field intensity in the transverse yz plane depends on the incident beam and its polarization states. Besides, the scattering efficiency and its components have something to do with admittance parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> and dimensionless size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ka$</tex>, The results have promising applications in scattering, particle manipulation, optical trapping, and other related researches.

articleTitle: Realization of Multi-Modes Transmission by Time-Modulated Frequency Diverse Array
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Frequency diverse array (FDA) features a range-angle-dependent transmit beampattern, unlike phased array (PA). It demonstrates the potential for radio frequency stealth and anti-interference in the transmission process. In this paper, a multi-modes transmit beampattern is realized using a time-modulated frequency diverse array (TM-FDA). At the center frequency, the proposed array operates in FDA mode. Because the phase difference created by time modulation and frequency modulation cancel each other out at the upper sideband (m=1), the array operates in low sidelobe PA mode.

articleTitle: Analysis of Incident Field Polarization of A DDA Based Inverse Scattering Imaging Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of incident field polarization is analyzed, which is very important to an inverse scattering imaging algorithm for metal objects. In the imaging algorithm, the inverse scattering problem is converted to the inverse source problem according to the Equivalence Principle. The equivalent surface currents are considered to be numerous dipole moments, which is, namely, Discrete Dipole Approximation (DDA). And the inverse problem is solved by using Tikhonov Regularization. The simulation results indicate that a circularly polarized wave is superior for better imaging results.

articleTitle: Attenuation Characteristics of Terahertz Electromagnetic Wave in Nonuniform Plasma Slab
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The propagation of terahertz electromagnetic wave in plasma is discussed. The attenuation and phase shift for the unmagnetized plasma slab can be modeled. The proposed formulas show that wave attenuation and phase shift in unmagnetized plasma depend on the collision frequency, wave frequency, plasma density and plasma thickness. Comparisons of terahertz wave attenuations by proposed models, Z- Transform Finite Difference Time Domain (ZT FDTD) method, Jamison et al.'s formula and experimental results show good agreement in uniform unmagnetized plasma. In nonuniform unmagnetized plasma, obtained results of the wave attenuation by proposed formula are compared with those obtained by WKB method. It is found that terahertz wave attenuations by our model and WKB method show good agreement.

articleTitle: A Crossed-Ellipse Slot Antenna Design with Enhanced Bandwidth using Characterisitc Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a novel probe-fed slot antenna design with wide bandwidth characteristic. The antenna consists of two simple crossed-ellipse slots and two square stub slots. The antenna is designed using theory of characteristic mode (TCM). Wide bandwidth characteristic is achieved by combining two typical characteristic modes (CM). Through adjusting the stub slots position and parameters, the total impedance matching can be improved. Simulated results show that the 10dB return loss impedance bandwidth of the designed antenna covers 2.14GHz (4.33GHz~6.47GHz), which demonstrates the design process.

articleTitle: Composite Electromagnetic Probe with High Measurement Fidelity
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Electric-field probes and magnetic-field probes are generally used to measure electric field and magnetic field separately. The asynchrony of the measurement brings errors to our experiment. In this paper, a composite electromagnetic probe is proposed to eliminate unsynchronized errors. The proposed composite electromagnetic probe integrates electric-field probe and magnetic-field probe through multilayer folding layouts and minimizes the mutual interference through isolated vias. The proposed composite electromagnetic probe is manufactured by PCB process. Results demonstrate that the proposed composite electromagnetic probe is provided with the ability to simultaneously measure electromagnetic field, and the sensitivity difference between the proposed probe and the reference probe is within 3dB when the frequency is from 0.01GHzto 4GHz.

articleTitle: 128-Element Multibeam Antenna Array with Integrated Feeding Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an 8 × 16-element multibeam antenna array with integrated feeding networks is proposed. The whole antenna array comprises two groups of 8×8 dual-polarized bow-tie dipole antenna elements and 2×16 integrated Butler matrix feeding networks. By modifying the Butler matrix structures, four beam clusters are generated for 45° area coverage in the elevated plane in the measurement. The proposed multibeam antenna array adopts only 64 feeding ports, reducing the number of radio-frequency (RF) chains and downscaling the matrix dimension of baseband processing. Based on the communication performance analysis, the scheme with the proposed array achieves approaching channel capacity compared with the conventional scheme, but uses fewer RF chains, leading to promising usage for low-complex and low-cost massive multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) systems.

articleTitle: The CRLB Analysis for Target Localization Based on UAV Swarms
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms-based localization technology are gaining ever-increasing popularity in the field of electromagnetic spectrum due to their highly controllable maneuverability, on-demand coverage and line-of-sight (LoS) links. This paper considers a UAVs-based passive localization system where each UAV is equipped with a uniform circular array to locate the target by processing the received signals. To estimate the accuracy of the localization system, we give a detailed derivation of the Cramer-Rao low bound (CRLB) of the UAVs-based angle-of-arrival (AOA) measurements.

articleTitle: Measurements and the Structural Elements Impacts on The LPDA Assembly Line
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The impacts of the structural elements on the LPDA assembly line is investigated in this paper. Impedance influence was analyzed by simulation and calculation by EMSS FEKO. The simulation model was fabricated and measured by experiments on the practical circumstance. The results are useful for practical application.

articleTitle: The Es Influence of Shortwave Communication in summer
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Sporadic E (Es) is the irregular structure of ionosphere occurred in the layer E sporadically and Es is of frequency occurrence in China, the Influence of Es is very important to shortwave communication. The latitudinal variation of foEs occurrence numbers with critical frequencies greater than several special values is discussed. An examination of the oblique incidence data obtained between Xian and Kunming, the results show that Es reflection can often increase the maximum usable frequency, and the received field strength is closely related to the variations of the ionospheric Es and F layers, which is the result of their interaction. Based on the observation data of short wave link from Xi'an to Kunming, the prediction results of the Es model is qualitatively evaluated. The results show that the predicted value of field strength generally reflects the variation characteristics of Es field strength.

articleTitle: Channel Characterization for the mmWave Vehicle-to-Vehicle Communication in the See-through situation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) is crucial autonomous driving for its wide bandwidth and low I complex vehicular communication scenarios, the shad of large vehicles has a significant influence on th to-vehicle (V2V) channel. Thus, it is necessary to channel characteristics in this case. This paper uses a ray-tracing simulator to research the influence of the and the beam switching technology on the V2V c the “See-Through situation”. Finally, through the ext channel parameters, the characteristics of the V2V (the mmWave band are explored. Conclusions can project ideas for the design of the vehicular communication li

articleTitle: Output Characteristics Analysis of Typical 24-pulse Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The output characteristics of a typical 24-pulse rectifier is analyzed both by theoretical analysis and simulation method. The result shows the 24-pulse rectifier outputs a DC voltage with harmonics and the base frequency of the harmonics is 24 times of the AC power frequency.

articleTitle: A Novel Technique for Broadband Design and Optimization of HF Whip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Maximum transfer of power from the source to the antenna takes place when the impedances of the two are matched. To achieve this goal, loading and matching network are often utilized to make an antenna operate over a large range of frequencies. In this paper, the FEKO and ADS are invoked with a recently invented natural heuristic algorithm namely sparrow search algorithm (SSA) in MATLAB to realize the simulation and optimization of their components, showing promising prospect of this proposed technique for the integrated design of antenna. The design results presented show that the optimized antenna has voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) all less than 2 from 3MHz to 30MHz with an average value of 1.5 and achieved the broadband design of HF whip antenna, which indicates the good application and satisfactory performance in antenna practice.

articleTitle: Prediction of Low-Latitude L-Band Ionospheric Scintillation Based on in-Situ Satellite Observations
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To explore the feasibility of the method predicting the occurrence of low-latitude L-band ionospheric scintillation based on in-situ satellite observations of plasma irregularities in the ionospheric F -layer over the magnetic equator, the ion density data provided by the Ion Velocity Meter (IVM) of the C/NOFS (Communication/Navigation Outage Forecasting System) satellite and GPS ionospheric scintillation data recorded at Sanya (18.3°N, 109.6°E; geomagnetic: 8.33°N, 181.89°E) and Guilin (25.29°N, 110.33°E; geomagnetic: 15.29°N, 182.53°E) during October 2011 and 2012–2015 (i.e., during moderate and high solar activities) were analyzed in this study. The results show that the success rate of predicting the occurrence of L-band ionospheric scintillation at Sanya and Guilin based on the C/NOFS satellite's in-situ observations of ionospheric plasma irregularities during 18:30-24:00 LT (i.e., between sunset and midnight) was 81.22% and 34.27%, respectively. However, the success rate of predicting the occurrence of L-band ionospheric scintillation at Sanya and Guilin based on the C/NOFS satellite's in-situ observations of ionospheric plasma irregularities during 18:30-05:00 L T (i.e., between sunset and sunrise of the next day) was 67.03% and 29.03%, respectively. The results show that this prediction method has a higher prediction success rate for L-band ionospheric scintillation at lower latitudes such as Sanya. However, this prediction method is not practical for predicting L-band ionospheric scintillation at a place near the crest of the equatorial ionization anomaly (i.e., Guilin).

articleTitle: A Novel Folded Dipoles Circularly Polarized Quasi-Yagi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel planar folded dipoles quasi-Yagi antenna with a good function is proposed. It is based on a simple structure of two pairs of folded dipoles, planar magnetic walls, two mental via-holes, and a director. The working principle of the antenna is studied and analyzed. The magnetic walls are combined with folded dipoles to form a circularly polarized beam. By simulation and optimization, The impedance bandwidth (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|≤ - 10 dB) of about 4.8% (5.65-5.93 GHz) and a 3 dB AR bandwidth of about 13.3% (5.28-6.03 GHz) around the center frequency of 5.8 GHz is achieved, which indicates that the proposed antenna is suitable for the RFID system.

articleTitle: Regression analysis of refractivity gradient in the lowest 65m near the ground based on relevance vector machine algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The change of the atmospheric refractivity gradient near the ground is an important factor affecting the performance of the radio system, and then, the radio environment in the lowest 65m near the ground is mainly for radio waves propagation such as shipborne and microwave base stations. This paper uses the atmospheric radiosonde data from 2016 to 2020, selects parts of China, uses the relevance vector machine (RVM) algorithm to obtain the refractivity gradient in the lowest 65m near the ground, and compares it with the linear numerical model. The results show that the accuracy of the results obtained by using the RVM algorihm is higher and better than the numerical model, which can better serve the radio system equipment.

articleTitle: Terrain Modeling of Virtual Asteroids based on Poisson Faulting and its Electromagnetic Scattering
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: For the research of electromagnetic (EM) scattering from asteroids and the subsequent measurement in the anechoic chamber, the surface models of virtual asteroids are constructed based on Poisson faulting. The circular near-field-to-far-field transformation (CNFFFT) is applied to predict the far-field radar cross-sections (RCS) for spherical and ellipsoid asteroid models, where the near-field echo from the virtual asteroid is simulated by the Multilevel fast multipole method(MLFMM). The simulation results show that the proposed model can be used to reproduce the near-field measurement data of virtual asteroids in the anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Research on Raindrop Spectrum Inversion Based on t-min Cumulative Rainfall Rate Time Series
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Rainfall attenuation is an important factor that affects and restricts 5G millimeter wave mobile communications. However, evaluating the propagation effect in the rainfall environment requires analyzing the statistical characteristics of the 1-min cumulative rainfall rate, but directly obtaining the 1-min cumulative rainfall rate data will consume a lot of manpower and material resources. Therefore, it is of great significance to convert t-min cumulative rainfall rate to 1-min cumulative rainfall rate. At the same time, because the raindrop spectrum contains the distribution characteristics of the cumulative rainfall rate, the inversion of the raindrop spectrum based on the cumulative rainfall rate time series is a key step to achieve the conversion of the rainfall rate. In this paper, based on the collected 10-min and 1-min cumulative rainfall rate time series, the raindrop particle diameter and sedimentation velocity are classified and quantified, so as to realize the inversion of the raindrop spectrum. The research results show that the distribution of rainfall particle number density can reflect the evolution characteristics and volatility of the cumulative rainfall rate, and is an important factor influencing the change of the rainfall rate at different cumulative times.

articleTitle: Vortex Splitting of the Bessel-Gaussian Beam in Atmospheric Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on multi-phase screen method, an atmospheric turbulence transmission link of 1500 meters can be decomposed sufficiently into a series of 150 weak thin turbulence phase screens with the same interval, and the transmission model of orbital angular moment (OAM) mode carried by a Bessel Gaussian beam in atmospheric turbulence was developed and employed to analyze the turbulence induced vortex splitting of OAM modes. OAM modes with different topological charges have different vortex splitting velocity in the atmospheric turbulence, it can be enhanced with the increase in Reynolds number.

articleTitle: Stimulated electromagnetic emission model of Plasma wake of a hypersonic aerocraft
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the stimulated electromagnetic emission spectrum (SEE) of the hypersonic aerocraft wake is analyzed by using Zakharov model. In order to obtain the spectrum of SEE, the Zakharov equation is solved in the frequency domain by Fourier transform, which not only speeds up the computational efficiency, but also avoids the complex calculation in the time domain. In some numerical simulations, it is indicated that the SEE spectrum can be obtained only when the plasma frequency meets the parametric instability. The SEE spectrum shows that when the electromagnetic excitation phenomenon occurs, there will be electromagnetic wave with a frequency similar to the plasma frequency. The SEE spectrum characteristics excited at different wakes can be used as the basis to judge the position and state of aerocraft. This method may provide a new idea for further exploring the hypersonic aerocraft detection by using stimulated radiation of the plasma wake.

articleTitle: Investigation on Effect from variational Electromagnetic Parameters of absorbing patch for RCS of Almond model
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The RCS of the almond model which was affected by the change from electromagnetic parameters (ε and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu)$</tex> of the absorbing patch was researched, and the moment method was utilized. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex> andμ of the absorbing patch can be measured and the values were assumed to vary with equal difference in the interval of 5%~30%, the measured values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex> worked as variable which were used to calculate the RCS of the almond model with the different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex> of the patch. Here, two almond model RCS were obtained, one is circumferential RCS which generated by the gradient of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex> of absorbing patch, and the other Radar Cross-Section (RCS) generated by the known electromagnetic parameter measurements. Comparing the two RCS mentioned above, the calculated results show that for the HH polarization, the undulation values of the almond model RCS vary within 0.4dB when the real part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex> of the absorbing patch vary within 5%-30% at 10GHz, and for the VV polarization, the undulation values changes within 2.5 dB, Moreover, the polar differences of both polarizations decrease with the increase of the real part of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>, in both polarization modes, the polar RCS is sensitive to the variation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>, and the VV polarization is much more sensitive than the HH polarization.

articleTitle: A Novel Scattering Path Probability Model for UAV-to-Ground Channels
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The scattering propagation is inevitable and important in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications, and a novel scattering path probability model for UAV-to-ground (U2G) channels is proposed in this paper. In this model, we divide buildings into three categories (i.e., scattering buildings, front buildings, and behind buildings), and discuss the effect of different buildings on the scattering path probability. By considering the factors, i.e., building height distribution, building width, and transceivers heights, the proposed model is suitable for different communication distances and heights. Moreover, the simulation results show that the probability model has good consistent with the ray-tracing (RT) simulation method, which verifies the effectiveness of proposed model.

articleTitle: A Single-Port Multi-Band Horizontal Omni-directional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a single-port multi-band horizontal omni-directional antenna for VHF/UHF band is proposed, which mainly consists of a sleeve dipole and an air-filled coaxial feeding network. The sleeve dipole achieves good radiation characteristics in the horizontal direction of the antenna in the designed four frequency bands. The gradual air-filled coaxial feeding network achieves better standing wave ratio characteristics in the designed four frequency bands. The antenna can reach voltage standing wave ratio less than 2.5 in the range of band f1:265MHz-305MHz, f2:560MHz-620MHz, f3:700MHz-860MHz, f4:980MHz-1045MHz. The ovality of the antenna in the horizontal direction is less than 0.5dB. The antenna operating bandwidth gain is greater than 1.2dBi, with a maximum gain of 5.9dBi. The measured results show that the antenna has good horizontal omnidirectional radiation characteristics in the designed four frequency bands, which is in good agreement with the simulation.

articleTitle: An Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm and Its Application on Inverse Scattering Problem
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is a stochastic optimization algorithm which imitates the predation of whale for searching their preies. Due to its search efficiency, WOA has been broadly utilized to solve sundry kinds of engineering problems. However, the traditional WOA is often trapped into local optima while solving highly ill-posed inverse problems. Therefore, a new improved WOA is proposed by modifying the original searching path. According to the different search mechanisms of the algorithm, the search path is combined and optimized in order to get better constrain for the search direction and enable the search towards the global optimum. One reconstruction of scatterer permittivity test is given to prove the efficiency of improved WOA. As expected, the proposed IWOA achieves better solutions compared with traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: Thermoacoustic imaging Using Back Projection Based on Deconvolution
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Thermoacoustic imaging (TAI) is a non-ionizing, high-contrast and high-resolution modality promising for diversified biomedical applications. The resolution of the reconstructed image by traditional imaging algorithm, such as back-projection (BP), is intrinsically dependent on the input microwave pulse width. In this work, it is demonstrated that the reconstructed images based on BP combined with GCV, that can reconstruct images with high quality, is largely independent on the microwave pulse width.

articleTitle: Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm to Optimize Millimeter Wave Channel Modeling of RBF Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper studies the radial basis function (RBF) neural network optimized by the improved particle swarm optimization (PSO). This neural network is used for channel modeling in complex office environments and compared with the channel modeling results of the basic RBFNN. Predicted and analyzed the path loss, delay spread and power angle distribution of the wireless channel in a 60 GHz indoor office environment. The comparison of multiple sets of parameters shows that the algorithm improves the prediction accuracy of RBFNN and speeds up its convergence better.

articleTitle: Microstrip Transducer Based on Pure Water for Ultra-Wideband Electromagnetic Pulse Measurement
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a detail design of a novel microstrip transducer for the measurement of ultra-wideband electromagnetic pulses (UWB-EMP). The transducer is based on two microstrip structures, which are set on the upper and lower surfaces of a shielding box composed of the ground planes of the microstrip structures. Pure water with high permittivity is used as the dielectric substrate to extend the time window obviously. By the subtraction operation of two outputs from the two microstrip structures, the interferences feeding into the transducer in common mode can be eliminated effectively. The proposed transducer has a wide bandwidth of about 3.5 GHz, and a long time window of 12.4 ns. Within the time window, the transducer can directly recover the incident field with high fidelity, which is a good candidate for the design of UWB-EMP measurement system.

articleTitle: Design of Database System for Strong Electromagnetic Radiation Effect
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aircraft or ships are often interfered by strong electromagnetic radiation during navigation, which always causes seriously damage to their electronic equipment. Quantitative analysis of these effect is essential to the design of the electronic system. In the past decades, case by case analysis has been reported in many publications. With the rapid progress of big data and machine learning algorithms, it is possible to adopt these new technologies to analyze this problem. Data is the key in big data technology, however, there is no database design has been reported for strong electromagnetic radiation effect data. To serve this problem, this paper proposes a design scheme of strong electromagnetic radiation effect database system based on relational database. In this system, the software part adopts modular design to improve the flexibility and scalability of the system; the authentication module and log module are introduced to ensure the security and stability of the database; the machine learning module is designed to provide the ability of system data analysis, and finally a relatively complete database system is developed for strong electromagnetic radiation effect.

articleTitle: A New Relationship between the Nakagami “m-coefficient” and the S4 Index for more accurately Describing the Fading Distribution of Ionospheric Scintillation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The radio system designers have to be aware of the statistical characteristics of the instantaneous variation of signal amplitudes in order to develop possible mitigation strategies. The applicable scopes of the Nakagami distribution and the Rayleigh distribution are analyzed based on the observations of the amplitude scintillations recorded in the low-latitude of China. It’ concluded that the scintillation amplitude is more likely to obey the Rayleigh distribution when the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> index is greater than 0.7. By the variation of “m-coefficient”, the Nakagami distribution could represent the Rayleigh distribution. Therefore, a new relationship between the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> index and the “m-coefficient” of the Nakagami distribution is put forward, which can much better describe the fading distribution of amplitude scintillations in the whole range of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and also is simple enough for the engineering application.

articleTitle: Study on Slanted grooves SPR Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Surface plasma resonance (SPR) sensor with a type of slanted grooves metal grating structure based on the Otto prism-coupling is proposed and the equivalent relationship of the dispersion relation between the slanted and rectangular groove is established, which based on the resonance frequency obtained by numerical simulations. The results show that the refractive index of the sucrose solution is range from 1.33 to 1.37 when the concentration is lower than 25%, the sensing sensitivity is up to 4.94THz/RIU. The structure possesses the advantages of simple operation, low cost and high sensitivity, which has considerable application prospects in liquid sensing detection.

articleTitle: Hybrid precoding in Massive Antenna Multi-User System with Modified Hybrid Connected Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new hybrid precoding architecture is proposed for massive antenna multi-user system. The proposed architecture is an extension of the hybrid connected structure (HCS), which can realize a good tradeoff between spectral efficiency and hardware cost by adjusting the number of sub-arrays. Based on the proposed architecture, the hybrid precoding matrix is optimized by using the alternating optimization (AO) and Riemannian conjugate gradient (RCG) algorithm. The proposed scheme is evaluated based on real measured channels at 28GHz in a railway station. Simulation results show that the achievable sum rate of proposed scheme is very close to that of the optimal full-digital precoding scheme. In addition, the achievable sum rate of the proposed scheme is higher than that of the existing schemes when the number of sub-arrays takes different values.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna with Pattern Diversity
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a low profile circularly polarized antenna which use an antiphase and in-phase hybrid feed network to realize its pattern diversity property. The antenna contains two square ring patches as radiators that are excited by two coupling slots on the ground, when the two radiators are excited by two antiphase signals, the antenna realizes its broadside pattern mode, when the two radiators are excited by two in-phase signals, the antenna can radiate dual beam. Thus, we use a hybrid feed network to produce two antiphase signals or two in-phase signals, the thickness of the antenna is only 0.045λ0 (λ0 is the free-space wavelength of the center frequency). Besides, a perturbation is introduced by the radiator to achieve circularly polarized radiation. The simulation results show the coincident operating bandwidth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert < 10\text{dB}$</tex> and AR<3dB) is 1.7% (3.52-3.58GHz).

articleTitle: Scattering from an Object above Flat Surfaces Using the Hybrid Iterative High Frequency Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid method is studied for EM scattering from a 3D object above a 2D flat surface. The method is a hybrid method of high frequency physical optics algorithm(PO) and PO itself. We derived the direct scattering field that can be used for both object and flat surface, and the coupling field between them. Finally, the method is utilized to calculate the difference scattering d-RCS of different objects above a flat surface, and compare it with MLFMM in commercial software. The verification results show that our method has high accuracy

articleTitle: The ionospheric effects during the Solar Eclipse on May 12, 2012
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on observed data from the network of long-running ionospheric observation sites, we analyzed the ionospheric effect of D-layer and F-layer about the Eclipse on May 12, 2012 within China. The results indicated that the ionospheric effect is more obvious at middle and low latitudes. The critical frequency of F2-layer(foF2) in QingDao and XinXiang stations is higher than referenced value, and the hight of F2-layer bottom is raised, the observed data (foF2) in GuangZhou station showed obvious photochemical effect, that is “Sunrise delay”.

articleTitle: Design of Active Absorptive/Transmissive Frequency Selective Surface Based on PIN Diode and Varactor
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An active absorptive/transmissive frequency selective surface (ATFSS) based on PIN diode and varactor is proposed in this paper. It includes lossy FSS, air layer and bandpass FSS from top to bottom. The structure can switch between wave absorption and wave transmission states at 2.65GHz, and realize the effective wave absorption on both sides of the central band. In the transmission state, the insertion loss is only 0.39dB at 2.65GHz, and the absorption rate is more than 80% in 1.64GHz-2.39GHz and 2.99GHz-5.97GHz. While in the absorption state, the absorption rate is more than 80% from 1.76GHz to 6.70GHz. It can be used for the antenna stealth, which reduce the out-of-band radar cross section (RCS) when the antenna is working, and realize the full band stealth when the antenna is silent.

articleTitle: A C-band Multi Beam Quasi-Yagi Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A multi beam antenna based on switch selection is proposed. the antenna is composed of Single Pole Eight Throw switch and eight 1x4 Quasi-Yagi array antennas. The 1x4 Quasi-Yagi array antenna is selected because of its low-cost advantage. The gain of the 1x4 Quasi-Yagi array antenna is about 15dBi, the beam width is about 45 degrees in E-plane, eight 1x4 Quasi-Yagi array antennas realize the 360 degrees coverage in azimuth direction. The multi beam antenna working state can be selected by controlling code according to the communication target direction. The control code is composed of 3 bit “0” or “1” from “000” to “111” correspond to antenna number 1 to 8. Thus, the multi target communication is realized by controlling switch state.

articleTitle: CORDIC-Based Hardware Twin Method for Loo and Corazza Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Digital channel twin is a useful tool to evaluate the physical or link level performance in satellite communication scenario. In this paper, a generical architecture for large-scale fading channel is developed. On this basis, a CORDIC-based generator has been designed for improving the efficiency of hardware for channel twin. For generating a single large-scale fading channel, the latency is cut by 62.5% over the classical CORDIC method for 16-bit data width, the hardware resource is reduced from 8.43% to 5.58% over the LUT method. Hardware generated results have shown that the statistical properties of proposed generation method, PDF consistent well with the theoretical ones.

articleTitle: Finite Period Effect of the Metamaterials Made of Multilayered Dielectrics on the Resonant Characteristics of a Rectangular Waveguide Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The finite period effect (FPR) of the metamaterials made of multilayered dielectrics (MDs) is numerically studied on the resonant characteristics of a rectangular waveguide resonator (RWR). The unit cell for the MD metamaterials includes two kinds of dielectrics as type-A and type-B with different permittivity values. One RWR is considered to be loaded with such MDs. These MD metamaterials are supposed with different periods but maintain the same occupation ratio. It is observed that both of the resonant frequency and quality-factor vary with the period of the MDs due to the FPR. Interestingly when the period is very small, the resonant characteristics of the RWR are approaching to that filled with a hypothetic material with the average permittivity of the type-A and type-B dielectrics.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Radiation Evaluation Methods for Mobile Base Stations Co-located with High Voltage Transmission Towers
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to clarify the electromagnetic radiation effects of mobile base stations installed on high-voltage transmission towers on electric power transportation inspectors, the electromagnetic field distribution characteristics of mobile base stations co-located with high voltage transmission towers were measured and studied. This paper uses specific absorption ratio (SAR) to evaluate human exposure in the scenario of mobile base stations co-located with high voltage transmission towers, and proposes a new physical area-based human exposure evaluation method, then provide safety guarantee and parameter reference for transportation and inspection personnel during daily operations.

articleTitle: Influence of Ship Swaying motion on performance of Maritime Laser Communications in the Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the Pierson-Moskowitz (PM) spectrum, the ship swaying motion model of vessels under different sea-states and sailing speeds conditions was developed and employed to analyze the effects of the ship swaying-induced pointing errors on outage probability of laser communications systems operated in the maritime turbulence, the influences of the atmospheric turbulence and visibility were also considered here. Results indicated that ship swaying-induced pointing errors became severe with the increase in offshore wind speed and sailing angle and the decrease in sailing speed, thereby inhibiting the performance of communication systems. The increase of turbulence strength and the decrease of visibility reduced the performance of the communication system.

articleTitle: A Digital-Analog Hybrid Antenna Array with 2-bit Time-Modulator
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A digital-analog hybrid antenna array is proposed and verified with 2-bit time-modulators. Under different configurations, the antenna array can be set as phased array for transmitting and digital array for receiving. Its principle is as follows. For the transmitting, the 2-bit time-modulators concentrate most power to the first harmonic with equivalent single sideband (SSB) modulation. The phase differences among all the elements are controlled by added modulation sequences. For the receiving, the power of received signal is distributed to harmonics under periodic phase modulation. Then the array manifold is estimated from generated harmonics, and the direction of arrival (DOA) can be acquired by spatial spectrum estimation. The proposed structure breaks down the boundary between the analog array and digital array. Numeric simulations and experiments are provided to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: An Effective Method for Obtaining the Input Impedance of Balanced Broadband Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to obtain the input impedance of balanced broadband dipole antenna, this paper uses three auxiliary impedances and the impedance transformation of the transmission line converter, and then establishes equations to deduce the relative expression of network parameters of the transmission line converter. According to network parameters of the transmission line converter and the input impedance of balanced broadband dipole antenna, the original input impedance of balanced symmetric dipole antenna is calculated, which provides the possibility for the subsequent accurate design of antenna matching network. Finally, two design examples are provided to verify the correctness of the derived relative expression of converter network parameters through a 450 Ω nominal impedance; By comparing the original input impedance of a 3MHz~30MHz short wave symmetric broadband dipole antenna, the software simulation results are in good agreement with the calculation results using the converter network parameter method, which verifies the effectiveness of calculating the input impedance of balanced broadband dipole antenna in this paper.

articleTitle: Challenging the Extremely High Selectivity Band Notch with Fragment - Type Structures
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Due to the high selectivity is critical for filtering antenna designs, this work devotes itself to challenge the remarkably roll-off characteristics by searching for the best fragment-type patterns etched on a UWB monopole radiator.

articleTitle: The Impact of Link-Delay Difference on RTS MIMO OTA Measurement
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Multiple input and multiple-output (MIMO) has been one of the essential techniques for the long-term evaluation (L TE) wireless terminals and the fifth generation (5G) wireless systems. MIMO over the air (OTA) measurement for the receiver sensitivity evaluation plays a significate role in research and development for wireless equipment. To perform MIMO measurement, the radiated two-stage (RTS) is developed for both 2D and 3D throughput tests with high accuracy and low cost. In OT A measurement, the engineers try their best to reduce the measurement uncertainties, as well as improve the measurement reliability and repeatability. Hence, the uncertainty caused by the link-delay difference, which has been ignored in the OT A test, is analyzed herein. In this paper, the relationship between the link-delay difference and the isolation of MIMO antennas is investigated and qualified. The proposed suggestions could reduce the uncertainty of MIMO throughput measurement when designing a MIMO anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Analysis of the influence of the multiple scattering effect on millimeter-wave cirrus measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: To study the role of the multiple scattering effect of ice particles when retrieving the microphysical parameters of cirrus using millimeter-wave radar, spherical and non-spherical ice particles' models with gamma size distributions were first established. Then, the XFDTD (X Finite Difference Time Domain) software, GMM (Generalized Multi-particle Mie) and simple addition method were used to calculate the radar cross section(RCS) values for the ice particle models at 94 GHz. Therefore, multiple scattering effects must be considered in practical meteorological detection.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of the Electron Density of Physical Model and Medium Frequency Radar in Kunming
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper study the diurnal variations of electron density in the D regions of the ionosphere in the spring, summer, autumn and winter in the low years of solar activity in Kunming due to the Kunming medium frequency (MF) radar observation data in 2009. It is found electron density in spring and autumn are slightly higher than that in summer and winter. We further compare with the existing physical model and the international ionosphere reference 2016 (IRI-2016) model. The results show that the diurnal variations of electron density have basically the same changing based on the radar data and the model data trends, especially during 10:00-16:00. But there is a difference in magnitude of the electron density value. In addition, radar data and physical models supplement the shortage of IRI model to a certain extent. They well describe the characteristics of the diurnal variation of electron density and its variation with height in the D regions of the ionosphere

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Channel Modeling and Analysis of Electromagnetic Field for WiFi
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As wireless networks become more and more popular, people are paying more attention to the question of whether WiFi signals are harmful to the human body. In this paper, a full 3D propagation model based on ray tracing and uniform diffraction theory is used to predict the electromagnetic radiation environment of indoor 2.4 GHz WiFi signals. The electromagnetic distribution of the ground and the wall of office in the study area are effectively calculated. The research content can provide a basis for further wireless channel modeling and electromagnetic situation research.

articleTitle: Fast Beamforming Algorithm For Large-Scale Irregular Array
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A fast beamforming method for large irregular arrays is proposed in this paper. The number of elements of spaceborne phased array is usually very large, which contains thousands of elements. Moreover, the demand for special beamforming of spaceborne large-scale phased array is also increasing. On the other hand, in order to reduce the number of array elements due to the complexity of equipment, sparse array or irregular array is usually used. The fast calculation of special beamforming for large-scale irregular arrays is an urgent problem to be solved. In this paper, the transmitting and receiving beams of a typical irregular array (512 elements) are designed respectively. Different beamforming schemes are adopted in different scenarios, and the amplitude and phase weights of each array element are solved quickly and accurately, so as to provide a solution for fast beamforming of large-scale irregular array.

articleTitle: 77GHz CPWG-feed Antenna Array for Applications of Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: As one of the important components of millimeter-wave imaging radar, antennas must have good performance, wide bandwidth, lower sidelobes, high-gain, low profile and easy to be integrated with RF front-end characteristics. This article presents design of CPWG-feed microstrip antenna array with lower sidelobe level at the operating frequency of 77GHz which can be applicated in MIMO imaging radar. According to the measurement results, radiation in sidelobes level of both E-plane and H-plane are below -15dB, the gain of the radiation is larger than 21dBi at the operating frequency 77GHz, the beamwidth of E-plane is 13.4degree, H-plane is 12.5degree. The feeding impedance is 50ohm CPWG transmission line, and frequency band width is larger than 5GHz.

articleTitle: A High Gain Planar End-Fire Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a planar end-fire circularly polarized (CP) antenna with high gain is investigated. The proposed antenna which consists of two V-shaped dipoles and substrate integrate waveguide (SIW), is Yagi and complementary structure. To obtain high gain, some parameters of the antenna are researched and analyzed. Simulated results indicate that the impedance bandwidth (12.42<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and 3-dB axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth (16.97%) of the proposed antenna, its gain can reach up to 6.45 dBic.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Calibration Algorithm for Cylindrical Conformal Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low gain, high sidelobe and beam orientation offset caused by channel error, an automatic calibration algorithm for cylindrical conformal phased array antenna is designed. Different from the traditional algorithm, this algorithm is divided into receiving calibration and transmitting calibration. It can calibrate the Intermediate Frequency (IF) channel and Radio Frequency (RF) channel of the antenna system at the same time, and avoid the error caused by the step calibration. The calibration coefficient can be obtained from the average value of several sampling points, while keeping the consistency of amplitude and phase. It can be observed that the accuracy of the calibration algorithm is 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−10</sup>without noise and 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>when adding 20 dB White Gaussian Noise.

articleTitle: An Effective Method for Analyzing the Transient Response of Transmission Line With Frequency-Dependent Network
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an effective method of combining the matrix pencil method (MPM) and piecewise linear recursive convolution (PLRC) is proposed to perform the transient response analysis of the transmission line (TL) containing the frequency-dependent network (FDN). Firstly, the admittances of the FDN at the sampling frequencies are obtained by calculation or measurement. Then, the corresponding poles and residues are generated by using MPM to process the sampled admittance data and introduced into the current expression in PLRC. Further, by substituting the current formula into the expression between the voltage and current at the connection point of the TL and FDN, the transient response analysis of the TL system can be realized. Finally, the availability and correctness of the proposed method is verified by two numerical examples.

articleTitle: A Printed Hepta-Band Antenna for Small Cell Phone
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A printed hepta-band antenna for small cell phone is presented. The antenna is mainly composed of a T-shaped branch and a coupled parasitic ground branch. The T-branch is connected with the microstrip transmission line, yielding three resonant points at about 1700 MHz, 2250 MHz and 3000 MHz Moreover, two additional resonant points contributed by the parasitic ground branch allow the proposed antenna to cover seven bands for 2G/3G/4G applications. The merit of the proposed antenna is that no matching network is required, which makes it cost-effective. The measurement and simulation results of the proposed antenna are almost consistent.

articleTitle: A metamaterial absorber based on interdigital stepped resonant structure
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A metamaterial absorber based on the interdigital stepped resonant structure is proposed. For transverse magnetic (TM) incidence, the proposed structure has a minimum absorption of 90% with the incident angle ups to 85°. Because of its effective absorption over a wide range of incidence angles, the proposed structure can be used to block or counteract unnecessary electromagnetic effects in the low frequency band.

articleTitle: Scattering Echoes Modeling of UAV Swarm in Flight based on Vector Superposition
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A method to obtain the echoes of UAV swarm from the echoes of a single UAV is presented by vector superposition. UAV swarm can be regarded as an extended target. Therefore, the echoes of UAV swarm can be simulated by the vector superposition which is generally applied in extended target. The echo characteristics of two different UAV swarms are studied in time domain. The research work of this paper will help to further obtain the relevant characteristics of UAV swarms by coherent accumulation.

articleTitle: Extraction and Analysis of Equivalent Circuit Parameters of Lossy Capacitive Patch Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a method to extract the equivalent circuit parameters of capacitive lossy patch elements by combining the full-wave simulated results and qualitative equivalent circuit analysis. A frequency selective surface (FSS) with the element of lossy patch can be equivalent to a series RC (resistor and capacitor) circuit parallel in the transmission lines. This paper has revealed the principle of how the structural parameters affect the equivalent circuit parameters. Besides, the parasitic inductor of the lossy capacitive patch (LCP) elements is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Development of photoelectric edge sensors for closed-loop active reflectors
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: With increasing demands on large-area deep surveys of submillimeter galaxies, a 60-meter single dish submillimeter telescope has been recently proposed [1]. In order to maintain a high level of surface accuracy for the 60-meter main reflector under the high-altitude site conditions, a high-performance closed-loop active surface control technology based on optoelectronic edge sensors has been developed. Two sensor types have been proposed. The first sensor is composed of a laser diode(LD) and a position sensing sensor (PSD), and the sensor error after nonlinear calibration is less than 0.6µm. The second sensor is composed of a LED and a CMOS with position accuracy and repeatability error better than 0.02 pixel completely(0.13µm), By placing the edge sensors across the gaps between adjacent composite panels, six-DOF panel position parameters can be determined with 2 edge sensors installed on each gap. Numerical simulation results show that such a sensor network achieves an overall surface measurement accuracy of 15µm with single sensor noise of 0.5µm, showing good application potential in real-time monitoring and maintenance of surface figure for large submillimeter telescopes.

articleTitle: Design of Ku Band Phased Array Antenna for Synthetic Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A Ku band phased array antenna with 192-elements which is applied to Synthetic aperture radar is presented in this paper. An E-type microstrip patch antenna with broadband characteristics is designed as an array element. An irregular array layout of the phased array antenna is constructed, which can not only obtain high gain and keep the output power of the T/R module but also suppress the sidelobe of the transmitting beam and receiving beam in both azimuth and range directions. Meanwhile, since the digital attenuator is not used, the cost of phased array antenna is reduced.

articleTitle: A Novel Signal Conditioning Circuit for Electromagnetic Field Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel signal conditioning circuit for electromagnetic field detection is presented in this paper. The signal conditioning circuit can realize big dynamic range and high sensitivity detection of the weak signal. The signal conditioning circuit consists of antenna, adjustable bandwidth filter, adjustable gain amplifier, AD converter, etc. All the composition ensures the performance of the field probe.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Power Meter using Perfect Absorber via a Multi-layer Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A millimeter-wave power meter using a perfect absorber is designed. The power sensor consisted of a highly-doped silicon absorption substrate with a multi-layer anti-reflection structure, is fabricated with the graded-index mechanism. Using differently doped silicon wafers can tune the transmissivity of each layer, which brings conductivity changing gradually from 1S/m to 4000S/m. The EM simulation results demonstrate that absorption above 99% can be achieved from 75GHz to 220GHz.

articleTitle: Parabolic-equation based study of atmospheric turbulent effects on evaporation duct radio wave propagation
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Evaporation duct is an imporatn factor affecting the near sea surface radio wave propgation. Based on the atmospheric boundary turbulence theory and the parabolic wave equation, the propagation model considing the randomized refractivity is proposed. The numerical simulation compared the influence of theturbulence the results shaows that accounting for the physical mechanism of the atmosphere turbulence is s an important factor. It can reduce the propagation distance of radar wave propagation and affect the detection probability and range of radar to the tarbet beyond the horizon.

articleTitle: Millimeters Wave Radar for Wireless Intelligent Sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Among various sensing technologies, millimeters wave radar sensing is most likely to meet the complex and advanced sensing needs required to realize the vision of a smart world. This article provides a systematic and complete definition of wireless intelligent sensing, which integrates intelligence into the entire wireless sensing system, which is denoted as WISe. The entire WISe framework includes electromagnetic waves transceiver equipment, signal processing algorithms, data analysis software, and intelligent applications. Intelligence is achieved by using various intelligent resources in all parts from hardware to software. WISe is application-driven and dominated; therefore, the details of WISe are described and illustrated through four example applications of healthcare, smart toilets, pet monitoring, and in-cabin monitoring of smart vehicles.

articleTitle: 3-D Hybrid Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD)/ Wave Equation Finite Element Time-Domain (WE-FETD) Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a new 3-D hybrid finite-difference time-domain (FDTD)/wave equation finite element time-domain (WE-FETD) method is proposed. Different from previous methods using first order Maxwell's curl equations, the FETD region in this method is wave-equation-based. The method forms a new hybrid FDTD/SETD/FETD framework. At the interface of different region, it employs the Discontinuous Galerkin method to couple the neighboring regions.

articleTitle: Subgridding FDTD Modeling of Ground Penetrating Radar Applied with Unconditionally Stable Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Traditional subgridding finite difference time-domain (FDTD) method can greatly save computation time and memory consumption. However, the limits of the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) stability condition still be met. In this paper, an explicit unconditionally stable technique is introduced into the subgridding FDTD approach and applied in the ground penetrating radar (GPR) modeling. Thus, a relatively large and unified time step can be used in coarse and fine grids, which breaks through the method's CFL condition limit.

articleTitle: On the phased array antenna radiation fields computational model based on the periodic boundary
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The phased array antenna radiation fields computational model based on the periodic boundary is constructed.
