The model takes advantage of the character of periodic arrange of elements of antenna and periodic distribution of radiation fields of antenna elements. The method is high efficient and accurate.

articleTitle: Application of Target Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics in Short-Range Dynamic Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In view of the way that radio fuse probe target for echo information with dynamic scanning detection in the scene of near-field, this paper designed an experiment of the application scheme, which the scheme used radar to image electromagnetic scattering from a target of interest, the complex echo signals in the detection results were divided according to the time series and the RCS mean value of the corresponding region was calibrated, thus the time-resolved/part-resolved target information can be used in the design and verification of near-field detector, providing a new method for the application of target characteristic information in the process of short-range dynamic detection.

articleTitle: Combination algorithm of long wave communication interference in complex electromagnetic environment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the process of long-wave communication signal propagation, the signal is susceptible to the interference of atmospheric noise in the channel and electromagnetic radiation generated by artificial equipment, especially the atmospheric noise interference has non-Gaussian and non-stationary statistical characteristics. The complex electromagnetic environment brings great uncertainty to the stable and reliable operation of the system. The traditional Window function algorithm based on Fourier transform can effectively filter out the out-of-band noise of the main frequency of long-wave signals, but it cannot filter out the in-band noise. To solve this problem, this paper designs an adaptive combination algorithm based on NLMS and leakyLMS algorithm on the basis of window function filter to suppress the in-band interference noise.

articleTitle: Decoupling of Dual-Polarized 5G Base Station Antenna Using Back Cavities
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A dual-polarization base station antenna array based on a back cavity and metal plate decoupling structure is introduced. There are two crossed dipoles on the upper surface of the horizontal dielectric plate to achieve ±45° polarizations. Each balun has an FR4 vertical substrate with Γ feeders transformer and slotted metal ground on the back. This antenna operates in C band (3.3-3.8 GHz) with VSWR < 1.5, the isolation between the two polarized ports is better than 27 dB. With the decoupling structure, the co-polarized coupling between two elements is improved by at least 9.5 dB, and the cross-polarized coupling between two elements is improved by up to 2 dB, and the gain is increased by 0.2 dBi in the working frequency band.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Scattering from the Surface of Transverse Dunes Using FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The height fluctuation of the surface of transverse dunes is simulated by exponential distribution and Monte Carlo method. Based on the general formula of soil moisture and die-lectric constant proposed by Herkelrath, the dielectric constant of sandy soil is calculated. FDTD method is used to study the influences of different factors on scattering coefficient. The re-sults show that the top height of sand dune, the horizontal distance between the bottom of windward slope and the top of sand dune, the incident wave frequency, the incident angle and the root mean square of height fluctuation have great influence on the scattering coefficient. The horizontal distance from the bot-tom to the top of leeward slope has a complex effect on the scat-tering coefficient.

articleTitle: Propagation loss of radio wave in atmospheric duct environment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the composition of radio wave propagation loss in atmospheric duct environment is analyzed. Based on the parabolic equation method, the transmission loss of atmospheric waveguide under given parameters is calculated by using Fourier distribution algorithm, and its accuracy is verified by comparing with the radar transmission loss measured in actual environment. The research in this paper has important reference value for evaluating radar detection performance and optimizing waveguide detection parameters.

articleTitle: Groove Gap Waveguide Leaky Wave Antenna with Fixed Frequency and Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a fixed-frequency beam-scanning leaky wave antenna (LWA) based on groove gap waveguide (GGW) technology is presented. The whole structure can be divided into GGW and radiating units. The radiating units are composed of 67 slot-coupled patch antennas, and the working state of each patch antenna is controlled by a PIN diode. A periodic reconfigurable method is adopted to realize the fixed frequency beam scanning characteristics of the antenna. Through full-wave simulation, it is found that the proposed GGW L W A can achieve beam scanning of -21 °~29° at 22 GHz.

articleTitle: V-band antipolar fin line microstrip waveguide conversion structure
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The V-band microstrip waveguide conversion structure cannot meet the requirements of simple installation and integrated design. The fin line structure with specific size and shape is etched on the surface of the film. By adjusting the parameters of the opposite pole fin line, the conversion structure can meet the requirements of practical performance. The test results show that the center frequency of antipolar fin line microstrip waveguide conversion structure is 71.6GHz, the internal reflection parameter S11 is less than -20dB in the bandwidth of 67.3-77.0GHz and 10GHz, and the conversion structure size is 6.56mm*1.47mm*0.127mm. The conversion structure is installed in the middle of the V-band waveguide along the E-plane of the waveguide, without slotting the waveguide wall, which meets the requirements of superior performance, simple installation and integrated design.

articleTitle: 21cm Global Spectrum Measuring Instrument For Lunar-Orbit Satellite Array
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ionosphere and radio frequency interference (RFI) make low frequency radio observation on Earth difficult. Lunar orbit is an ideal site for making low frequency observations, to probe the redshifted global 21cm signal for understanding the Cosmic Dawn and Epoch of Reionization. We present a global spectrum measuring instrument specially designed for deploying on lunar orbit. The instrument consists of an electrically small frequency-independent antenna and a differential two-way cross correlation receiver. The system can make real-time vector network measurement for the antenna and receiver, and it makes absolute calibration and relative calibration using the noise wave parameter calculation. A prototype has undergone ground test in Xinjiang. Some preliminary analysis of the system performance and test data are presented, which verified the feasibility of system design.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Point-to-Area Propagation at VHF Band
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The measurement campaign for point-to-area propagation at radio wave frequency 90.5 MHz is introduced and the measured basic transmission loss is compared with the Recommendation ITU-R P.1546-6 model. The experiment was carried out in Beijing, China. It can be concluded from the comparison that the measured loss is greater than the predicted loss in most circumstances.

articleTitle: Calculation of Lightning Induced Voltage of Buried Cable Metal Sheath
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to research the lightning induced overvoltage on the metal sheath of buried cables, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm is used to calculate the underground lightning electromagnetic field. By using the vector fitting method, the field-line coupling model is simplified, the lightning induced overvoltage on the buried cable sheath is calculated, and the effect of vertically layered soil on the induced voltage on the buried cable sheath is analyzed.

articleTitle: Time-domain Inversion Cascade Network (TICaN) for Sophisticated Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a time-domain inversion cascade network (TICaN) is proposed to reconstruct the permittivity via measured electric fields, emerging superior efficiency with-out sacrificing accuracy. TICaN is appliable to both piecewise homogeneous and inhomogeneous scatterers. In comparison of conventional inversion algorithms, a well-trained TICaN is able to avert the tedious iterative calculation and acquire a precise so-lution simultaneously once the measured electric field is obtained. We believe this work offers enormous potential for applications pertaining to real-time time-domain inversion problems.

articleTitle: Microwave Switch in a Circular Waveguide with Gas Microwave Discharge in a High-power Microwave Pulse Compression System For a Solar Space
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: High-power microwave (HPM) beams are used in space science for transferring energy from Earth-to-space, space-to-Earth, and space-to-space. Increase of the power of the microwave beam of a high-power microwave pulse compression system (HPMS) without any changes in its weight and size characteristics is currently an urgent task. Losses in a plasma of gas discharge tube of microwave switch of a HPMS may reach up to 50% at output energy. Understanding the process of microwave frequencies interaction with plasma, as well as microwave frequencies parameters, will reduce the losses in the gas-discharge tube of the switch during energy output. This will increase the power of the HPMS microwave beam at the same weight and size characteristics, which will reduce the cost of deploying the microwave energy in the Earth orbit. This paper presents results of an experimental study of H11 wave switching in interference microwave switches based on TE-tees made from S-band circular waveguides made for energy output devices in resonant microwave compressors. The switching is carried out by the plasma of a gas microwave discharge initiated in a quartz tube located along the diameter of the waveguide. The simulation experiments at high-power levels helped to determine the basic conditions for effective switching. It is shown that the use of S-band circular waveguide switches made from circular waveguides in resonant microwave compressors makes it possible to switch a wave with power up to 0.5 GW and form stable nanosecond microwave pulses with power up to 1 GW and a repetition rate up to 100 Hz.

articleTitle: A study of a set of conducted susceptibility test signals which can effectively excite susceptibility
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a set of conducted susceptibility test signals based on the Basic Emission Waveform Theory is proposed. Based on the analysis of three elements of electromagnetic interference, the four basic signals proposed by Basic Emission Waveform Theory can be used as a basic set of conducted susceptibility test signals to achieve a more accurate simulation of the electromagnetic environment. The test platform of electromagnetic susceptibility is built to carry out conducted susceptibility tests and analyze the electromagnetic susceptibility to the test signals of the Equipment Under Test (EUT). Finally, it is verified that analog signal sets, digital signal sets, pulse signal sets, and mismatched signal sets can effectively excite the EUT's conducted susceptibility.

articleTitle: Estimation of Ground Scattering Coefficient Based on Small Perturbation Method
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper introduces a method to evaluate the electromagnetic (EM) scattering of the land surface. A detail of small perturbation method (SPM) is firstly presented, which is adopted to evaluate the EM scattering of the mentioned rough surface with large incident angles. We then obtain the scattering coefficient of sandy-loam soil in different polarizations. Then we give a minute analysis to the results of scattering coefficient. At last, we analyze its current condition and problems in SPM.

articleTitle: A novel low-profile broadband circularly polarized bowtie antenna with AMC surface
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel low-profile bowtie antenna is designed for broadband and circularly polarized communications. The proposed bowtie antenna is composed of four radiated branches, and each branch consists of three hexagons, three hexagonal rings and a semi-hexagonal ring, which can generate multi-resonance and result in a wide impedance matching bandwidth. In addition, the introduction of hexagonal rings increases the current path, bringing in small antenna size (0.39AL *0.39AL *0.012AL). Two ports are utilized to feed the radiators to achieve circular polarization. To improve the circularly polarized property, two pairs of rectangles, with different dimensions in x and y direction, are added inside the four semi-hexagonal rings. Moreover, an AMC surface is designed as the ground of the bowtie antenna to achieve low-profile and high-gain performance. The presented AMC ground, made up of 12*12 units, brings the composed antenna about a low profile. The total size of the composed antenna is 84*84*8mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>(1.03AL *1.03AL *0.098AL). The simulated results show that the presented low-profile broadband bowtie antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth from 3.69 to 6.22 GHz (51.06%) and an axis ratio bandwidth of 55.3% (3.4GHz-6GHz). And the maximum gain can reach 8.31dBic at 4GHz.

articleTitle: DOD and DOA Estimation of Coherent Targets in Bistatic MIMO Radar Based on DFSS_ESPRIT
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, the direction of departure (DOD) and the direction of arrival (DOA) of multiple targets with same Doppler frequency in bistatic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar are estimated based on diagonal forward space smoothing (DFSS) combining with estimating signal parameters via rotation invariance techniques (ESPRIT). Firstly, the signal model with Doppler frequency of bistatic MIMO radar is introduced. Secondly, DFSS_ESPRIT is used for decoherence and angle estimation. Simulation results show that the proposed method can estimate the DOD and DOA of multiple coherent targets, which verifies the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Using Python to Launch Electromagnetic Scattering Simulation with FEKO
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper provides details on how to use Python to launch the typical commercial electromagnetics software package. FEKO is a representative example that can be directly called from Python. The example of a scattering simulation of a right cylinder for both two polarizations are presented using a direct call to FEKO with Python.

articleTitle: Beam-pointing Deviation Analysis of the Wide band Phased Array and Array-fed Reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In wide-band phased array and array-fed reflector antenna, the traditional phase-shift method causes beam-pointing deviation versus frequency. The excursion of beam-pointing is analyzed for the wide band phased array and array-fed reflector antenna through simulating using beam forming theory in this paper. The theoretical analysis shows that the beam-pointing drift of the planar phased array in azimuth and elevation are independent of the antenna size, and the beam-pointing drift of the array-fed reflector antenna is not superior than the phased array antenna, but it is much easier to compensate the beam-pointing deviation of array-fed reflector antenna.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics of VLF Electromagnetic Wave in Earth-ionosphere Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the propagation theory of VLF electromagnetic wave in earth-ionosphere waveguide, taking VTX-Kolkata propagation path as an example, the propagation characteristics of VLF electromagnetic wave in earth-ionosphere waveguide are studied in this paper. Firstly, the electron density and the collision frequency along the propagation path are obtained through the ionospheric IRI2016 model and NRLMSISE-00 atmospheric model. Then, combined with the SO-FDTD algorithm, the variation of field intensity along the propagation path in a whole day are calculated. Finally, the temporal and spatial variation characteristics of VLF electromagnetic wave on the propagation path are analyzed.

articleTitle: Assessment of Ionospheric Correction Algorithm Based on Data Ingestion during Ionospheric Storm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents an ionospheric correction algorithm based on data ingestion, which is realized by updating the driving parameters of the model with GNSS TEC. The ionospheric correction algorithm is evaluated by comparison between observation results and model results which are calculated based on the previous day vertical TEC data-driven model and the previous 15min vertical TEC data-driven model from July 14<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> to July 19<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, 2012. The evaluation results show that during the ionospheric storm, the average RMS of the driving model based on the vertical TEC of the previous 15 minutes is 3.2 TECU, which is much smaller than that of the driving model based on the vertical TEC of the previous day, which is 14.1 TECU. Therefore, a higher update rate of ionospheric driving parameters should be used to correct the ionosphere delay during ionospheric storm.

articleTitle: Transceiver Beamforming for MmWave Dual-Polarized NOMA Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, we investigate a mmWave dual-polarized non-orthogonal multiple access (DP-NOMA) communication system. An achievable sum rate (ASR) maximization problem is formulated to optimize the Tx and Rx beamforming vector. To solve the non-convex problem, we first fix the beamformer at the BS and derive the close-form expression of the optimal beamforming vector for each user. Then we adopt boundary compressed particle swarm optimization method to obtain the solution of BS beamformer. Numerical results show that among all the considered transmission schemes, our proposed DP-NOMA has the best performance.

articleTitle: Design of a VLF/LF band Borehole Electromagnetic Transmitter and Magnetic Dipole Transmitting Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The borehole electromagnetic wave imaging system(CT) is composed of ground system, winch, transmitting and receiving nipples. The system uses electromagnetic wave tomography technology to obtain the received field strength at different positions by changing the positions of transmitter and receiver, and then obtain the resistivity profile between two holes through inversion. In an engineering application, a VLF / LF band borehole electromagnetic wave transmitter and magnetic dipole transmitting antenna are designed according to the requirements.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of the dynamics of the temperature of electrons heated by fast electrons formed during the modification of ionosphere by RF waves
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: We study the dynamics of the temperature of electrons heated by fast electrons generated during the modification of the ionosphere by powerful electromagnetic waves. A correct expression is proposed for the contribution of electron-electron collisions to the heating of Maxwellian (thermal) electrons in the presence of a stationary flow of fast electrons in the plasma. Simulation are performed for the parameters corresponding to the real values in the ionospheric plasma of the F-layer at an altitude of h ~ 200–300 km, used in earlier works.

articleTitle: Development of new mechanical magnetoelectric antenna and its application in electronic warfare
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: According to the essence of mechanical antenna theory, the concept of magnetoelectric antenna is defined. The reason why magnetoelectric antenna can break through the traditional theory of antenna miniaturization is also explained. On this basis, the radiation field of magnetoelectric antenna is deduced. The development process of magnetoelectric antenna is sorted out and the periodical results of magnetoelectric antennas are displayed. The existing technical problems of magnetoelectric antenna are comprehensively described and the application prospect of magnetoelectric antenna in electronic warfare field is forecasted.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Directivity on Near Region Field Distribution in Rectangular Tunnel
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The effect of antenna orientation on field distribution is discussed. The elevation angle and azimuth angle are adjusted to make median received power get the maximum. The electric field distribution by optimizing the pitch angle and azimuth angle is shown. The Yagi antenna is used for transmitter and the number of transmitter changes from 1–8. Then two different scenarios are shown and discussed, in which the location of receiver changes. For different scenarios and locations of receiver, the optimal numbers of antennas are given.

articleTitle: A New Methodology to Identify the Conducted Emission Source of Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new method for identifying internal conducted emission (CE) source of Integrated Circuits (ICs). By studying the spectrum characteristics of three typical internal interference sources, sine wave, square wave and spike, and the general characteristics of the power distribution network (PDN) transfer functions of ICs, the envelope detrending method is proposed, which combines machine learning and classification algorithms to make it possible to identify the conducted emission source of ICs.

articleTitle: Wideband Cosecant Square Vertical Planar Printed Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel broadband high gain cosecant square array antenna is presented. The proposed array antenna is composed of 32 high gain vertical planar printed antennas and a low-loss inverted microstrip line feeding network. All of those structures are printed in the same dielectric substrate. The working bandwidth of the antenna array is 6-7.35GHz. When the array antenna is utilized without a feeding network, the shaped region reaches up to 30 degrees and has a peak gain of 19.4 dBi to 20.5 dBi. An array antenna with a feeding network has a peak gain of 18.1 dBi to 19.3 dBi. The good radiation performances make the antenna suitable for the wireless communication systems and radar antenna application.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method to Eliminate DOA Ambiguity of ULA
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, we first retrospect the causes of direction of arrival (DOA) ambiguity of uniform linear array (ULA), which is the existence of two collinear steering vectors of corresponding backward and forward directions in ULA. Then, we redesign the array structure to eliminate collinearity of the steering vector and carry out theoretical analysis and simulation verification. Finally, we conduct validation experiments. The results clearly show that the newly designed array eliminates the DOA Ambiguity to some extent and improves the accuracy of estimation.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Patch Antenna Integrated in a 77 GHz Automotive Radar for Parking Assistant Application
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A single patch antenna has been designed, verified, and integrated to a 77 GHz automotive radar module for short range parking assistant application. The S11 and the E- /H-plane radiation patterns of the implemented single patch antenna were characterized. A center frequency of 76.38 GHz with 10-dB bandwidth of 2 GHz fulfills designed operating frequency range between 76–77 GHz. The field-of-view (FoV) both on azimuth and elevation planes achieves ± 120°. Two-way radar performance tests were additionally carried out in in- and outdoor scenarios. Corner reflectors and parking lot could be stably detected with correct position information based on direction of arrival (DoA) estimation. In-vehicle tests have been done both under high-speed and low-speed detection modes. With four implemented radar sensors installed around, the perception and sensing capa-bility of the test vehicle has great potential to meet the require-ments of automotive parking assistant application.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a Novel Dual Polarized Annular Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized antenna that operates with high isolation and high gain is proposed. The antenna is fed by a pair of orthogonal microstrip lines in the top layer of the substrate to excite the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode in the circular substrate integrated waveguide(SIW) resonant cavity, the structure works at 5.7GHz with a -10dB impedance bandwidth of 1.4% and has a maximum in-band gain of 9.1dB while the port isolation is above 22.6dB.

articleTitle: Compact Circularly Polarized Crossed Dipole Antenna with Wide Bandwidth and Wide Axial Ratio
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A compact circularly polarized (CP) crossed dipole antenna with wide bandwidth and wide axial ratio (AR) is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a pair of crossed dipoles, a double three-quarter rings with a 90° phase shift, four split rings resonator and four parasitic patches. The combination of the crossed dipole with a three-quarter ring can produce an AR point. It is found that the introduction of four split rings resonator on both surfaces of the substrate can increase the bandwidth, make the structure compact, and can produce an AR point at high frequency. The parasitic patch around the split ring resonant produces perturbation that combines the two AR points and introduces a new AR point. The ultimate simulation results show that the proposed antenna has a 10 dB impedance bandwidth of 69.6° (1.35-2.79 GHz) and a 3 dB AR bandwidth of 58.5% (1.4-2.56 GHz). In addition, it has a stable gain in the whole CP frequency region.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cluster Characteristics for 5G Millimeter Wave Channel in a Substation Scenario
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In the near future, millimeter-wave (mmWave) technology will be gradually applied in various Internet of Things (IoTs) scenarios to meet the high data rate requirements of billions of terminals and sensors. In this work, 28 GHz mmWave channel measurements were conducted in a high-voltage substation. Based on the measurement data, the multipath components are extracted and identified into different clusters. The cluster characteristics including delay and angle domain parameters, numbers of clusters and multipaths, as well as power decay factors are calculated and analyzed. Numerical results show that the cluster characteristics fit quite well with the expected distributions or models. The channel characteristics can be useful for the simulation, planning and construction of power IoTs.

articleTitle: Geographical Information-Specific Emulator with EM Propagation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A Geographical Information- specific configuration for multiple emitter emulator is introduced in this paper. Using the EM wave environment-specific propagation modeling method during the process of signal generation and modulation, can help increase the fidelity of the EM spectrum status simulation in actual operation.

articleTitle: An Optical Transparent Broadband Absorber Based on Hexagonal Ring
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, an optical transparent broadband absorber based on hexagonal ring is proposed. The structure is composed of Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) resistance film and air substrate. The absorptivity can reach more than 90% over the frequency band from 4.47 to 18.38 GHz. Compared with the reported optical transparent broadband absorbers in recent years, the proposed structure has larger absorption bandwidth and smaller thickness, as well as better incident angle stability. Due to its optical transparency, the structure can be widely applied.

articleTitle: Simulation and Characteristic Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering from Turbulent Wake
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ship wake can be used as an effective auxiliary means for remote sensing detection of ship targets because of its large geometric scale, long existence time, non-stealth and strong scattering. In this paper, the ship turbulent wake with complex structure is studied, its macroscopic characteristics and microstructure are analyzed, and its geometric model and the foam particle model are established. The dielectric parameters of seawater at different frequencies are calculated by double Debye model. Based on the Rayleigh approximation and the vector radiative transfer theory (VRT), the foam scattering model is established, and its scattering characteristics under different incident conditions are compared and analyzed. Using the particle size distribution function of the wake foam obtained from the experiment, the scattering coefficient of the turbulent wake is calculated at different regions, and the refined electromagnetic scattering simulation of the turbulent wake is achieved. This work can provide theoretical support for radar remote sensing detection engineering of ships and their turbulent wake.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna with stable performance
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna with good in-band performance and simple structure is proposed in this paper. The radiator is a square patch with four filleted corners, and a slot is etched in the radiated patch for improving the impedance matching. The rounded corners of the radiating patch are used to produce one null point for the curve of axial ratio. A parasitic open loop with a pin is placed around the radiator and is used to produce the other null point for the curve of axial ratio, leading to a wide 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARB). The simulation impedance bandwidth (IB) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> 11 < -10 dB is around 18.8% (3.23-3.90GHz), the simulation 3-dB ARB is around 13.3% (3.30-3.77 GHz), and the in-band gain is larger than 7.5 dB.

articleTitle: End-fire Hybrid Metasurface Antenna for mm- Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This article introduces a hybrid metasurface antenna with high gain fed by low loss substrate integrated waveguide. The pure metasurface antenna consists of only 3 x 3 rectangular patches. The hybrid metasurface antenna is composed of rectangular patches and parallel wires. The inversion results of the eigen-parameters of the parallel line unit show that the equivalent refractive index in the 33–37 GHz frequency band is greater than 1.5. The endfire gain of the hybrid metasurface antenna ranges from 8 to 12.1 dBi in the 33–37 GHz frequency range. Compared with metasurface antenna with only the rectangular patch, the gain is improved by more than 3.6 dB. Therefore, the hybrid metasurface antenna is an excellent candidate for future millimeter wave applications due to its wide bandwidth and high gain.

articleTitle: A near real-time global ionospheric data assimilation and forecast system
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ionosphere is currently one of the most important contents of space weather forecasting. The establishment of a reliable and accurate ionospheric characteristic parameter specification and forecast system is of great value to space science research and military and civilian radio information systems. Based on the ground-based GNSS and Global Ionospheric Radio Observatory (GIRO) digital ionosonde real-time data of the International GNSS Service Organization (RT-IGS), and International Reference Ionosphere (IRI) was chosen as the background model, China Research Institute of Radio Propagation (CRIRP) adopts Gauss-Markov-band-limited Kalman filter assimilation technology, combined with super-large-scale matrix sparse storage and processing methods, and developed a near-real-time global ionospheric data assimilation and forecast system (RT-GIDAM) on “China Electronics Cloud”. RT-GIDAM can realize the global ionospheric TEC and electron density nowcast and forecast in near real-time (with a delay of about 5min), higher spatial resolution (5°×2.5°) and time resolution (15min). The establishment of RT-GIDAM can provide data support for space physics research and related radio system applications.

articleTitle: Propagation characteristics of Bessel Gaussian localized wave in turbulent atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the generalized Huygens-Fresnel principle, the average light intensity of the Bessel Gaussian localized wave is calculated. The intensity evolution and beam broadening effect of Bessel Gaussian localized wave in atmospheric turbulence are studied by numerical simulation. The results show that the atmospheric turbulence effect of Bessel Gaussian localized wave can be improved by adjusting the light source parameters and turbulence parameters. The research results provide a more ideal development direction for improving the spectrum utilization and information capacity of the existing free-space optical communication technology.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized mmWave Antenna Based on Zero Mode
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Compared with the conventional patch antenna, the antenna utilizing shorting pins can significantly reduce the size. In this paper, we introduce a method to miniaturize antenna dimension with loading shorting pins in mmWave band. First, the theoretical analysis on relationship between loading shorting pins with inducing zero modes is investigated, followed by designing a microstrip patch antenna in 26 GHz band with three shorting pins. Consequently, 35% size reduction is obtained. Moreover, the influence of the position and number of shorting pins are studied and simulated as well.

articleTitle: Measurement of Spectrum Emission Mask in Different Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, measurements of spectrum emission mask (SEM) are performed in conduction and over-the-air (OTA) testing. By comparing the results between different scenarios, it is shown that interferences, such as spurious emission interference and out of band interference, influence on SEM only in OTA testing.

articleTitle: A Design and Realization of GA-Optimized Wire Antenna with A On-Body Matching Network
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a based on the loaded dipole antenna of GA-optimized and matching network is proposed. The genetic algorithm(GA)-optimized is used to optimize the position and value of inductance/resistor (L/R) loads to achieve matching in frequency range. Finally, the antenna achieves impedance matching in the operating frequency range of 20-1600MHZ-hence a 80:1 bandwidth (195%), with VSWR less than 3.5, and the gain is gradually increased from -19 dBi to -2.1dBi.

articleTitle: Tian Ma 65-m Telescope State Awareness System
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The Tian Ma Radio Telescope (TMRT) is the largest fully steerable radio telescope in Asia. It has a primary reflector of 65-m in diameter with a shaped Cassegrain configuration and is mainly used for deep space exploration and radio astronomy observations. It is composed of a series of systems, such as antenna system, active surface system, receiver system, and digital system. The TMRT's equipment is very complicated. To improve the maintainability, operating efficiency, and reliability of TMRT, the Tian Ma Telescope State Awareness System (TMTSAS) was developed. The system implements remote, unmanned, multi-user, real-time, visual state, abnormal state alarms, and data sharing functions.

articleTitle: Interference Characteristics of Flat Top Laser Transmission in Atmospheric Turbulent Media
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to study the target echo interference characteristics of laser echoes in atmospheric turbulent media and obtain clear and effective interference information, this paper uses the flat-top laser to establish a statistical light intensity transmission model in atmospheric turbulent media and specifically analyzes the laser transmission distance, light spot cross-section, and turbulence intensity, respectively. The research shows that in the atmospheric turbulent medium, it is the main factor that the transmission distances of the flat-top laser effects on the light intensity, and the light intensity decreases monotonically with the increase of transmission distance. The larger the turbulence intensity is, the larger the cross-section radius of the flat-top laser is. This paper provides a theoretical basis for the construction and selection of effective interference areas.

articleTitle: Satellite-Borne K Band Phased Array Antenna Element With Harmonic Suppression Capability
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to suppress harmonic emissions of the K band active phased array, a K-band cross dipole antenna element with harmonic suppression capability is proposed. A coaxial band-pass filter designed through the series structure of high-and-low impedance lines is integrated into a traditional cross dipole antenna, which can achieve harmonic suppression effect without increasing the antenna size. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna can suppress the harmonic emissions by 27.4dBc. The proposed antenna provides a good solution for improving the electromagnetic compatibility index of phased array antenna systems.

articleTitle: Realization of high-order modes on compact spoof surface plasmonic waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this work, transmission of high-order modes of spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) is realized on compact guided wave structure. On the basis of conformal surface plasmons, metal via holes are applied in the microwave substrate to connect front and additional back metal constructions, which effectively reduces the overall width of the whole structure. The dispersion relations of periodic unit shows that it can supports multiple high-order modes, and matches well with transmission characteristics of guided wave structure constituted by several units. The proposed design with features of compact size and easy fabrication will make contributions to development of communication system.

articleTitle: Thomson Scattering of a Vector Laguerre-Gaussian Beam by a Non-Relativistic Electron
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to explore the scattering effect of vortex beams in plasma, the Thomson scattering of a vector Laguerre-Gaussian beam by a non-relativistic electron is studied in this paper. By expressing a Laguerre-Gaussian beam as the superposition of a series of plane waves, the expression of scattered electric field is derived according to Thomson scattering theory. The scattering power in unit solid angle of each point on the receiving plane is simulated numerically. The influence of the radial mode numbers of Laguerre-Gaussian beams and velocity of the electron are analyzed. The work provides an important theoretical basis for further exploring the scattering characteristics of vortex beams in complex plasma environment.

articleTitle: The Design of Polarized Antenna Arrays Based on High-Order Mode
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, different polarized antenna arrays based on high-order mode(HOM) are presented for the fifth-generation communication, respectively. Firstly, two linearly polarized antenna arrays are demonstrated with high gain and high efficiency thanks to the low-cost property of HOM. In one of them, 3 x 4 slots are excited simultaneously by the high-order mode. A TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">340</inf> HOM cavity excited 2x2 slot antenna array is presented in another one. Then, two circular antenna arrays are proposed based on the HOM phase distribution. A sequentially rotated feeding network is introduced for antennas' better performance. Last but not least, an 8x 8 dual circularly polarized antenna array is proposed, showing the huge potential of HOM in antenna design with miniaturized size, high gain, and high efficiency. Four sequentially rotated patches fed by high-order mode are set as a subarray to form dual circular polarization. It is concluded that the HOM fed antenna arrays feature high gain, high efficiency, and diverse polarizations.

articleTitle: Simulation optimization of Wire bonding line matching based on FDTD algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to solve the serious impedance mismatch problem of the gold wire bonding line in millimeter wave microassembly process in 8mm band, this paper simulated and optimized the process of the gold wire bonding line based on FDTD algorithm. As the parasitic inductance and parasitic capacitance of the gold wire bond line increase sharply in 8mm band, the output impedance of the gold wire bond line is not 50Ω. At this time, the output impedance mismatch between the wire and chip is serious, and the transmission efficiency of the system is greatly reduced. In the 32ghZ-36ghz band, the echo loss of single chip bonding to microstrip transmission line is improved by 10-15dB after simulation optimization compensation. This improves the transmission efficiency of the system and has a good engineering application prospect.

articleTitle: A Novel Blind SNR Estimation Algorithm for SC-IFDM Ionospheric Scatter Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The ionospheric scatter communication system is challenging due to its large transmission loss and usually works under low signal to noise ratio (SNR). A novel blind SNR estimation algorithm for single carrier interleaved frequency division multiplexing (SC-IFDM) system is proposed to improve the accuracy of the estimation. The received time domain data are used to estimate the signal power and noise variance based on the order moment algorithm. The SNR of each SC-IFDM symbol as well as its average SNR over a whole sub-frame can be estimated. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing estimators at the low SNR region, and that the credible range can be extended to approximately -18dB. Besides, the algorithm is non-pilot aided, making it appealing to wireless systems for saving overhead.

articleTitle: Observation and Analysis of the Sunrise Effect of 19.8kHz Signal in Xinjiang
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Very low frequency waves (VLF) have a frequency of 3~30kHz. They are transmitted over long distances in the earth-ionosphere waveguide, with small propagation loss and high skin depth, so they are widely used in navigation, submarine communication and other fields. In addition, it has important significance in ionospheric remote sensing. During the period from April 22 to May 22, 2021, a very low frequency receiver was used in the Yili area of Xinjiang to observe the 19.8kHz signal from the Australian NWC, and the characteristics and laws of its amplitude response during the sunrise were counted. The statistical results found that the amplitude response of different test points all showed minimum values, showing certain regularity and consistency as a whole, and the minimum value appeared almost all later than the sunrise time. Observing a certain observation point at different times, the angle between the sunrise terminator and the propagation path gradually decreases, and the time interval between the sunrise time and the time when the minimum value appears becomes larger. When observing different observation points at the same time, the angle of the sunrise terminator does not change. The smaller the angle between the propagation path and the sunrise terminator, the greater the time interval between the sunrise time and the occurrence time of the minimum.

articleTitle: Modeling of Cone Absorbing Material Based on Neural Network and Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: When calculating the absorption capacity of periodic cone-shaped absorbing materials, full-wave simulation is often difficult due to the large electrical size. And the theoretical calculation formula of the transmission line can only be applied to the case where each layer is a uniform medium. Therefore, this paper uses optimization algorithms to extract the equivalent material parameters of absorbing materials with different volume ratios in the air, and trains the BPNN (back propagation neural network) based on this data, which can effectively calculate the effective material parameters on specified frequency, actual material parameters and volume ratio. The equivalent medium model established in this paper not only breaks through the limitation of the Maxwell Garnett model on the frequency of use, but also uses the optimization algorithm to avoid the inapplicability of the S-parameter extraction method in the case of high-order modes.

articleTitle: The Simulation of Backscattering Mueller Matrix for the Wind-Generated Bubbles in the Ocean by Using a GPU-Accelerated Monte Carlo Model
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A graphics processing unit (GPU) accelerated Monte Carlo model is developed for polarized light propagation in the seawater containing bubbles. The speedup of the parallel algorithm is approximately 35x. The two-dimensional (2D) patterns of the backscattering Mueller matrix for wind-generated bubbles is simulated by using this parallel model. The simulation results show that only seven matrix elements are independent, and the 2D distributions of the backscattering Mueller matrix elements of bubbles are relevant to the wind speeds.

articleTitle: Time Domain Hybrid Method for the Coupling Analysis of Transmission Line with Junctions
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Numerical methods prosed for the coupling effects analysis on transmission line (TL) with junction structure, which are excited by ambient wave, are still rare in the published literature. By combining the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method with TL equations and charge conservation law, a hybrid method with high-efficiency in the time domain is proposed in this work. Within this method, we first decompose the whole structure of TL into two groups, i.e. several independent TL segments and some junction structures. For the TL segments, the TL equations and FDTD method is jointly employed to build the coupling models of each TL segment and obtain the corresponding transient responses. Based on this, the voltages at the junctions are solved by the charge conservation law and FDTD method jointly. By numerical simulation of the case where a transmission line with two junctions on a perfect electrical conductor (PEC) ground is excited by ambient wave, the accuracy of the proposed method is verified by comparing its results with the one obtained by applying commercial simulation software CST.

articleTitle: The FDTD simulation of very low frequency waves propagation in the ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The VLF (very low frequency) waves can not only propagate in the ground-ionosphere waveguide, but also enter the ionosphere to form whistler waves that propagate along the magnetic field lines and propagate to the magnetosphere or even to the magnetic conjugate region. But the physical process of the VLF propagation in the ionosphere has not been concluded in detail yet, especially for the nonlinear process of ionospheric heating caused by the powerful VLF waves. Moreover, the properties of the D region are hardly measured by satellites or rockets. Thus, the simulation of the VLF propagation profoundly influences the researches of propagation and wave-particle interaction. This work presents a GPU-accelerated FDTD (finite-different time-domain) scheme which simulates the VLF signals spreading from ground to the higher ionosphere. The scheme divides the space into coarse and fine grids to cope with the great changes of VLF wavelength caused by ionospheric refractive index. This work also combines the numerical results and the detection data of the ionosphere by DEMETER satellite and zh-1 satellite to verify whistler waves transmission path at higher satellite altitude.

articleTitle: Fuze Echo Recognition Based on Improved V-G Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that it is difficult for the traditional fuse target recognition algorithm to recognize the object with the same size as the target under the condition of ground object coupling and low signal-to-noise ratio, the V-G convolution neural network is used for Fuse echo The improved V-G convolution neural network is used in this method, and the data of laser and radio fuse missile target rendezvous is used as The improved V-G convolution neural network is used in this method, and the data of laser and radio fuse missile target rendezvous is used as the training library to identify the targets outside the library and classify the targets inside the library. The simulation results show that the recognition accuracy is more than 95%, and the fuse echo recognition can be carried out efficiently.

articleTitle: Research on the Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics of Wingtip Vortices
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The detection of aircraft wingtip vortices has always been a key issue for aviation safety and aircraft stealth. Previous work mostly used density variation and water vapor variation to calculate dielectric parameters and the distribution of radar cross section(RCS). Here, the atmospheric pressure variation around the aircraft are calculated and simulated using Ansys Fluent software and numerical models such as fluid mechanics N-S equation. To investigate the change of its scattering cross section, we calculated the fluctuations of the dielectric parameters around aircraft for the given data of atmospheric pressure fluctuations. Finally, we show the relation between RCS and radar receiving horizontal angle under three incident wave angles, and the change rule of RCS and receiving angle both in the horizontal polarization and vertical polarization cases. This conclusion has a positive effect on the study of the scattering characteristics of wingtip vortices.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Switching Antenna Based on Coding Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A transmission-type multi-beam switching antenna based on coding metasurface is designed. The U-shaped slot microstrip antenna is used as a source element, and the coding metasurface above the microstrip antenna is used to control multiple beams. The coding metasurface have two kinds of particles with different transmissivity responses to TM wave, corresponding to two basic coding element 0 and 1 respectively. PIN diodes are loaded on the metasurface. The designed antenna can dynamically switch between 4 beams or 2 beams by controlling the on or off state of PIN diodes.

articleTitle: A Frequency Tunable Helical Filter with Liquid Loading
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A frequency tunable helical filter using distilled water is presented. The filter frequency tunability is realized by using distilled water loaded helical resonator. Due to the high dielectric constant of distilled water, adjusting the volume of distilled water can change the equivalent electrical length of the helix, thus realizing the frequency reconfiguration. A third-order tunable cavity filter is designed. The simulation results show that the center frequency tuning of the proposed BPF is ranged from 315 to 425 MHz and the insertion loss is varied within 0.3 dB -1dB. This tunable filter has great potentials for the radar communication system.

articleTitle: A method for evaluating feed reflection of monocone based on single port S parameters
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper presents a method to evaluate the reflection level of monocone feed point based on monocone single port S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>. This method only needs one single port measurement of a monocone through the vector network analyzer. Based on the obtained S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> data, the reflected signal of any excitation signal at the feed point can be evaluated as long as the spectrum of the excitation signal is within the frequency range of interest. Compared with the time domain method, the method proposed in this paper has many advantages.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Method for Path Loss Prediction in Mobile Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The study of wireless channel propagation characteristics is important to channel availability analysis and wireless network optimization. The existing deterministic channel models are greatly restricted by the high complexity. This paper proposes a deep learning (DL) method for path loss (PL) prediction in mobile communication systems, which uses satellite images and neural network (NN) to achieve efficient and reliable prediction. A Deep Neural Network (DNN) framework is established based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), where CNN extracts environmental features of propagation paths from satellite images and BPNN predicts PL according to the distance features and environmental features. The results show that DNN proposed in this paper can reduce the time cost with satisfying accuracy compared to the traditional Ray-tracing method with the lack of a detailed model of the scene and material parameters. The DL method for making a quick prediction of the PL in this paper can be used to optimize the mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: Study on wave absorption of finite thickness alternate layered lossy dielectric and lossy magnetic dielectric
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the common lossy dielectric and lossy magnetic dielectric, this paper attempts to approach the intrinsic impedance of air by alternating stacking. Taking E-M pattern and E-M-E pattern as examples, the effects of the number of cycles and the ratio of dielectric to magnetic thickness on the input impedance of laminated structures are studied. The calculation shows that in terms of eliminating reflection, this stacking method is much better than using lossy dielectric or lossy magnetic dielectric alone.

articleTitle: High Precision Translational Compensation for Ultrahigh Resolution ISAR
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In recent years, due to the emergence of ultrahigh resolution (UHR) radar systems, the bandwidth of radar has been increasing. However, conventional imaging algorithms have difficulties in the translational compensation of UHR inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) data with high order range cell migration (RCM) and phase error. In this paper, a high-precision translational compensation method based on power flatness optimization (PFO) is proposed. The algorithm constructs the optimal criterion of power flatness and ensure the complete extraction of the prominent point energy. Then, the original data is compensated in the two-dimensional data domain through the prominent point phase inversion matrix. The results show that the proposed algorithm has significantly improved accuracy in the translational compensation of ultrahigh-resolution ISAR imaging compared with traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: An experiment of GNSS-based single-station tropospheric refractivity profile inversion
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: The retrieval of tropospheric refractivity profiles based on GNSS signals has significant advantages in terms of temporal and spatial resolution, operability, and equipment cost. This work presents an experiment of GNSS-based single-station tropospheric refractivity profile inversion at the coast area of Qingdao. The satellite broadcast ephemeris, clock error, and corresponding correction data are used to carry out real-time Precise Point Positioning to extract the observed GNSS tropospheric slant path delays, then ray-tracing simulations are exploited to calculate the corresponding theoretical GNSS tropospheric slant path delays, and finally the NSGA-II algorithm is used to perform multi-objective optimization to inverse the tropospheric atmospheric refractivity profile. The comparison results with nearby radiosonde data show that operational GNSS-based tropospheric refractivity profile retrieval is feasible, and further improvement is still needed on inversion accuracy in the coastal area.

articleTitle: A Pattern Reconfigurable Hemispherical Dielectric Liquid Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A pattern reconfigurable hemispherical dielectric resonant antenna (DRA) is proposed in this paper. It combines a solid and a liquid hemispherical DRA in one structure with different sizes. The pattern reconfiguration can be achieved by exciting different modes. The solid DRA with a small size operates with the TE111 mode, which has a conical radiation pattern. The outer liquid DRA with a large size works at the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf> with an omnidirectional pattern. It is demonstrated that the proposed antenna has a wider bandwidth from 1.8 GHz to 2.6 GHz for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{11} < -10\text{dB}$</tex> and can realize a pattern reconfigurable without any active components. This design has great application potential in the mobile communication.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of the Two-Dimensional HIE-FDTD Method Including Lumped Resistors
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Here, the stability analysis of the two-dimensional (2-D) hybrid implicit-explicit finite-difference time-domain (HIE-FDTD) algorithm with lumped resistors is discussed. Specially, there are three different difference schemes of lumped resistors are discussed: the explicit, semi-implicit, and implicit scheme. The stability analysis of the proposed method showed that the HIE-FDTD algorithm loaded with lumped elements is weakly conditionally stable and is not affected by the lumped resistor. In the end, a microstrip circuit loaded with lumped resistor is used to verify whether the analyzed numerical results are consistent with the experimental results.

articleTitle: Scattering of pulsed Terahertz wave by sand particles
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A pulsed Terahertz wave scattered by a spherical particle is numerical analyzed in this paper using a generalized Lorenz-Mie formula. The envelope information of Terahertz wave covers a spectrum range of 0.2THz-3.75THz is extracted from the original signal generated by a femtosecond laser source and then fitted by using the single peak function. The complex refractive index of particles changes with the frequency in the Terahertz band are obtained using the cubic spline interpolation algorithm based on the original data extracted from the HITRAN2012. Scattering efficiency, backscattering efficiency and polarization of sand particles are investigated. The effects of particle size and pulse width on the scattering characteristics are analyzed.

articleTitle: Ionospheric response to strong geomagnetic storm during 07-09 September 2017 in China
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A G4-level strong geomagnetic storm occurred from September 7 to 8, 2017, and it caused seriously impact on the Earth's ionosphere. In this work, the ionospheric response to geomagnetic storm during 07–09 September, 2017 is studied in China region. The variation of foF2, hmF2 and the disturbance index P induced from foF2 are analyzed during the storm time. It is found that travelling ionospheric disturbance played an important role in the developing of the positive ionospheric storm during this strong geomagnetic storm.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of an Electrically Small Broadband Whip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to solve the difficulties faced by the current application of short wave antenna and meet the application of future, the active whip antenna with electrical miniaturization and broadband came into being. Based on the working principle of short wave active whip antenna, several important parameters such as bandwidth, gain and noise characteristics are analyzed and calculated. Finally, a design example of short wave active whip antenna with working frequency range of 2MHz-30MHz is provided. The designed active whip antenna has small size, light weight, wide frequency band and convenient disassembly, and can be widely used in some mobile occasions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wireless Channel Measurement Data in Urban Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Nowadays, how to further strengthen the understanding of the propagation characteristics and channel characteristics of wireless channels in complex urban environments and enhance the technology of wireless communication is essential. In this paper, theoretical analysis, practical measurement and model simulation based on ray tracing algorithm are combined. The environmental sensitivity and frequency sensitivity are verified by actual measurement and model simulation. Finally, the accuracy of the model is verified by experimental data, and some suggestions are put forward for the establishment and optimization of the later wireless channel model.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Polarized Crossed Dipole for Wireless Communication System
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband dual-polarized crossed dipole with simple structure is presented. The radiation element of the proposed antenna is composed of two orthogonal patch dipoles to realise a wideband operation. A metallic reflector is used to achieve the unidirectional radiation. To further improve the antenna bandwidth, an air layer is introduced. A simple feed network. is used to convert unbalanced feed to balanced feed. The results indicate that the prototype has a good performance within the frequency band from 8GHz to 12GHz for return loss ≥ 10dB. The proposed antenna has certain application prospects in wireless communication, radar and other fields.

articleTitle: Synthesis Design of Wideband Absorber Based on 3-D Frequency Selective Structures
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband 3-D absorber based on 3-D frequency selective structures (FSSs) is presented. It is composed of stacked printed circuit boards with non-uniform slot lines on one side and shunt microstrip lines on the other side as well as resistors. In order to provide a synthesis method for it, the equivalent circuit model is introduced, which can also be used to design high-order and wideband absorbers. The closed-form equations are derived, and all the circuit parameters can be solved through the synthesis procedure. Then, an absorber is designed and simulated. The simulated results exhibit a wide absorption bandwidth of 1.9-8.23 GHz, that is 125% in fractional bandwidth, with absorptivity more than 90%. Moreover, the absorber can achieve angular stability even under incident angle of 50°.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Attenuation Characteristics for Earth-Space Paths in Infrared Band
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In this paper, taking Beijing as an example, the attenuation characteristics of atmospheric molecules and aerosols in the infrared band along the vertical path are studied by using MODTRAN software and Monte Carlo method. The atmospheric profiles of pressure, temperature, relative humidity, horizontal and vertical components of wind speed, specific humidity, water vapor pressure and absolute humidity in Beijing are obtained from the Reanalysis Data of ECMWF. The total transmittance of atmospheric molecules along the 0-30km vertical path is calculated by MODTRAN software. It is found that the total transmittance of atmospheric molecules is mainly related to the water vapor content in the air. The water vapor content is related to the humidity in each region and has an obvious relationship with the season. Then, the aerosol transmittance of 0-3.8km vertical path in Beijing is calculated by Monte Carlo method. The transmittance under the interaction of atmospheric molecules and aerosols in Beijing area of 0-3.8km vertical path is obtained. This work may provide technical support for the establishment of Earth to space / space to Earth link communication.

articleTitle: Bowknot-type Resonator Loaded Dual-wideband Folded Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Modern communication needs to meet the requirements of the 5th generation (5G) communication system, while taking into account the 2nd generation (2G), 3rd generation (3G), and 4th generation (4G), wideband base station antennas, operating in 1.71 to 2.69 GHz, 3.3 to 3.6 GHz, and 4.9 to 5 GHz, wideband base station antennas, operating in 1.71-2.69 GHz, 3.3-3.6 GHz, and 4.9-5 GHz, is much needed. Besides, it also needs to meet the 65°±5° 3dB-width in the horizontal plane. In this paper, a bowknot-type resonator loaded dual-wideband folded dipole antenna for commercial communication base station (2-5G) applications is proposed. Compared with traditional folded dipole antenna, an additional bowknot-type resonator is introduced into folded dipole antenna. The bowknot-type resonator generates an additional new resonant mode. The simulation results show: (1) The Band-I with a center frequency of 2GHz has an impedance of -10dB with operating frequency range varying form 1.62GHz to 2.64GHz and The Band-II with a center frequency of 4.95GHz has an impedance of -10dB with operating frequency range varying form 4.63GHz to 5.22GH, (2) 70°± 5° half-power beamwidth for the low frequency bands in the horizontal plane, (3) the maximum and minimum gain are 5.1 dBi (at 2.0 GHz) and 3.8 dBi (at 2.64 GHz) in 1.90-2.64 GHz band, and the gain is 5 dBi at 4.95 GHz (4.63 to 5.22 GHz band). It achieves the needs of 2-5G base station applications.

articleTitle: Variation characteristics of ionospheric electron density and plasma temperature at high latitudes in winter of high solar activity
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Based on the detected data from European Svalbard Incoherent Scatter Radar(ESR), the characteristics of electron density and electron and ion temperature in the ionospheric 200 ~ 450 km are analyzed and compared with the values calculated by the empirical model of incoherent scatter radar. Found that more than 200 km and ionospheric electron and ion temperature with height and the tendency of the world is very consistent, there are two in the morning and afternoon peak and valley value lower in the afternoon, evening and night increase. In general, the maximum electron temperature occurs at 6:00-7:00 UT (about 2500 K) in the morning, and the minimum occurs at 17:00-19:00UT (about 1000 K) in the evening, which is different from the characteristics of ionospheric plasma parameters in middle and low latitudes. Comparing the measured electron temperature with ESR empirical model, the variation trend of electron and ion temperature is basically consistent. However, firstly, there are some differences in the peak time of electron and ion temperature and electron density. Secondly, the diurnal and height variation of the empirical model values are more significant. By analyzing the correlation between electron temperature and electron density, it is found that under the influence of strong solar activity, the generally accepted relationship between electron temperature and electron density is only established in winter. The above results enhance the understanding of the characteristic variation of ionospheric plasma parameters in high latitudes and contribute to a deeper understanding of the characteristics of ionospheric variation.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Cylindrical Cavity Resonator with High Quality Factor Using Metallic Sector Mushroom Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: Compact cylindrical cavity resonators (CCRs) are proposed by loading metallic sector mushroom metamaterials exhibiting high quality factors. One such metamaterial CCR is considered with radius of 20mm and height of 10mm. It is numerically demonstrated to resonate at nearly 2.6GHz with the quality factor of nearly 1830. These properties are equivalent to a CCR loaded with a hypothetical dielectric with ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 4.86 and tanδ = 0.00035. The low loss level is however very difficult to find from the practical material library.

articleTitle: Research on Open Reconfigurable Antenna Array Architecture
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to adapt to the development of the phased array antennas and the demand of the open system architecture of the software radar, this paper divided the RF front end into basic module and defined the key interface and control logic. By establishing a modular and scalable open antenna array architecture and standardizing the module functions and interfaces, it is convenient for multiple parties to participate in the development, realize the multi-system reuse of the module, and support the multi-function RF tasks.

articleTitle: Broadband magnetoelectric dipole antenna for 5G base station applications
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: An antenna with a simple structure for 5G base station applications is proposed in this paper. It consists of two pairs of magneto-electric dipoles fed by a Γ -shaped feedline. The proposed antenna has 54% impedance bandwidth from 2.93 to 5.10 GHz, covering 5G n78 (3.3 to 3.8 GHz) and n79 (4.8-5 GHz) band, voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR)<1.7.

articleTitle: A novel way for testing z-direction permittivity by TM0n0 mode cylinder cavity
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: A novel way to measure the permittivity of substrate in the Z direction has been proposed in this document. Compared with the traditional stripline resonant method, this method is simpler to operate with the help of TM mode cylindrical cavity and ensures accuracy with the help of mode match method. To demonstrate the feasibility of this method, a verity experiment with simulation and measurement has been shown in this document. As a result, the calculation results can well match the simulation results. However, the current line cut cannot be solved perfectly in the actual test, which makes the tangent of the loss angle increase the error a lot.

articleTitle: Multilayer Impedance Gradient Microwave Metamaterial Absorber Based on Honeycomb Cores
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: This paper proposed a multilayer impedance gradient metamaterial absorber constructed by honeycomb structures. Honeycomb cores coated with a combination of barium titanate, graphene and carbonyl iron are made by flow casting method. Gradient impedance was realized through controlling the content of graphene at one single layer of metamaterial absorber. The microwave absorption was obtained by the arch measurement system with different thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex> and size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> of honeycomb. Experimental tests show that the size and resonance frequency increase at the same time while the thickness and frequency change in opposite directions. The mechanism concluded by simulation and experiment is destructive interference and multiple scattering. It can be expected that the proposed multilayer impedance gradient metamaterial absorber has potential application value in radar stealth materials and electromagnetic interferences.

articleTitle: Neural network recognition of ionospheric anomaly events based on GNSS RO data
publicationTitle: 2021 13th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory (ISAPE)
abstract: In order to develop the first generation satellite brain laboratory prototype, we have carried out a technology research in its intelligent cognition system. Specifically, based on GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) RO (radio occultation) data, the neural network cognition method of ionospheric anomaly events is established. For the three kinds of ionospheric anomaly events (sporadic E layer, ionospheric plasma bubble and space activity), by establishing input data samples and setting hidden layer, the recognition rates of neural network are 96.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, 98.3 % and 97.7%, respectively. This result proves the effectiveness of the neural network in ionospheric anomalies recognition. The next improvement aspects include increasing more kinds of physical quantities to the input data samples as well as adding the intensity cognition or classification module of ionospheric anomaly events.

articleTitle: Research on Highly Squinted SAR Imaging of sea surface in large scene
